chapters.title: Chapter 151: Ancient Ruins II
paragraphs: The sun was slowly going down.
The orange evening light was passing through the massive branches of the forest and creating long and complex shadows on the ground.
But Lian was not paying attention to the beauty around him, all his focus was on finding a trace that could lead him to Kain.
And maybe... to the ruin that had been buried under this land for a long time.
At first, there were only a few small signs, and he had to find the location of the ruin based on them.
A broken pillar, a stone that was carved in an unnatural shape, and geometric lines that were carved on a massive rock.
But the further he went, the more these signs increased, broken pillars were sticking out from the soil.
Some of them were ten meters tall, some had completely collapsed and only a small part of them could be seen.
The carved stones became larger and more regular.
He even found the remains of a stone road a few times, buried under thick layers of soil and tree roots.
A road that was clearly once part of a massive structure.
Lian knelt on one of the old stones, touched its surface with his hand, and traces of carving tools could still be seen on it.
Even though it had been hundreds or maybe thousands of years since it was built.
"It must be nearby..." he whispered quietly.
The further he went, the more sure he became, Seraphina had not been wrong, there really was something in this area.
Finding ruins and all the signs related to them was actually one of the popular lessons in high school, he always got the highest score in every theoretical lesson.
Although in the view of most students they were very boring, it is these boring lessons that can have the most value for awakened ones.
The closer he got to his destination, a strange feeling also grew inside him.
The feeling of being watched.
"Hmm?" At one point, he suddenly felt like someone was standing behind him.
He immediately turned around but saw nothing.
Just the forest, the trees, and the shadows, he thought maybe he was hallucinating, because his senses also did not detect anything strange.
But a few minutes later, the same feeling returned, this time he was even sure that something had moved among the branches.
But when he went toward it... he found no trace.
No footprints, no smell, no mana, practically nothing, as if something had disappeared right at the moment it was about to be seen.
The third time, he even heard quiet footsteps, footsteps that moved alongside him for a few seconds.
But again, when he stopped... everything fell into silence.
This made his hand unconsciously go into a ready position several times.
He had seen many monsters, but this feeling... was more like being watched by something familiar, like being watched by other humans?
"No one should have found this ruin yet, or at least it should be like this." His frown deepened.
It was not unlikely that other awakened ones from other bases had also found this ruin, but no base other than theirs should be nearby.
So the possibility of it being other awakened ones was low.
Could he be mistaken? However, he did not lower his guard, he preferred to trust his intuition.
Finally, after some searching, the forest suddenly changed.
The trees became fewer, the ground became rockier, and a massive wall appeared in front of him.
Lian remained completely still for a few moments, the wall’s height was over fifty meters, part of it was buried under tree roots.
Other parts were covered with moss and plants, but what mattered was the massive crack that was in its center.
A crack that was too regular to be natural, like a gate, like the entrance to something much larger.
He moved forward quietly and placed his hand on the stone, strange symbols were carved on it.
Lines that had no resemblance to human languages, but despite the passage of time, they were still intact.
As if their builders never intended to let them be forgotten.
"It must be it." Lian took a deep breath, he had found the ruin.
When he passed through the crack, the first thing he noticed was the silence.
An unnatural silence, no sound could be heard, nothing, even the forest outside seemed to not dare to enter this place.
Sunlight barely entered the ruin, stone corridors were submerged in darkness, and the air inside was strangely cold, although he did not feel the cold.
[ You have found the ancient ruin (Lost Light) ]
[ Reward: +3 to all stats added ]
He looked at the notification, the reward was not that valuable, but considering he is not the first to discover it, it is normal.
"Lost Light?" Just from the name, no information could be extracted.
Lian slowly activated Night Eyes, his pupils changed, and the surrounding darkness became brighter.
A few minutes later, he found the first real clue.
Footprints, a relatively fresh trail on a layer of dust, he immediately knelt down to examine it closely.
The footprints belonged to a human, and more importantly... they were not old, maybe only a few days had passed since they were made, a little further ahead, he found the remains of a dead fire.
A few pieces of burnt wood, some ash, and then... something that made him immediately pick it up.
A small metal device, it was a compass specifically for the Ruined Realm, Lian recognized it well, this was one of the items that Kain always carried with him.
He stared at it for a few seconds and then clenched his fist firmly.
"So you were really here..." Now he was sure, Kain had reached this ruin.
Fortunately, all his efforts had not been in vain, his friend was really here, but was he still here? And if he was here, where in this place?
He continued on his way.
The deeper he went, the stranger the ruin became, the corridors became larger.
The ceilings became higher, and the walls were covered with dim crystals that had probably once been a source of light.
Massive statues could be seen on both sides of the path, but most of them were broken.
Some had no heads, some were cut in half, and some were so worn that it was hard to recognize their original shape.
But what caught Lian’s attention was that many of them did not look human at all.
Some had four arms, some had unusual heads, and some were creatures that he could not even imagine what race they belonged to.
As if this ruin was built by a civilization that had perished long ago, a civilization that had no connection to today’s world.
"These must be mythical creatures, if my guess is correct, this is a temple of mythical creatures." Every culture and civilization naturally had its own mythology.
Of course, these were only his guesses and could be wrong.
At that same time, the book of treasure began to tremble, Lian immediately took it out, the pages turned quickly, and the map appeared.
Several golden points lit up on the map.
Lian’s eyes narrowed.
One point, two points, five points, their number was large, and all of them were located deep in the ruin.
Some were probably treasures, some were ancient artifacts.
The intensity of the book’s reaction was almost on the same level as the Sunheart Bloom, maybe even a little more, all the treasures here were at least A rank in value.
But for now, these did not matter, and he did not have the chance to look at their types, not until he found Kain, he closed the book and continued on the path.
After a long time, he reached a hall that even made him stop for a moment.
A massive hall, larger than anything he had seen in the ruin so far.
Giant pillars held the ceiling, and in the center of the hall... a massive door stood.
Its height was over twenty meters, its surface was covered with unknown symbols, but what caught Lian’s attention was not the door itself, but what was on it.
Blood, a trail of fresh blood on the old stones.
A few drops, then more drops, and then... a dragged trail on the ground.
As if someone wounded had passed through here and entered that door.
Lian’s heart beat a little faster, he moved forward quietly and looked at the blood, the blood was dry but fresh, at most from the past day.
If this blood belonged to Kain... then he was not far from him.
And if someone else was beyond that door... then he might enter the most dangerous part of this mission at any moment.
He stood in front of the door for a few seconds, silence, darkness, and the faint smell of blood.
Then he took a deep breath, placed his hand on the door, and pushed it gently.
The massive door began to open with a heavy sound.

chapters.title: Chapter 152: The Divine Of Light
paragraphs: The massive door slowly opened with a heavy and muffled sound.
A thick layer of dust fell from its edges, and the smell of age, stone, and thousands of years of moisture spread in the air.
Lian stood there for a few moments, behind this door there could be any kind of threat and danger, even though he was confident in his power, he knew it was not absolute.
Unfortunately, if he faced a danger that he could not handle, he could not use the ability to leave the Ruined Realm either.
He was also a member of the Quest, and until it was completed, he could not leave the Ruined Realm either.
He slowly stepped inside, the sound of his shoes hitting the old stones echoed several times in the space ahead.
The hall in front of him was much larger than he had imagined, the ceiling height was easily over a hundred meters.
Giant pillars, each the size of a multi-story building, extended on both sides of the hall.
Among them, hundreds of stone statues were placed, all in two regular rows, and all with the same posture, their heads slightly bowed, and their gazes fixed on the center of the hall.
The space was so vast that even the sound of Lian’s breathing was lost among the pillars, and every step he took, its echo would return from the darkness several seconds later.
He felt like he had entered a temple that no living creature had set foot in for thousands of years, this ruin was clearly very old with just a simple look.
It could be hundreds of years old to maybe thousands of years old, and this showed how old and ancient the civilizations of this world were, but unfortunately, most of them had perished.
His gaze fell to the ground again, the blood trail continued, but it was no longer just a few drops, sometimes a bloody handprint could be seen on the wall.
A few meters ahead, the mark of a knee that had been dragged on the stone.
And in some places, a clear trace of a human body being dragged on the ground remained.
Lian quietly knelt next to one of the traces and touched the dried blood with his finger.
His mind started analyzing quickly.
"If this blood belongs to Kain, he was still alive when he entered this hall, but the severity of the bleeding..."
A frown settled on his face.
"He was badly wounded." An awakened one has a high rate of self-healing, but it is not absolute, and it depends on the wound and the type of wound.
Some wounds cannot even be healed by self-healing, especially wounds caused by powerful magic.
Now the question is, if Kain was wounded, how was he wounded?
This conclusion alone was enough to make his steps faster.
The closer he got to the center of the hall, the more the grandeur of the structure showed itself.
Suddenly he stopped in front of something that even made him forget to breathe for a few moments.
A massive statue, its height maybe reaching twenty meters.
The figure of a woman made of white and shining stone, but what shocked him was not the size or the art of its construction.
But its indescribable beauty, the face of the statue... was perfect.
As if all the concepts of beauty in the world were summarized in its existence, calm eyes, a very faint smile, and hair that flowed down to her shoulders.
Even though it was only a statue, its presence created a strange sense of peace.
Lian unconsciously stared for a few seconds.
"Really... could a creature exist that is this perfect...?"
The base of the statue was covered with unknown writings, this time the symbols were different from all the writings he had seen on the way.
And the system reacted.
[Ancient Civilization Language Detected]
[Translating ... ]
The system was able to identify a few words.
Praise be to Divine of Light
The Eternal Radiance
The First Flame
Lian quietly repeated under his breath.
"Divine of Light... the god of light...?"
But he immediately shook his head.
Here, the word God was not used, but Divine, but in fact, he had understood that it was synonymous with God.
This was not the first time he had heard about such a word, and even the title Divine of Light itself was not new to him.
In the nine Ruined Realms that had appeared and been cleared so far, traces of worship of similar beings had always been seen.
The names sometimes had small differences, but their identity... was always the same.
As if all the destroyed worlds worshipped the same beings.
Not different gods, but the same gods, and one of them was the goddess of light, or in other words, the Divine of Light, known by various titles in the previous nine Ruined Realms.
The goddess of light, the source of light, The First Light, The Almighty of Light, The Bringer of Light, and The Mother of Light, and now Divine of Light.
And this was one of the greatest mysteries of the Ruined Realms.
Who were the gods really? Did they actually exist at one time? Or were they just legends that were repeated in all civilizations?
Lian had no answer, in fact, no one had an answer, and in none of the previous realms had an answer been found either.
He started walking again.
A few minutes later, just as he was passing through one of the stone corridors, he suddenly heard a very faint sound from beneath his feet.
Click.
The stone he had stepped on went down only a few millimeters.
Lian’s eyes immediately narrowed.
"Damn..."
A mechanical, old, and rusty sound was heard from deep within the walls.
The next moment... both walls split open, and hundreds of poison-coated stone arrows were fired with incredible speed.
Lian moved almost instinctively.
Mana exploded in his muscles, and his body moved like a shadow among the arrows, one of the arrows passed only a few centimeters from his face.
Another scratched his clothes, and a third pierced the stone pillar behind him.
With a few quick jumps, he got out of the trap’s range, a few seconds later everything fell into silence again.
He breathed calmly.
"How are they still working after all these years?" He looked at the wall that the arrow had hit.
The wall was completely melted and destroyed.
If he had reacted only a moment later, his body would now be full of holes like a sieve.
His guard went higher than before, he did not expect the traps to still be active in an ancient ruin that was several hundred years old.
A few minutes later, he found the first corpse.
Or better to say... the first skeleton, the bones were completely dry, the decayed and worn clothes around it still remained.
A thick layer of dust had settled on everything, it was clear that hundreds of years had passed since this person’s death.
But the strangest part... was the absence of any wounds.
No fractures, no cuts, no holes, nothing, as if his body had just... been emptied from the inside.
Lian looked at the skeleton for a few seconds.
"His life force... it seems like it was completely sucked out." An unpleasant feeling formed inside him.
This corpse definitely belonged to a native of this world, and this terrible thing had probably happened to him hundreds of years ago when the monsters attacked this place.
At that same moment, the book of treasure started trembling again, this time more intensely, Lian quickly opened it, and the map appeared.
And he saw something he had never imagined, one of the golden points... was moving.
Not slowly, but completely clearly, from one corridor to another.
He stared for a few seconds.
"Moving...? A treasure should not move..."
There were only two possibilities, either a creature was carrying one of the treasures with itself, or... the treasure itself was a living creature.
At that same moment, the same feeling returned.
The feeling of being watched, stronger than before, the hairs on the back of his neck stood up.
He immediately turned around, but the corridor was empty.
Night Eyes was still active.
He extended his senses to the maximum possible limit, but... nothing.
No mana, no sound, no smell, yet he was sure, completely sure, something was here, something had been watching him since the moment he entered.
But for some reason... it had decided not to attack, and only watched.
"Could it be waiting for something?" He thought to himself, but what could this thing be waiting for?
In the absolute silence of the ruin, suddenly a faint sound reached his ears.
Clink...
Clink...
The sound of metal hitting stone, and then... a very quiet cough.
Lian immediately froze, held his breath, and put all his focus on listening.
But a few seconds later... silence again, as if nothing had happened.
He was not sure if he had really heard a sound... or if this ruin was playing with his mind.
Following that direction, a few minutes later he reached a massive crossroads.
Four corridors, each extending in a different direction, but what stopped him... was the blood trail.
The same blood trail that had come this far... had suddenly disappeared.
No drops, no traces, no trail, as if someone had suddenly vanished at this very point.
For a moment, dark thoughts crossed his mind.
"Could it be..."
"No." He immediately shook his head.
"It is too early to jump to conclusions." He could not let his emotions overcome his logic.
His gaze shifted between the four corridors, at that moment, the book of treasure trembled gently and pointed to one of the right corridors.
But the blood trail... was in none of them.
Lian stood in silence for a few seconds, then opened his status panel and fixed his gaze on one of his skills.
Blood Hunt.
A skill that could sense the presence of living creatures and their blood traces, he had not used it much until today.
But now... maybe it was the only thing that could lead him to Kain, but at least with its current level, it was useless.
"It is time to upgrade it..." he whispered quietly under his breath, and his gaze fixed on the upgrade option for the skill.

At that same moment, the same feeling returned.
The feeling of being watched, stronger than before, the hairs on the back of his neck stood up.
He immediately turned around, but the corridor was empty.
Night Eyes was still active.
He extended his senses to the maximum possible limit, but... nothing.
No mana, no sound, no smell, yet he was sure, completely sure, something was here, something had been watching him since the moment he entered.
But for some reason... it had decided not to attack, and only watched.
"Could it be waiting for something?" He thought to himself, but what could this thing be waiting for?
In the absolute silence of the ruin, suddenly a faint sound reached his ears.
Clink...
Clink...
The sound of metal hitting stone, and then... a very quiet cough.
Lian immediately froze, held his breath, and put all his focus on listening.
But a few seconds later... silence again, as if nothing had happened.
He was not sure if he had really heard a sound... or if this ruin was playing with his mind.
Following that direction, a few minutes later he reached a massive crossroads.
Four corridors, each extending in a different direction, but what stopped him... was the blood trail.
The same blood trail that had come this far... had suddenly disappeared.
No drops, no traces, no trail, as if someone had suddenly vanished at this very point.
For a moment, dark thoughts crossed his mind.
"Could it be..."
"No." He immediately shook his head.
"It is too early to jump to conclusions." He could not let his emotions overcome his logic.
His gaze shifted between the four corridors, at that moment, the book of treasure trembled gently and pointed to one of the right corridors.
But the blood trail... was in none of them.
Lian stood in silence for a few seconds, then opened his status panel and fixed his gaze on one of his skills.
Blood Hunt.
A skill that could sense the presence of living creatures and their blood traces, he had not used it much until today.
But now... maybe it was the only thing that could lead him to Kain, but at least with its current level, it was useless.
"It is time to upgrade it..." he whispered quietly under his breath, and his gaze fixed on the upgrade option for the skill.

chapters.title: Chapter 153: The Price of Ambition
paragraphs: The cold and darkness had covered everything...
A drop of blood separated from Kain’s fingertips and fell to the ground.
Tap...
The sound of its impact echoed several times in the small space of the room.
Kain was leaning against the stone wall, breathing, short and heavy breaths, every time his chest rose, a severe pain ran from his side to his shoulder.
He had pressed his hand on the deep wound on his side, but the blood still had not stopped, and his face had completely lost its color.
His clothes were almost entirely red with his own blood.
Several deep cuts could be seen on his arms and legs, and one of the wounds had turned black.
Poison, his body still had not been able to expel it.
He closed his eyes.
"How many days... have passed?" He really did not know.
In this room there was no window, no light, and no way to tell the passage of time.
Only pain, thirst, and the quiet sound of his own heartbeat.
A few days ago... when he had first arrived at this area, the situation was completely different.
That day he was full of hope, full of motivation, all the time only one thought repeated in his mind.
"I must not fall further behind Lian and Seraphina."
During his time in the Ruined Realm, contrary to everyone’s expectations, he had made extraordinary progress.
In just a few days, he had reached Level 13, for a first-year student, this speed was almost unbelievable.
Of course, the reason for this rapid progress was all the risks he had taken and he had been willing to go to dangerous areas.
This same matter had given him a lot of confidence.
When he saw the first broken pillars from a distance, his heart started beating faster.
Ancient ruins, one of the most valuable places any awakened one might find in their entire life.
"Maybe this is the chance... maybe there is something here that can reduce the gap between me and those two."
With this thought, he had entered the ruin.
In the Ruined Realms, ancient ruins always had legendary value.
Some of them were remains of temples, some were shrines where thousands once worshipped.
Some were tombs of very powerful ancient figures of these worlds, some were treasuries that ancient civilizations had built to protect their wealth.
And some... were so old that no one even knew what purpose they served.
Almost all the legendary artifacts that had been discovered over the past decades had been obtained from these ruins in the Ruined Realms.
For this reason, every awakened one dreamed of finding one of them one day.
Kain was no exception to this rule.
He had moved carefully through the dark corridors, passed several old traps, crossed through stone cracks.
Passed several massive doors, and the further he went, the higher the mana density became.
Until he finally reached the most central part of the temple.
And there... for a moment he was completely stunned, in the center of a circular hall, a small spring was located.
Golden-blue water, the surface of the water was calm, but a gentle light was coming from inside it.
The air around the spring was so saturated with mana that every breath created a strange feeling of freshness.
Even his body’s cells seemed to be fed by that energy.
The system suddenly activated, but unlike always, it did not display complete information.
Only a warning appeared.
[Unknown Divine Energy Detected]
Kain hesitated for a few moments, he had no information about the nature of this spring, and the mention of divine energy had made him even more uncertain.
Divine energy is one of the mysteries of the Ruined Realms, humanity has had contact with it a few times, but it is not clear at all what it is, and no information about it is available.
Some say it belongs to the gods, and some say it is the only way to go beyond five evolutions.
But something deep inside him told him that this opportunity might never repeat itself.
He quietly took a step forward and entered the water, and the moment his skin touched the water...
The entire world exploded, pain, pain that he could not even describe with words.
He felt every single cell of his body breaking and being rebuilt.
He screamed, but he did not even hear his own voice.
Then... everything fell into darkness.
When he opened his eyes again... the first thing he saw was the hall’s ceiling.
He struggled to get up, his body was heavy, but at the same time... he felt powerful.
He looked beside the spring, dry, completely dry, not even a drop of water remained.
The entire spring had disappeared, he examined his body.
His mana... had multiplied several times, his heartbeat was different, even his blood flow he could feel.
As if something inside him had changed, but before he could find time to think... he heard a voice.
"Heretic!"
Kain turned around.
Two people.
No... two humans! They wore white and gold clothes, and armors that bore no resemblance to modern equipment.
On the chest of both, a golden sun symbol could be seen, one held a long sword in his hand, and the other held a staff made of white crystal.
Both of their eyes were burning with anger.
"You have defiled the sacred water of light!"
"Your sin can only be cleansed with death!"
"Divine of Light will never forgive you!"
Kain was completely shocked for a few moments.
Humans, really humans! Natives of this realm.
He knew the existence of natives in the Ruined Realms was not impossible, but they were so rare that most people considered them legends.
And now... two of them were standing in front of him.
Kain immediately prepared for battle, he could feel the intense anger from them.
"Wait! I did not know..."
But neither of them listened, the swordsman attacked with unusual speed, sparks spread in the air.
Kain barely deflected the first strike, but at the same time, the mage raised his hands, and several spears of light fell from the sky.
Explosion.
The stones of the hall floor shattered, Kain was dragged several meters on the ground.
He tried to resist, tried to counterattack, but the gap in their power was too great.
Their coordination was perfect, every time the swordsman pushed him back, the mage would block his escape route.
Only a few minutes later... his body was covered in wounds, blood was flowing from several points, and an unknown poison had entered his body.
He was lucky that because of that spring he had become several times stronger, and otherwise, he himself knew he had no chance of surviving against these two.
He had no choice but to run.
He ran through the entire ruin, passed through corridors, passed through halls.
Several times he tried to leave through the main entrance.
But every time... the stone gates were closed, and all the exits were sealed, as if the entire ruin had turned into a massive prison.
"Damn it... why won’t they open?!" Fear had filled his entire being.
Behind him, the sound of those two humans’ footsteps could be heard again.
While gathering his last strength, he suddenly slipped next to one of the walls, blood splashed from his hand onto the stone, and at that same moment... the entire wall began to shake.
The symbols carved on it lit up one after another.
The wall quietly moved aside, a small room appeared, Kain did not even have time to think, and he threw himself inside.
A few seconds later... the wall closed again.
The sound of those two humans’ footsteps stopped behind the wall, Kain panted for a few moments and then quietly looked at the wall.
"My blood...?"
"My blood opened the door?"
Suddenly he remembered the spring.
Maybe... after absorbing that water... he was no longer completely human.
Since then... more than a day had passed, maybe more.
His wounds would not heal, the poison was still flowing inside his body, and he was getting weaker every hour.
He stared at the dark ceiling of the room and really thought about death.
"Maybe... it ends here..." A bitter smile settled on his face.
"I am sorry..." The faces of his best friends... the faces of his family... all appeared in his mind one by one.

He knew today’s result was because of his own greed... if he had not been greedy, he would not be in this situation now, he could have lived longer... he could have enjoyed being with his friends more.
At that same moment... BOOOOOOM!!
The entire room shook violently.
The stone wall in front collapsed with a massive explosion, huge pieces of stone scattered in the air, and dust covered everything.
Kain, with the last remaining strength he had, prepared for battle, even if he was going to die... he did not want to die without fighting.
His heart was beating fiercely.
"They found me... those two people..."
The dust slowly cleared, and a shadow entered the room through the smoke.
His steps were calm, confident... a few seconds of silence followed, and then... a familiar voice echoed in the space.
"Finally found you..."
Kain froze, for a moment he thought he was hallucinating, but when the dust completely cleared... he saw that person’s face.
His eyes opened wide in disbelief.
"...Lian?"

chapters.title: Chapter 154: The Holy Spring
paragraphs: Lian stood in front of the massive crossroads of the ruin, Kain’s blood trail had ended right in front of him.
There was no body, no sign of a battle, and not even a trace of a continued path, as if someone had suddenly vanished from the ground.
He examined all four corridors for a few moments.
The book of treasure was still pointing toward one of the right corridors, but there was no way to be sure of Kain’s exact location.
If he continued like this, he might have to search the entire ruin for hours or even days.
Time that Kain no longer had, Lian calmly opened his skill panel and fixed his gaze on the name of one skill.
Bloodhunt.
He took a deep breath.
"If there is ever a time to upgrade it... it is now." Without the slightest hesitation, he spent the necessary fragments.
Suddenly, mana began to flow intensely within his body.
Red veins passed under his skin, and for a moment his entire body was immersed in a blood-colored light, and a heavy pressure passed through his being.
A few seconds later, the system screen appeared before his eyes.
[ 15 fragments used ]
[ Bloodhunt Successfully Evolved ]
[ New Skill Acquired ]
[ Predator’s Instincts ]
[ Rank: Great ]

[ Description: Detects every living being possessing blood within a 10km radius. Precisely determines direction, distance, and physical condition. Tracks blood trails even after all visible traces disappear. Distinguishes different bloodlines. Mana consumption varies according to detection range. ]
A very faint smile settled on Lian’s lips, as he had expected, the potential of this skill was ultimately Great, but the upgrade was very good.
Its capabilities had improved far more than what he had expected.
"Just what I needed." He immediately activated the skill.
At that same moment... the entire world changed, the walls disappeared, the stones faded, the corridors no longer existed.
All he could see... were countless veins of blood.
Dried blood on the ground, remains of blood from thousands of years ago, blood of beasts that once lived in this ruin.
Everything appeared like red threads before his eyes, but suddenly... one of those threads caught his attention.
Thin, weak, irregular, and more importantly... fading.
"Kain..." Lian’s heart beat faster, it was not hard to guess that this blood thread most likely belonged to his friend.
The blood thread went directly toward the wall in front.
Not beside it, but... inside it.
He stepped forward a few steps, placed his hand on the wall, there was no seam.
No door, no mechanism, but his skill was not wrong, Kain was right behind this wall.
"There must be a hidden room."
Lian stepped back a few steps, mana quickly gathered inside his right fist, blue lightning twisted around his arm.
[ Thunder Calamity ]
The sound of thunder exploded through the entire corridor, his fist struck the wall with all his power.
BOOOOM!
The entire stone wall exploded from the middle, massive pieces of stone scattered in the air, and dust covered the entire room.
A few seconds later... when the dust slowly cleared... Lian’s eyes fixed on the small room.
Kain was sitting there, his back leaning against the wall, his entire clothes covered in blood.
Several deep wounds could be seen on his body, his face had almost turned white.
But when his gaze fell on Lian... he just stared for a few moments.
Then... he smiled, a tired but real smile.
"I thought..." His voice was barely audible.
"My time was up..." A few moments later, he gave a weak laugh.
"I knew... if anyone could find me... it would be you..."
Lian did not say anything, he just quietly moved forward, sat down next to him, took out a few healing potion bottles from his storage space.
He poured them into his wounds, then took out a clean cloth and wiped away the dried blood.
"It is over now, I am here now." He finally said quietly.
The anxiety faded from Kain’s face, he finally felt truly saved, but the fear that had accompanied him all this time slowly disappeared, replaced by calm.
A few minutes passed, and his face color improved a little.
Lian finally broke the silence.
"Now tell me, what exactly were you doing here? What happened to you?"
Kain lowered his gaze, was silent for a few seconds, and then slowly began to explain.

About finding the signs of the ruin, about his decision to go forward, about the golden spring, about three days of unconsciousness, about the attack by two humans, about his escape, and about hiding in this secret room.
When he finished... Lian just sat still for a few moments and then let out a long sigh.
"You are crazy, really crazy, you were killing yourself, what if I had not found you? Were you going to die here?" He knew his friend might do crazy things.
But to this extent? To put himself in such great danger? His death was practically certain, if he had not shown up, he would definitely have died within a few hours.
"...I am sorry." Kain lowered his head.
Lian did not say anything for a few moments and then sighed again.
"I hope this is the last time I have to come after you because of your stupidity..."
Kain gave an embarrassed bitter smile, but he was sure that such a thing would not happen again... not after bathing in that golden water.
"Two humans..." Lian whispered under his breath.
At that same moment, Dreadmaw’s words came alive in his mind.
Seven regions, seven lands, the last realms where native humans of this world still lived.
Just from those words, it was clear that the number of native humans in this Ruined Realm was greater than in all the previous Ruined Realms.
He himself had seen a native human of this world before, but now... Kain had seen two of them.
"They might really be from those seven regions..." It could not be a definite guess, but the possibility was high.
A few moments later, he looked at Kain again.
"What was that spring? How did you absorb it?"
Kain shrugged.
"I don’t know myself, when I entered the water, I was unconscious for three full days, and when I woke up, no water remained."
"Was it worth almost losing your life?" Lian frowned.
Kain was silent, as if he was fighting with himself, should he say it? Or should he not say it? He trusted Lian, after all, he had just saved his life.
But what he had obtained was too big, bigger than anything ever heard of.
"Do you promise not to tell anyone?" He finally said quietly.
"You know me." Lian answered without pausing.
Kain gave a faint smile.
"That’s right..." He took a deep breath.
"After I woke up, my class was upgraded."
"What?" Lian frowned.
"It had upgraded from three stars to four stars."
Time stopped for a few seconds, Lian just stared at his friend.
Class upgrade... it was not impossible.
But in the entire two hundred and fifty years, less than five cases of it had been recorded, and those five cases were very special.
This event... was beyond rare.
But Kain was not finished yet.
"That is not all, all my stats had almost tripled."
Lian was still in shock when his friend continued.
"And I don’t think I am human anymore."
"What do you mean?" This time Lian was completely surprised.
"My race has changed, from Human to Descendant of Light."
He paused for a moment.
"And I also got a title, Born Of Light."
Lian was completely silent, a change in bloodline was not a strange thing, there were treasures that could do such a thing.
But... class upgrade, tripling all stats, race change, all of this... just because of one spring? What kind of spring could have such insane power?
A spring that could turn an average awakened one into a genius?
Although it was not as insane as his class and innate skills, the things Kain had obtained could still shock the world.
If this news got out... the entire world would go crazy looking for such a spring.
"So what was that spring really?" Lian asked quietly.
"I don’t know, I only know that when I entered it... everything changed." Kain shook his head.
But at that same moment... a cold, quiet, and hate-filled voice echoed from the depths of the dark corridor.
"That..."
Both turned around at the same time, quiet footsteps echoed on the ancient stones.
"The tears of the Divine of Light."
Two golden dots of light appeared in the darkness, slowly turning into two humans in white and gold armor, on the chest of both, a bright sun symbol was carved.
Their eyes were full of anger, and one of them raised his sword.
"And you impure heretics... destroyed it."
The other stepped forward.
"The sacred water we protected for thousands of years has been defiled by you." An aura of light flared around both of their bodies.
"So... the only remaining way... is your execution."

Kain lowered his gaze, was silent for a few seconds, and then slowly began to explain.

About finding the signs of the ruin, about his decision to go forward, about the golden spring, about three days of unconsciousness, about the attack by two humans, about his escape, and about hiding in this secret room.
When he finished...
Lian just sat still for a few moments and then let out a long sigh.
"You are crazy, really crazy, you were killing yourself, what if I had not found you?
Were you going to die here?" He knew his friend might do crazy things.
But to this extent?
To put himself in such great danger?
His death was practically certain, if he had not shown up, he would definitely have died within a few hours.
"...I am sorry." Kain lowered his head.
Lian did not say anything for a few moments and then sighed again.
"I hope this is the last time I have to come after you because of your stupidity..."
Kain gave an embarrassed bitter smile, but he was sure that such a thing would not happen again... not after bathing in that golden water.
"Two humans..." Lian whispered under his breath.
At that same moment, Dreadmaw’s words came alive in his mind.
Seven regions, seven lands, the last realms where native humans of this world still lived.
Just from those words, it was clear that the number of native humans in this Ruined Realm was greater than in all the previous Ruined Realms.
He himself had seen a native human of this world before, but now...
Kain had seen two of them.
"They might really be from those seven regions..." It could not be a definite guess, but the possibility was high.
A few moments later, he looked at Kain again.
"What was that spring?
How did you absorb it?"
Kain shrugged.
"I don’t know myself, when I entered the water, I was unconscious for three full days, and when I woke up, no water remained."
"Was it worth almost losing your life?" Lian frowned.
Kain was silent, as if he was fighting with himself, should he say it?
Or should he not say it?
He trusted Lian, after all, he had just saved his life.
But what he had obtained was too big, bigger than anything ever heard of.
"Do you promise not to tell anyone?" He finally said quietly.
"You know me." Lian answered without pausing.
Kain gave a faint smile.
"That’s right..." He took a deep breath.
"After I woke up, my class was upgraded."
"What?" Lian frowned.
"It had upgraded from three stars to four stars."
Time stopped for a few seconds, Lian just stared at his friend.
Class upgrade... it was not impossible.
But in the entire two hundred and fifty years, less than five cases of it had been recorded, and those five cases were very special.
This event... was beyond rare.
But Kain was not finished yet.
"That is not all, all my stats had almost tripled."
Lian was still in shock when his friend continued.
"And I don’t think I am human anymore."
"What do you mean?" This time Lian was completely surprised.
"My race has changed, from Human to Descendant of Light."
He paused for a moment.
"And I also got a title, Born Of Light."
Lian was completely silent, a change in bloodline was not a strange thing, there were treasures that could do such a thing.
But... class upgrade, tripling all stats, race change, all of this... just because of one spring?
What kind of spring could have such insane power?
A spring that could turn an average awakened one into a genius?
Although it was not as insane as his class and innate skills, the things Kain had obtained could still shock the world.
If this news got out... the entire world would go crazy looking for such a spring.
"So what was that spring really?" Lian asked quietly.
"I don’t know, I only know that when I entered it... everything changed." Kain shook his head.
But at that same moment... a cold, quiet, and hate-filled voice echoed from the depths of the dark corridor.
"That..."
Both turned around at the same time, quiet footsteps echoed on the ancient stones.
"The tears of the Divine of Light."
Two golden dots of light appeared in the darkness, slowly turning into two humans in white and gold armor, on the chest of both, a bright sun symbol was carved.
Their eyes were full of anger, and one of them raised his sword.
"And you impure heretics... destroyed it."
The other stepped forward.
"The sacred water we protected for thousands of years has been defiled by you." An aura of light flared around both of their bodies.
"So... the only remaining way... is your execution."

chapters.title: Chapter 155: A One-Sided End
paragraphs: "You two must be the same bastards who tried to kill my friend." Lian gave them a cold look.
With just one look, it was clear that they were really human, but what caught his attention was that he had not noticed their presence.
Could they have some kind of skill that hides their presence? Or does it have to do with their fancy shiny armor?
Although the two did not seem to have any interest in talking to him.
Both did not hesitate even for a moment, as soon as the last words left their mouths, mana exploded throughout the hall.
A golden aura formed around both of their bodies and lit up the dark space of the ruin.
The swordsman stepped forward, his movements were calm, but with every step he took, the mana pressure increased.
At the same time, the light mage stood a few meters back and raised both his hands, several golden magic circles appeared one after another behind him.
Each circle was covered with unknown symbols that Lian had never seen before.
They clearly used magic arts from a different civilization than theirs, and with just one look, they seemed more complex but more powerful.
The mage whispered with a cold voice.
"Holy Judgment."
The next moment, the hall’s ceiling was covered with golden light, dozens of massive spears of light formed and fell toward Lian with terrifying speed.
Almost simultaneously, another circle appeared beneath his feet.
"Radiant Chains."
Chains of light burst out from the ground and rushed toward Lian’s legs and arms with incredible speed.
At that same moment, the swordsman’s sword also shone, and the entire blade was covered with sun-like light.
"Solar Edge."
The mana power around the sword multiplied several times, and the air around the blade was splitting even before impact.
"Be careful, they are really strong." Kain warned strongly.
Lian, without the slightest change in his expression, watched both of them, their raw power was not very high.
If compared based on the awakened system... they were probably around level twenty to twenty-four.
But what made them dangerous was not power.
It was skill and mana control, coordination, and combat experience, these two had clearly fought together for years.
And from these initial displays, it was clear their magic skills focused more on control and destructive power, but this also made them slower and more complex.

’Two advantages and two disadvantages, in contrast, our world’s magic system is faster and more precise, but mana control depends on the person, and destructive power is the same.’ He thought to himself.
The swordsman, ignoring the spears of light, charged directly at Lian.
His sword came down toward his neck with lightning speed, but right before impact... Lian’s skin changed.
[Diamond Skin]
An invisible but extremely hard layer covered his entire body.
The sword hit his neck and a blinding spark spread through the hall.
The sound of metal on metal echoed, but... no blood flowed, and no wound was created.
The swordsman froze, his eyes widened in disbelief.
"Impossible..." How? How could his strike not deal any damage to this heretic?
He did not even have time to pull his sword back, blue lightning covered Lian’s entire fist.
[Thunder Calamity]
Lian just threw a simple punch, but that one punch... was like a meteor striking.
BOOOM!
The strike hit the man’s stomach directly, and all the air in his lungs was expelled in an instant, his body lifted off the ground and was thrown back like a heavy bullet.
One stone pillar shattered.
Then the second pillar.
And the third.
Finally, with another explosion, he hit the end wall of the hall.
His entire white and gold armor cracked, for a few seconds he could not even breathe, and started coughing up blood.
His face turned pale, as if a mountain had collapsed on him.
The light mage, seeing this scene, lost his color, how could this heretic have such power? Where did he come from?
But he still did not stop his attack, dozens of light spears fell toward Lian at the same time, and each of them could pierce the body of a level twenty monster.
But Lian just ignored them, and the next moment...
All the light spears passed through the space around his body without hitting him, his dodging speed was so high that the two could not even see it with their eyes.
And in their view, it was as if he had not moved at all, and the attacks had passed through him.
"How is this possible...?! What kind of demonic skill is this?!" The mage stepped back in terror.
They had picked the wrong opponent, an enemy they had no chance against, but they still could not retreat.
This was about their goddess’s honor and reputation.
But Lian was no longer interested in continuing this show, mana exploded in his body once again.
His muscles contracted, the wind around him became chaotic.
In the eyes of both humans... he disappeared, the swordsman who was just trying to get up suddenly felt an intense cold behind his neck.
Before he could even turn around... he heard Lian’s calm voice behind him.
"It is over."
Glacial Reaper Claw.
A massive claw of ice passed through the air, leaving four deep marks on the man’s armor.
The metal split like paper, the flesh and bones did not escape this attack either, and the man fell to the ground again with a painful scream.
This time he could not get up again, blood was flowing from under his armor.
The light mage accepted reality for the first time.
This battle... was not a battle at all, it was a one-sided massacre, they had no chance! They had no chance to kill this heretic and restore the goddess’s honor.
He did not even look at his comrade, with a trembling hand, he pulled out a golden scroll from his belt.
Lian noticed, but the distance was still a little far.
The mage tore the scroll, a bright light filled the entire hall, the eyes could not see anything for a moment, when the light faded...
The mage was no longer there.
Silence.
"...He ran away?" Kain, who had been watching this entire scene with his mouth open, whispered quietly.
He could not believe that the two who had brought him to the brink of death were so powerless and defenseless against his friend, like insects facing a monster.
’And I thought the gap between us had gotten smaller.’ He sighed and pushed the foolish thoughts out of his mind.
He still had a long way to go.
Lian, without taking his gaze off the escape route, answered calmly.
"Yeah, he sold out his friend."
The wounded swordsman tried with all his might to get himself on his feet, his hand went toward his sword, but before he could touch it...
Lian’s foot landed on his chest, the pressure was so high that all the bones in his ribcage creaked.
No matter how much the man tried, he could not move even a few centimeters, the power gap was too great.
Lian bent down and picked up the glowing sword, examined it for a few moments, the sword had excellent quality.
But stranger than that... all the mana inside the sword was fading away, as if it only worked in its original owner’s hands.
He threw the sword a few meters away.
"That’s it...? It is over?" Kain was still looking in disbelief.
"It was over from the start." Lian shrugged.
The swordsman stared at him with hatred, his lips bloody, but he still shouted with all his being.
"Heretic... the Divine of Light... will destroy you..."
Lian calmly bent down and grabbed the collar of the man’s white and gold armor, there was no trace of anger on his face, only calmness, his gaze fell on the end of the corridor for a moment.
There was no trace of the mage anymore, he looked at his captive again and a very small smile settled on his lips.
"It seems... your friend left you alone." A few seconds of silence followed, and then his voice became quieter.
"Now, how about answering a few questions?"

chapters.title: Chapter 156: Leaving The Ancient Ruin
paragraphs: The sound of the white-robed man’s heavy breaths echoed in the silent space of the hall.
Despite the deep wounds covering his entire body, he still stared at Lian and Kain with that same hate-filled gaze.
No fear could be seen in his eyes, only hatred, unlike the mage who was clearly a coward, this one seemed to have no fear of death.
His fanaticism and faith in his goddess had reached a level that made the concept of death meaningless to him.
"What is your name?"
"Heretic." The man said with hatred.
"Where did you come from?" Lian did not frown, in interrogation and asking questions, one of the most important factors is patience, and he was a relatively patient person.
"Unclean."
"Where did you come from? Where is your land?"
"Death to you."
A few seconds of silence followed.
"I don’t think he will talk..." Kain whispered quietly under his breath, anyone could tell that this one was not the type to talk, and they were just wasting time.
"Then you chose the hard way." Lian let out a long sigh, his patience had run out.
The next moment...
His fist landed directly on the man’s face, the sound of breaking nasal bones echoed throughout the hall.
Before the man even had a chance to groan, the second fist hit his jaw.
Then the third.
Fourth.
The fifth strike dragged him several meters on the ground, Lian had not even used Thunder Calamity.
All these strikes were delivered with pure physical strength alone, each strike was like being hit by a steel hammer.
The man’s face quickly swelled, his lips were torn, one of his teeth fell to the ground, and his right eye was almost closed.
But Lian still did not stop, another strike hit his stomach, the air inside the man’s lungs was expelled all at once, and his body curled up like a shrimp on the ground.
Kain even unconsciously turned his gaze away from the scene, he had seen his friend fight just a moment ago, and had seen how ruthless he could be.
But this was the first time he saw his friend deliberately beat someone this badly to get information.
This was on a different level of cruelty.
A few minutes later...
It was hard to even recognize the man’s face anymore, his face was so swollen that he really looked like a pig that had fallen into the hands of a group of hunters.
Lian bent down, grabbed the collar of his white and gold armor, his voice remained calm.
"Now... let’s try again."
This time...
The man did not stay silent, no one would dare to stay silent after all that beating.
"...We..." He coughed several times, blood came out from the corner of his lips.
"We came from the third region..."
"Third region?" Lian raised an eyebrow, the man nodded with difficulty.
"One... of the seven human regions..."
Kain looked at Lian in surprise, but Lian’s own face was calm.
Seven regions, so Dreadmaw’s words were true, the native humans of this world were still alive, at least a significant number of them.
Not just alive, but they had civilization, they had government, and they had maintained their own territories.
"Are all those seven regions still standing?" Lian asked quietly.
"Yeah... each region... is under the protection of a Divine..."
Lian was silent for a moment, the same old mystery appeared before his eyes again, in the previous nine Ruined Realms, these same names existed.
The Divines, or the gods.
But no one knew what those beings really were.
The man continued.
"We... are followers of the Divine of Light..."
A kind of pride suddenly appeared in his wounded eyes, as if for him, his goddess was above any pain and suffering, above his life and death.
"Light... is the beginning of everything, she is our way, she protects us."
Lian calmly looked around the hall, the massive statues, the magnificent pillars, the symbols of light, and everything suddenly found new meaning.
"So this was the temple of the Divine of Light?"
The man nodded with pride.
"The first and most sacred, all the later temples were built based on this one."
"If it was this sacred, then why did you abandon it?" Lian asked again.
This time the man almost shouted.
"We did not abandon it!" His voice was full of anger, "The tears of the Divine were not yet complete... for hundreds of years... it had to gather energy..."
"We were just waiting." His gaze suddenly fixed on Kain, deep hatred surged in his eyes, if a look could kill, Kain would have died thousands of times by now.
"When we arrived... everything was gone, the spring was destroyed, it is all this heretic’s fault."
No sign of guilt or remorse could be seen on Kain’s face, why should he feel such feelings? He was just lucky enough to get this opportunity first.
If it was really that important to them, they could have just come here sooner.
"What should we do with him now?" After a few minutes of silence, Kain asked quietly.
Lian thought for a few moments.
"I don’t know for now, but his information is very valuable, it is better to hand him over to the government or the federation, killing him now has no benefit."
Kain came a little closer and lowered his voice.
"But... what if my secret gets out?"
Lian gave a faint smile.

"Relax, he doesn’t even understand what a class is, it is unlikely he knows anything about class upgrades or your race, and if the government asks you... just say that spring made your stats multiply several times."
"That’s it, you don’t need to say anything about the rest.
"Okay..." Kain breathed a sigh of relief, even though he trusted Lian enough to tell him the truth, he had no plan to tell the federation the truth.
But suddenly he frowned... could he hide this truth forever? The gap between a three-star and four-star class was large.
Sooner or later, everyone would find out.
He sighed and decided to think about it later.
Before leaving the ruin, Lian took out the book of treasure again.
The golden points were still shining on the map, this time he was in no hurry, the first point was behind one of the massive statues.
After moving a few stones, a metal box appeared.
Inside it were several crystals.
The second point was under the stone floor of one of the rooms, a few sealed scrolls, and the third point was inside a hidden wall, a black metal cube.
Then a few other objects, he put them all into his storage space without examining them.
Now was not the time for curiosity, first they had to get out of here and return to the base as soon as possible.
When they reached the exit gate... the door was still closed.
"Why is it closed?" Lian looked at the prisoner, when he had come, this door was completely open, so it being closed could only mean one thing.
"We closed it, we did not want two barbarian heretics to escape." The man answered with the same hatred.
"I understand heretic, but barbarian?" Lian paused on one word.
The man spat a bloody tooth from his mouth with difficulty.
"You are those outsiders... who fell from the sky a few weeks ago, the ones who killed our people, only barbarians do that."
Lian was silent for a moment, twenty-five thousand victims, on the first day this realm opened, they were summoned here.
If even a small percentage of them encountered the native people... conflict would have definitely occurred.
And probably some of the natives had been killed, and from these people’s perspective... the awakened ones from Earth were invaders who had suddenly descended from the sky and massacred their people.
Lian looked at the man again.
"Open the gate."
"Never." The man laughed.
Lian stepped forward, his eyes completely calm.
"Either you open it yourself, or we start the interrogation all over again."
The color drained from the man’s face, he resisted for a few seconds, but in the end he broke, with a trembling hand, he touched several ancient symbols on the wall.
The entire ruin began to shake, the sound of massive stones colliding echoed through the corridors, and the gate slowly opened.
Sunlight shone into the temple again after several days.
Lian looked at the sky for a moment and took a deep breath.
"We have to get back as soon as possible, the base is still under siege, and they might need our help now more than ever."
Kain also nodded, he had heard the situation from Lian and knew what was happening.
They just hoped the base had not fallen during this time...

"We were just waiting." His gaze suddenly fixed on Kain, deep hatred surged in his eyes, if a look could kill, Kain would have died thousands of times by now.
"When we arrived... everything was gone, the spring was destroyed, it is all this heretic’s fault."
No sign of guilt or remorse could be seen on Kain’s face, why should he feel such feelings?
He was just lucky enough to get this opportunity first.
If it was really that important to them, they could have just come here sooner.
"What should we do with him now?" After a few minutes of silence, Kain asked quietly.
Lian thought for a few moments.
"I don’t know for now, but his information is very valuable, it is better to hand him over to the government or the federation, killing him now has no benefit."
Kain came a little closer and lowered his voice.
"But... what if my secret gets out?"
Lian gave a faint smile.

"Relax, he doesn’t even understand what a class is, it is unlikely he knows anything about class upgrades or your race, and if the government asks you... just say that spring made your stats multiply several times."
"That’s it, you don’t need to say anything about the rest.
"Okay..." Kain breathed a sigh of relief, even though he trusted Lian enough to tell him the truth, he had no plan to tell the federation the truth.
But suddenly he frowned... could he hide this truth forever?
The gap between a three-star and four-star class was large.
Sooner or later, everyone would find out.
He sighed and decided to think about it later.
Before leaving the ruin, Lian took out the book of treasure again.
The golden points were still shining on the map, this time he was in no hurry, the first point was behind one of the massive statues.
After moving a few stones, a metal box appeared.
Inside it were several crystals.
The second point was under the stone floor of one of the rooms, a few sealed scrolls, and the third point was inside a hidden wall, a black metal cube.
Then a few other objects, he put them all into his storage space without examining them.
Now was not the time for curiosity, first they had to get out of here and return to the base as soon as possible.
When they reached the exit gate... the door was still closed.
"Why is it closed?" Lian looked at the prisoner, when he had come, this door was completely open, so it being closed could only mean one thing.
"We closed it, we did not want two barbarian heretics to escape." The man answered with the same hatred.
"I understand heretic, but barbarian?" Lian paused on one word.
The man spat a bloody tooth from his mouth with difficulty.
"You are those outsiders... who fell from the sky a few weeks ago, the ones who killed our people, only barbarians do that."
Lian was silent for a moment, twenty-five thousand victims, on the first day this realm opened, they were summoned here.
If even a small percentage of them encountered the native people... conflict would have definitely occurred.
And probably some of the natives had been killed, and from these people’s perspective... the awakened ones from Earth were invaders who had suddenly descended from the sky and massacred their people.
Lian looked at the man again.
"Open the gate."
"Never." The man laughed.
Lian stepped forward, his eyes completely calm.
"Either you open it yourself, or we start the interrogation all over again."
The color drained from the man’s face, he resisted for a few seconds, but in the end he broke, with a trembling hand, he touched several ancient symbols on the wall.
The entire ruin began to shake, the sound of massive stones colliding echoed through the corridors, and the gate slowly opened.
Sunlight shone into the temple again after several days.
Lian looked at the sky for a moment and took a deep breath.
"We have to get back as soon as possible, the base is still under siege, and they might need our help now more than ever."
Kain also nodded, he had heard the situation from Lian and knew what was happening.
They just hoped the base had not fallen during this time...

chapters.title: Chapter 157: Return to the Siege
paragraphs: Lian and Kain, after hours of non-stop movement, finally reached one of the high rocky ridges a few kilometers from the base.
It was almost noon when they arrived, exactly one day had passed since Lian had left the base, and he had done his best to return as quickly as possible.
They had not even gotten close to the outer walls yet when the sound of explosions could be clearly heard.
Every few seconds, the ground beneath their feet would tremble, sometimes blue lightning would illuminate the entire horizon, and sometimes fiery explosions would color the sky.
Kain stared at the distance for a few moments, massive columns of smoke had risen kilometers into the sky.
"So it is not over yet..." he whispered quietly, this was both good news and bad news.
Good news because it meant the base had not fallen yet, and bad news because it meant they had not been able to win either.

Lian did not answer, in the battle against the Ironfang Ravagers they had won within a few hours, but this time it was different, with a day passing, it was clear there was no hope of victory with the base’s current power.
He calmly climbed up the rock and stood on the highest point, his eyes scanned the entire battlefield.
What he saw was even larger than his worst predictions.
The siege was still ongoing.
Not hundreds but thousands of monsters had surrounded the Base, Thunder Spine Serpents were emerging from the forests like an endless wave.
Their long bodies and metallic scales shone under the sunset light, and every few seconds, dozens of lightning bolts would shoot from their bodies toward the base walls.
On the other side of the field, Ironhorn Marsh Drakes were advancing like moving fortresses.
Their armored bodies hit the massive walls again and again, each collision creating a tremor across the entire area.
But the Base had still not fallen, the mana towers were firing non-stop, and the mana cannons were tearing dozens of monsters apart with each shot.
The mages stationed on the walls were raining down ice, fire, and thunder on the battlefield.
The defensive barriers were still active, and every time a wave of monsters got close to the wall, blue shields would appear and neutralize part of the attacks.
However... not everything was perfect.
In several places on the wall, large cracks had appeared.
Some parts of the stones had collapsed, several watchtowers no longer existed.
The ground outside the base... could no longer be seen, the entire plain was buried under a pile of corpses.
Bodies of thunder serpents, horned crocodiles, and the bodies of awakened ones who would never return.
Blood had turned the ground a dark red, the smell of death reached even where they were standing.
This was practically a war, and a war on a large scale with thousands of participants and heavy casualties on both sides.
"Many have died..." Kain said with a dry throat.
Lian nodded quietly, he had also noticed, some of the commanders he had seen yesterday were no longer on the wall.
The forces were constantly being replaced, whenever a group retreated, another group would take its place.
They were still resisting, but this resistance was costing a heavy price, reaching a conclusion in this situation was very difficult.
He had thought that if the egg’s presence disappeared from the base, the monsters would give up, but it seemed he had been wrong.
Unless the monsters still believed the egg was inside the base, or they had not come just for the egg and had another reason.
But it could not be said with certainty.
Something else caught Lian’s attention, the strongest monsters... had still not entered the battle.
In the distance, on a high hill, the Abyssal River Drake was standing, its massive body looked like a black mountain in the twilight.
Its red eyes were watching the entire battlefield, several other Fallen ones were also present around it.
None of them were attacking, just... watching.
Sometimes one of them would let out a short roar, at that moment, a new wave of monsters would charge toward the wall.
Sometimes one of the Fallen ones would change the direction of several hundred monsters with just a movement of its head, everything was too organized.
"They are tiring them out." Lian said quietly, this was a conclusion he had easily reached.
Kain did not take his gaze off the field.
"What do you mean?"
"The defensive mana arrays have limits, the mages have mana, the awakened ones have stamina, but none of them are infinite." He paused for a few moments.
"When everyone is exhausted, that is when they will enter themselves."
"Then... nothing of the base will remain." Kain quietly let out his breath and realized the severity of the situation.
Lian looked at his friend, Kain’s face color had still not returned to normal, the poison had still not completely left his body.
His wounds had closed, but his body was still weak, although the sacred spring had given him strange power, that unknown poison was still consuming part of his ability.
Besides, he was still level 13, even with tripled stats, he could barely fight level 15 or 16 monsters.
If he entered the battlefield right now... he might not last more than a few minutes.
Then his gaze fell on the prisoner, the white-robed man was still unconscious, after all that noise, Lian had knocked him out with one blow to make things easier.
For now, carrying him was easier than enduring his words.
"What should we do now?" Kain asked quietly, nothing came to his mind, and in such situations, he could only hope for his friend.
Lian did not answer, all his attention was on the field, in any case, this matter was his fault, and he had to take responsibility for it.
So he could not just ignore the base and stand aside, besides, killing all these monsters had great benefits.
But what exactly should he do?
If he attacked the monster army from behind... they would undoubtedly be caught off guard.
He could kill dozens or even hundreds of monsters in a short time.
The pressure on the defenders would decrease, but... his gaze fixed on the Abyssal River Drake.
If that creature noticed his presence even once... everything would be over, neither Abyss Veil nor Fallen Wolf Speed could save him.
The power gap was too large, escape would be almost impossible.
He examined different scenarios one after another.
Direct attack? Suicide.
Waiting? Every minute, more humans were being killed.
Returning secretly? He might succeed, but he would have to leave the prisoner and Kain behind, and it was not worth it.
No path was perfect, he really felt like he was at a dead end.
At that same moment, a small movement caught his attention, a few Thunder Spine Serpents broke away from the front line.
They moved toward the river, and a few minutes later... another group took their exact place.
Lian frowned.
A few minutes later, the same thing happened with the Ironhorn Marsh Drakes.
A group retreated, and a fresh group took their place.
Kain also noticed.
"They are rotating their forces..."
"Yeah..." Lian looked more carefully, this was not just a force rotation, everything had a clear order, their movement path was constant, their timing was almost the same.
No chaos could be seen in the monster army, as if a precise commander was managing everything.
He observed the same paths for a few more minutes.
Every time, the same groups, the same time, the same path, and his eyes slowly narrowed.
In his mind, the puzzle pieces were coming together one after another, if these rotations were planned...
Then maybe... the very plan itself was their weak point.
A gentle wind passed over the bloody plain.
The sound of explosions could still be heard from a distance, Lian took one last look at the Abyssal River Drake.
Then his gaze fixed again on the movement path of the rotating groups, and his lips moved slightly.
"Maybe... there is a way."
"What way?" Kain looked at him.
Lian still did not answer, his gaze remained fixed on the battlefield, and in his mind, a plan was slowly taking shape...
He was not sure if it would work or not, but it was worth a try.
