Valerian was the first to break the silence.
"Where did you find him?"
"In an ancient ruin, and not me, Lian captured him." Kain answered quietly.
Both commanders were silent for a moment.
"That same boy again..." Elizabeth whispered under her breath.
"Lian?
Who is he?" Valerian frowned.
"The hero of this base." Then without exaggeration, she summarized the events of the past few hours.
From destroying a large part of the monster army, and finally... to holding the Abyssal River Drake until the reinforcements arrived.
The more she explained... the more serious Valerian’s face became, and at the end, he just said quietly.
"All of this... was done by an eighteen-year-old boy?
If that’s true... his talent is truly monstrous." He thought for a few moments and then added.
"I want to meet him personally later."
"He’s in the medical center for now, he hasn’t woken up yet." Elizabeth answered.
"Then we should deal with this native matter first." Their gazes fell on the native again.
Two days passed.
The war was over, but the medical center was still busy, hundreds of wounded were being treated.
In one of the quiet rooms...
Lian was lying on a special treatment bed.
His body was almost completely bandaged, healing crystals were slowly infusing mana into his body.
Next to the bed...
Seraphina was sitting on a chair, over the past two days, she had come almost every few hours to check on his condition.
Most of the time, she had stayed there.
At that moment, the door opened and Kain entered.
"Are you feeling better?" Seraphina looked at him and asked, she knew Kain’s condition was not good either, and something had happened to him out there.
"Yeah, my wounds were nothing compared to him." Kain gave a faint smile.
"So you found that ruin, huh?" The girl asked curiously.
Kain nodded and then told the story of the ruin, about finding it, about the two native humans, about being wounded, and how Lian had arrived in time and saved him.
But about the sacred spring... the class upgrade... the race change... and the title Born of Light... he did not say even a single word.
That secret... for now, would remain only between him and Lian, and when he finished...
"A native human..." Seraphina said quietly, she still found it hard to believe.
"So this realm might really be different from all the previous ones." And a few moments later, she asked.
"Besides that... did you find anything special inside the ruin?"
Kain shrugged.
"I’m not sure, Lian took a few treasures, but we haven’t looked at them yet."
"So the ruin wasn’t that special..." Seraphina sighed.
Kain laughed.
"Why are you disappointed?
The three races that had closed off the area are gone."
"After things calm down completely, we can explore up to a thousand kilometer radius and even further."
"That’s when the real and cooler ruins will start."
Seraphina also smiled quietly, maybe... the main adventure was just on the verge of beginning.
The morning of the third day...
Sunlight was coming through the window into the room, a quiet calm had covered everything.
Lian’s fingers moved slightly, then his hand trembled, his eyelids slowly opened.
The image in front of him was blurry at first, but gradually became clear.
The first thing he saw... was Seraphina, her head resting on the edge of the bed, she had fallen asleep there from exhaustion.
He was finally awake...

chapters.title: Chapter 164: The Calm After the Storm III
paragraphs: The air in the treatment room was calm.
The white walls with blue veins were shining, and the healing crystals installed in the four corners of the room were slowly spreading healing energy in the space.
The steady sound of the machines filled the room’s silence, and through the large window next to the bed, the gentle light of the sun was shining inside.
Lian slowly looked around to test his vision, and there was no sign of that heavy darkness or dizziness.
The only thing he felt was pain, pain that was flowing through almost all the bones in his body.
With some difficulty, he moved his head and noticed that almost his entire body was covered with bandages.
He had been awake for a few dozen minutes now, after he woke up, Seraphina had rushed to bring the doctors and healers of the base here to examine him.
At that same moment, the door opened.
An elderly physician wearing the white robe of the healers entered. When he saw that Lian was awake, he gave a faint smile and calmly approached the bed.
"Finally awake."
"...How many days was I unconscious?" Lian asked with a hoarse voice, just by considering how he felt, he was sure he had slept for more than a day.
"You were unconscious for two full days." The physician opened the file and looked at the information inside.
"You had burned almost all of your mana, more than ten bones were fractured, and much of your internal organs were damaged." He paused for a moment and then continued with a serious look.
"If you hadn’t activated those defensive skills simultaneously... not even one healthy cell would have remained in your body." They had checked his entire condition step by step.
A large part of the attacks that had hit this boy had been absorbed by his defensive skills and had kept his body safe.
Lian involuntarily gave a bitter smile, he was really lucky that he had obtained Molten Armor just a few days ago, otherwise he would have had no chance of standing against that monster.
He would have been killed in that first attack.
The physician shook his head.
"In all my life... I have only seen two people survive after such damage, and now... you are the third." A few moments of silence passed between them.
At that same time, Seraphina finally returned to the room, and her eyes sparkled for a moment and she breathed a sigh of relief.
She calmly came next to the bed.
"My work here is done, his condition is completely stable." The physician looked at both of them and left the room.
"Finally, I was afraid it would take longer, do you know how worried you made me! In just one month, you’ve worried me to the point of death three times!" Seraphina said angrily.
First, when Lian was summoned to the Ruined Realm as one of the victims, second, when he went to the border city, and now this is the third time.
She couldn’t understand this boy, is it really that hard to stay away from trouble and danger?
"I’m sorry." Lian said with a weak smile.
Seraphina made a fake frown.
"Half your body was almost destroyed, if you had arrived a few minutes later, you probably wouldn’t be here now." She then slowly let out her breath.
"For two days, I came here almost every few hours." A tired smile settled on her lips.
"Thank you so much, honestly, I never had a mother to nag at me, but I guess you’ve filled that position well." Lian added sarcastically.
"Sigh! Was that an insult or a compliment?" Seraphina looked at him with a real frown.
"Whichever you prefer."
"Forget it... I think I should go back to my work now, everyone is still busy collecting loot and rebuilding the base." She looked at Lian for a few moments.
"You just rest."
Lian calmly nodded.
"Okay."
Before leaving, Seraphina made sure once more that his condition was stable, and then the door closed.
Lian was completely alone and finally had the chance to look at his status.
A few seconds later... he opened the system window.
At that same moment... the entire space in front of him was filled with blue notifications, so many that even scrolling the page was not enough.
Dozens of notifications related to experience, killing monsters, new skills, quest rewards, he calmly started closing the notifications and finally reached the most important one.
[ Emergency Quest Completed ]
[ Base #3 Successfully Defended ]
[ Rewards: +1 Level, +100 Stat Points, +10 Fragments ]
"Reward reduction due to external help, huh..." Lian involuntarily smiled, the system’s behavior was clear, and he had guessed such a thing.
He continued closing the notifications, at the bottom of the page, the amount of his free stat points was displayed.
Stats points: 110
A frown settled on his face.
"One hundred and ten?" He had not been present in the final battle against the Abyssal River Drake, so there was no way he could have gotten points for killing that monster.
So... where did those ten extra points come from? He thought for a few moments and then suddenly his gaze fell on his current level.
[ Level 16 ]
At that same moment, he understood.
"Right..." The Quest had caused him to go up one Level, so those ten points... must be the Level Up reward.
But his frown deepened.
"Only ten?" He remembered the general information about five-star classes.
Between Level 10 and 20... each Level gives fifty Stat Points, but the Monster class gives only ten?
He was silent for a few seconds and then shrugged.
"So this class finally has a weakness too." But he very soon lost interest, for him, obtaining Stat Points was much easier than for normal people.
By hunting monsters, they constantly generated points.
In contrast, only four Levels remained until the first Evolution, and that thought alone was enough to revive excitement in his being.
He immediately opened the next page and decided to take a look at his new skills.
[ New Skills Acquired ]
His eyes sparkled a little, he had obtained four new skills.
He opened the first skill, which he had obtained from the Ironhorn Marsh Drake.
[ Iron Fortress Charge ]
[ Rank: Common ( + ) ]

[ Description: Concentrates all physical power into a direct charge, charge speed increases significantly, upon impact, a powerful shockwave is released, the chance of breaking shields and armors is very high, the longer the charge distance, the greater the impact power. The power of each strike depends on the amount of mana consumed. ]
Lian read the description for a few moments.
"Not bad for breaking defensive lines." This was a skill he could use in wars to break the enemy’s military formations.
Then he went to the second skill, which he had obtained from the Thunder Spine Serpent.
[ Thunderstep ]
[ Rank: Common ( + ) ]

[ Description: With each movement, lightning energy is stored in the user’s legs, allows instant Dash over short distances up to 500 meters, after each Dash, an electrical explosion is created, enemies around who are at least 5 levels weaker than the user become temporarily paralyzed. Consumes 2 mana per minute. ]
This time Lian’s eyes really sparkled.
"If I combine this with Fallen Wolf Speed..." He did not even finish the sentence, this skill could take his speed to a completely new level.
Without a doubt... this was one of the best skills he had obtained so far.
Besides, paralyzing enemies was also a huge help, even if it only works on enemies 5 levels weaker than him, it can be very helpful in wars or battles with large groups of monsters.
Besides, if it is upgraded, its range and offensive power might increase too.
The third skill.
[ Predator’s Frenzy ]
[ Rank: Common ( + ) ]
[ Description: Each time the user kills an enemy 5 levels higher, Attack Speed increases by 3 units, Critical Damage also increases by 3 units. Consumes 3 mana per minute. ]
A calm smile settled on Lian’s face.
"So the more I kill, the stronger I become, but if I’m not mistaken, attack speed and Critical Damage are among the traits that become accessible after the first evolution."

This was exactly suitable for his own crazy fighting style, and what caught his attention was that this skill increased trait stats that an awakened one who has not passed the first evolution does not have access to.
Critical Damage and attack speed are both traits that can be increased with fragments, but unfortunately, their panel is still not open.
And the last skill, which he had obtained from the River Fang Eel.
[ Water Air ]
[ Rank: Common ( + ) ]
[ Description: The user can breathe underwater without any problem, resistance in water increases by 20%. ]
Lian calmly nodded, compared to the previous ones, it was weaker, but at least he no longer needs to worry in water environments.
Defense... Diamond Skin and Solar Forge Aegis, almost perfect.
Speed... Fallen Wolf Speed, Thunderstep.
Tracking... Predator’s Instincts.
Field control... Eternal Frozen Apocalypse.
And now... his offensive power had also made a big leap, but despite all this... he quietly whispered under his breath.
"But still not enough to kill a Level 35."
The battle with the Abyssal River Drake had taught him that he still had a very long way to go to reach the most powerful creatures of this world.
Still... a long road lay ahead.
At that same moment...
Knock...
Knock...
The quiet sound of knocking on the door was heard, Lian raised his head.
The door opened and one of the doctors entered the room and said with respect.
"Two people have come to see you."
Lian raised an eyebrow.
"Who?"
The doctor paused for a moment.
"Commander Elizabeth." And then he continued.
"And Commander Valerian Cross."
Lian remained motionless for a few seconds, then calmly closed the system window.
It seemed... the commanders of both bases had come to say hello.

chapters.title: Chapter 165: The Calm After the Storm IV
paragraphs: Lian was sitting half-reclined on the bed.
A few moments later, the door opened and two people entered.
Commander Elizabeth.
And next to her, a tall man also entered the room.
Commander Valerian Cross.

Both commanders looked at Lian for a few moments, if the news that two commanders from two different bases had come to visit an 18-year-old awakened one had spread, it would probably have caused a great shock to everyone.
Both of them, although they are not among the most powerful in the world, are the chosen representatives of their country for leading and protecting the bases.
And now both of these individuals had come to visit a hero who had played a big role in saving the base.
Valerian was the first to break the silence.

"His appearance is better than what I expected, clearly his body is out of danger, but he still shouldn’t put too much pressure on himself." Then he calmly approached the bed and his gaze fixed directly on Lian.
"Nice to meet you, sir. I guess I don’t need to introduce myself," Lian said with a little awkwardness, the guy had gotten too close!
"Nice to meet you, I am Commander Valerian, commander of Base #5."
"If it weren’t for you... when we reached the Frontier Base, probably nothing of this base would have remained, I have to thank you."
The room fell into silence for a few moments and Lian gave a faint smile.
"I just tried to do my duty."
"Sometimes that is the hardest thing in the world, you did a very great thing." A small smile settled on Valerian’s face.
He had done a small investigation about this boy’s identity and was aware of his achievement in the border city, and more importantly, he was also aware that he was from the Vorhelm clan.
He had always known the Vorhelms as arrogant and self-satisfied people, and in his imagination they were like that, but this one seemed to know when to be humble and respectful.
"I also have to thank you, protecting this base is my duty, but you helped much more than I did." Elizabeth also nodded calmly and added.
Lian just smiled, he didn’t know if these two would still have these reactions if they knew that he himself was responsible for what had happened.
"For the help you gave, definitely a big reward will be arranged for you and it will be paid by the government, also you will receive payment for all the monsters you killed." Then she added.
"Thank you." Lian’s eyes sparkled, as if he was going to receive more reward than he had expected.
Unfortunately, he could not ask for the monster corpses to feed the Devourer because it would look very suspicious, but it was not a problem.
He could collect corpses himself by hunting, and he could probably also buy from the black market.
"I heard you captured a native human alive, I would like to know how." Valerian did not waste any more time and went straight to the main point.
Lian gave a quick look at Elizabeth and then started telling the story.
About finding the ruin, about Kain’s disappearance, about the long search through the ancient corridors.
About the two white-robed guards, about the battle, and finally, capturing one of them.
But he did not say even one word about Kain’s changes or what had happened in the depths of the temple, and when he finished, Valerian said slowly.
"The initial interrogation has been done." He placed his hands behind his back and continued.
"The information we obtained... is more important than anything we expected."
"That man... is from one of the seven human regions of this world." Elizabeth’s face also became serious.
Lian remained silent, he knew this part himself.
Valerian continued.
"The name of his region is Region Three, apparently they use numbers for the names of the regions."
Even saying that name was accompanied by a kind of respect for the prisoner.
"According to him, the population of that region is a few hundred thousand people."

"They have an organized government, they have a permanent army, economy, education system... almost a complete civilization, but one region. It is completely isolated, according to the prisoner, very tall walls and defensive layers have completely closed off the region to keep them safe from monsters."
This form of remaining civilization is practically the most advanced they had ever heard about.
The issue was so big that they sent all the information to the federation.
"So this world’s civilization never disappeared." Lian whispered quietly.
"At least not completely, their population does not seem large, maybe a few million people, which is very small compared to our world which reaches billions." Elizabeth answered.
But very soon, the atmosphere of the room became heavy again and Valerian said with a frown.
"We also have a big problem, that mage escaped according to you."
Lian frowned.
"That means now there is a high chance Region Three knows one of their people has been captured by us."
Elizabeth took a deep breath and added.
"And more importantly, they know someone infiltrated their temple and bathed in that spring... the Spring of Light?"
Lian said nothing, it seemed these two also knew about that spring, and they had definitely interrogated Kain too, and his friend had probably told them the same amount he had told him.
His face did not change, but his mind started analyzing the situation quickly, from the perspective of those natives... Kain had destroyed their most sacred heritage.
"If before this only powerful monsters were our enemy, from today maybe a human civilization has also become our enemy." Valerian said with a calm but heavy voice.
A heavy silence filled the room, no one had a sentence to answer.
A few minutes later, Valerian changed the subject.
"Anyway, tonight the commanders’ council meeting will be held, all commanders Level 30 and above will be present." Then he looked directly at Lian.
"I would like you to be there too."
"Me?" Lian was surprised for a moment.
"You are the only one who faced that ruin, those humans, and those monsters, your information is more than all of ours, your opinion is valuable for this meeting."
Lian also nodded and did not refuse, the two left after saying goodbye, and he also, after thinking and after a little effort, got up to get ready.
A few hours later...
The Base council hall.
A large hall with a high ceiling, its walls covered with maps of discovered areas, in the center of the room, a massive table was placed.
On it, a 3D map of the region was displayed, all the high-level commanders were present.
Lian had also come and was sitting in a corner.
With the arrival of Valerian and Elizabeth, the meeting officially began.
Elizabeth placed her hand on the map, a blue aura appeared around it.
"This is the current range of Base #3." A circle with a radius of approximately one hundred kilometers lit up on the map.
"Until the recent battle, the three main races north of the base were the biggest obstacle to our advancement." Their names appeared one by one on the map.
Ironfang Ravagers.
Thunder Spine Serpents.
Ironhorn Marsh Drakes.
"But now all three races have been destroyed." A few red points on the map went dark.
"The path is open and we can finally start advancing again, although before that we definitely need to regain some strength."
Valerian stepped forward, he was not the commander of this base but he could advise however he wanted.
"My suggestion is this." He expanded the blue circle on the map.
Four hundred kilometers... six hundred... eight hundred... one thousand... and finally... one thousand five hundred kilometers.

"In the next three months, increase the exploration radius from one hundred kilometers to one thousand five hundred kilometers." By reaching this radius, two bases could almost create a safe corridor to each other.
Valerian continued.
"The targets are clear, ancient ruins, mana mines, valuable plants, hidden and special areas." And then with a short pause he said.
"And native civilizations, these are the most valuable things we should be looking for, we need to find out exactly where those seven regions are."
One of the commanders said excitedly.
"If there really are seven human countries, there might also be thousands of undiscovered ruins and hidden areas."
"This way we can progress faster and cleanse this Ruined Realm."
A few people nodded in agreement with him.
At that same moment... Elizabeth turned her gaze toward Lian.
"What is your opinion?"
The entire hall fell silent, even Valerian waited for the answer.
Lian stared at the map for a few moments and then said calmly.
"I don’t think our priority should be the ruins."
A few people looked at each other in surprise, ruins were one of the biggest ways to progress.
Lian continued.
"First we should find the humans, if they are enemies, no ruin is valuable, in fact, the ruins might be traps that they use against us, exactly like what happened to me and my friend."
"We need to gather as much information as possible about them, if they really see us as a threat, they might do something against us sooner or later."
He knew that from the perspective of the native people of this world, they were considered barbarians, and that meant they did not have a good view of them at all.

"And sooner or later we will be forced to go to war with a complete civilization, but if we can form an alliance with them, it is worth more than a thousand ruins, maybe with their help we can even find the seven crystals and the seven cores of the world."
No one said anything immediately, even the experienced commanders looked at the map in silence.

Everyone realized that the biggest discovery of this mission was not an ancient ruin... and not even a Fallen monster, but the truth that beyond the known borders... living, powerful, and unknown civilizations were still breathing.

"His appearance is better than what I expected, clearly his body is out of danger, but he still shouldn’t put too much pressure on himself." Then he calmly approached the bed and his gaze fixed directly on Lian.
"Nice to meet you, sir.
I guess I don’t need to introduce myself," Lian said with a little awkwardness, the guy had gotten too close!
"Nice to meet you, I am Commander Valerian, commander of Base #5."
"If it weren’t for you... when we reached the Frontier Base, probably nothing of this base would have remained, I have to thank you."
The room fell into silence for a few moments and Lian gave a faint smile.
"I just tried to do my duty."
"Sometimes that is the hardest thing in the world, you did a very great thing." A small smile settled on Valerian’s face.
He had done a small investigation about this boy’s identity and was aware of his achievement in the border city, and more importantly, he was also aware that he was from the Vorhelm clan.
He had always known the Vorhelms as arrogant and self-satisfied people, and in his imagination they were like that, but this one seemed to know when to be humble and respectful.
"I also have to thank you, protecting this base is my duty, but you helped much more than I did." Elizabeth also nodded calmly and added.
Lian just smiled, he didn’t know if these two would still have these reactions if they knew that he himself was responsible for what had happened.
"For the help you gave, definitely a big reward will be arranged for you and it will be paid by the government, also you will receive payment for all the monsters you killed." Then she added.
"Thank you." Lian’s eyes sparkled, as if he was going to receive more reward than he had expected.
Unfortunately, he could not ask for the monster corpses to feed the Devourer because it would look very suspicious, but it was not a problem.
He could collect corpses himself by hunting, and he could probably also buy from the black market.
"I heard you captured a native human alive, I would like to know how." Valerian did not waste any more time and went straight to the main point.
Lian gave a quick look at Elizabeth and then started telling the story.
About finding the ruin, about Kain’s disappearance, about the long search through the ancient corridors.
About the two white-robed guards, about the battle, and finally, capturing one of them.
But he did not say even one word about Kain’s changes or what had happened in the depths of the temple, and when he finished, Valerian said slowly.
"The initial interrogation has been done." He placed his hands behind his back and continued.
"The information we obtained... is more important than anything we expected."
"That man... is from one of the seven human regions of this world." Elizabeth’s face also became serious.
Lian remained silent, he knew this part himself.
Valerian continued.
"The name of his region is Region Three, apparently they use numbers for the names of the regions."
Even saying that name was accompanied by a kind of respect for the prisoner.
"According to him, the population of that region is a few hundred thousand people."
"They have an organized government, they have a permanent army, economy, education system... almost a complete civilization, but one region.
It is completely isolated, according to the prisoner, very tall walls and defensive layers have completely closed off the region to keep them safe from monsters."
This form of remaining civilization is practically the most advanced they had ever heard about.
The issue was so big that they sent all the information to the federation.
"So this world’s civilization never disappeared." Lian whispered quietly.
"At least not completely, their population does not seem large, maybe a few million people, which is very small compared to our world which reaches billions." Elizabeth answered.
But very soon, the atmosphere of the room became heavy again and Valerian said with a frown.
"We also have a big problem, that mage escaped according to you."
Lian frowned.
"That means now there is a high chance Region Three knows one of their people has been captured by us."
Elizabeth took a deep breath and added.
"And more importantly, they know someone infiltrated their temple and bathed in that spring... the Spring of Light?"
Lian said nothing, it seemed these two also knew about that spring, and they had definitely interrogated Kain too, and his friend had probably told them the same amount he had told him.
His face did not change, but his mind started analyzing the situation quickly, from the perspective of those natives...
Kain had destroyed their most sacred heritage.
"If before this only powerful monsters were our enemy, from today maybe a human civilization has also become our enemy." Valerian said with a calm but heavy voice.
A heavy silence filled the room, no one had a sentence to answer.
A few minutes later, Valerian changed the subject.
"Anyway, tonight the commanders’ council meeting will be held, all commanders Level 30 and above will be present." Then he looked directly at Lian.
"I would like you to be there too."
"Me?" Lian was surprised for a moment.
"You are the only one who faced that ruin, those humans, and those monsters, your information is more than all of ours, your opinion is valuable for this meeting."
Lian also nodded and did not refuse, the two left after saying goodbye, and he also, after thinking and after a little effort, got up to get ready.
A few hours later...
The Base council hall.
A large hall with a high ceiling, its walls covered with maps of discovered areas, in the center of the room, a massive table was placed.
On it, a 3D map of the region was displayed, all the high-level commanders were present.
Lian had also come and was sitting in a corner.
With the arrival of Valerian and Elizabeth, the meeting officially began.
Elizabeth placed her hand on the map, a blue aura appeared around it.
"This is the current range of Base #3." A circle with a radius of approximately one hundred kilometers lit up on the map.
"Until the recent battle, the three main races north of the base were the biggest obstacle to our advancement." Their names appeared one by one on the map.
Ironfang Ravagers.
Thunder Spine Serpents.
Ironhorn Marsh Drakes.
"But now all three races have been destroyed." A few red points on the map went dark.
"The path is open and we can finally start advancing again, although before that we definitely need to regain some strength."
Valerian stepped forward, he was not the commander of this base but he could advise however he wanted.
"My suggestion is this." He expanded the blue circle on the map.
Four hundred kilometers... six hundred... eight hundred... one thousand... and finally... one thousand five hundred kilometers.

"In the next three months, increase the exploration radius from one hundred kilometers to one thousand five hundred kilometers." By reaching this radius, two bases could almost create a safe corridor to each other.
Valerian continued.
"The targets are clear, ancient ruins, mana mines, valuable plants, hidden and special areas." And then with a short pause he said.
"And native civilizations, these are the most valuable things we should be looking for, we need to find out exactly where those seven regions are."
One of the commanders said excitedly.
"If there really are seven human countries, there might also be thousands of undiscovered ruins and hidden areas."
"This way we can progress faster and cleanse this Ruined Realm."
A few people nodded in agreement with him.
At that same moment...
Elizabeth turned her gaze toward Lian.
"What is your opinion?"
The entire hall fell silent, even Valerian waited for the answer.
Lian stared at the map for a few moments and then said calmly.
"I don’t think our priority should be the ruins."
A few people looked at each other in surprise, ruins were one of the biggest ways to progress.
Lian continued.
"First we should find the humans, if they are enemies, no ruin is valuable, in fact, the ruins might be traps that they use against us, exactly like what happened to me and my friend."
"We need to gather as much information as possible about them, if they really see us as a threat, they might do something against us sooner or later."
He knew that from the perspective of the native people of this world, they were considered barbarians, and that meant they did not have a good view of them at all.

"And sooner or later we will be forced to go to war with a complete civilization, but if we can form an alliance with them, it is worth more than a thousand ruins, maybe with their help we can even find the seven crystals and the seven cores of the world."
No one said anything immediately, even the experienced commanders looked at the map in silence.

Everyone realized that the biggest discovery of this mission was not an ancient ruin... and not even a Fallen monster, but the truth that beyond the known borders... living, powerful, and unknown civilizations were still breathing.

chapters.title: Chapter 166: Back to Acadmey
paragraphs: The commanders’ council hall was slowly emptying.
After hours of discussion, reviewing maps, and making decisions about the Base’s future, the commanders were leaving their seats one by one.
A few were still discussing the seven human territories whose existence was no longer just a legend.
Others were leaning over the 3D map, talking about possible exploration routes up to a radius of fifteen hundred kilometers.
With the destruction of the three main races around the base, advancement had become possible, and this opportunity could pave the way for them greatly.
However, because of Lian’s words, everyone had developed a bad view of the ruins, and this had become a cause for concern.
Ruins had always been a source of treasures and many paths to progress, and the fact that they might now be used as traps by the natives had caused fear.
But did they really have to abandon the ruins? In the end, it was suggested that if they did find a ruin, they should definitely enter it as a group and try to avoid entering alone.
Valerian was the last person to pass by the command table. He stopped in front of Lian and gave him a careful look.
"Thank you for the points you mentioned. They made us understand that this Ruined Realm can be different from all the previous ones. Even the ruins will no longer be that safe."
Lian gave a short smile.
"You’re welcome. I just made a simple point. We have to be careful with our lives. After all, if we die, we cause monsters to enter our own world." He then added.
"Besides, fighting and being at war with monsters is one thing. Being at war with an intelligent and powerful civilization of humans is another. We need to be careful."
Valerian nodded calmly.
"When you are fully recovered, my base will always welcome you. I think our cooperation has just begun."
"Thank you for the invitation." Lian replied with respect.
"It was a pleasure meeting you. It’s time for me to return to my own base." The level 40 commander gave a faint smile and, without saying anything more, left the hall.
A few steps away, Elizabeth was also ready to leave. Before exiting, she paused for a moment and turned back.
"For now, just rest. You fought more than your share. This time, let your body breathe. We will need you for advancement in the Ruined Realm."
Lian nodded.
"Of course."
When the hall door closed, only a few officials remained. The meeting... had finally ended.
A few hours later... the sun was slowly hiding behind the massive walls of the Base, and the orange light of sunset was shining through the window of Lian’s quiet room.
Knock knock knock
"Come in."
The door opened slowly and Kain entered. Upon seeing Lian sitting on a chair this time, he smiled.
"Finally free from the meeting."
"Fortunately."
Kain sat on the chair opposite and for a few seconds both looked out the window in silence, then he asked.
"So, what’s your next plan?"
Lian did not say anything for a few moments, his mind went to his armor, or better to say... the remains of his armor.
A large part of it had melted, parts were completely broken, and a few metal plates were no longer usable.
Practically, he no longer had any armor.
"First, a new armor. My current one is finished."
"When I returned to the Vorhelm clan’s home, I obtained a monster skin. It shouldn’t go to waste, and I’m sure something good can be made with it." He continued a few moments later.
Kain looked at him in surprise.
"The skin of one of the most powerful monster races known to exist. If an armor is made from its skin, it will probably become one of the best S-rank armors." He thought for a moment.
"Maybe even an Ancient rank armor."
"That’s not something just anyone can do. Making an Ancient rank armor requires truly high skill." Kain’s eyes widened slightly.
"That’s why I was looking for you. Do you know anyone who can help?"
"Maybe I know someone." Kain thought for a moment, then as if remembering something, he pondered for a few moments.
"Who?" Lian raised his gaze.
"A blacksmith in the capital, but getting him to accept the order is very difficult."
Many people thought blacksmithing, like being a warrior or a mage, was an awakening class.
But the reality was completely different. No one awakened with the Blacksmith class.
Blacksmithing was a profession.
After the emergence of the Ruined Realms, humans had discovered thousands of books, tools, maps, and remnants of technologies from destroyed civilizations.
It took decades for researchers to reconstruct only a small part of that knowledge, and from that research, new professions were born.
Master Blacksmith.
Alchemist.
Artifact Craftsman.
All of them were professions, not classes. Anyone could learn them, but reaching mastery sometimes required several decades of time.
For this reason, true masters were very rare.
Kain continued.
"His name is Magnus Ironsoul. He has been making armor and weapons for over thirty years. They say most of the armor used by high-level guild leaders now is his work."
"But he’s a strange person."
"What kind of person?" Lian asked curiously. He didn’t know any blacksmiths, but he had always been curious about them.
"He has a strange obsession. He doesn’t accept all clients."
"If he finds the materials worthless, he won’t even look at them. And if he doesn’t like the client’s personality... he’ll throw them out directly." Kain laughed.
"I heard even the President had to wait weeks for his turn."
Lian thought for a few seconds and then smiled.
"Then we’ll try."
"Really?" Kain raised an eyebrow.
"Yeah."
Lian looked outside.
"Before I start my next exploration, I need a new armor. This time I want to go much further, at least five thousand kilometers. Without proper armor... it’s very dangerous."
He planned to go on an exploration journey instead of exploration patrols.
This way, reaching level 20 would happen much sooner.
"Right now?" Kain asked in surprise.
"The sooner, the better."
His friend looked at him for a few moments and then shrugged.
"Anyway, I don’t have anything special to do right now, so let’s go."
Lian nodded calmly, but suddenly something came to his mind.
"There’s another thing I need to do. A few of the treasures from that ruin are still in my storage space. I need to sell them."
The next morning... finally, the main gate of the Base opened calmly and without anxiety.
Lian and Kain were ready to leave, but before reaching the portal, someone was waiting for them.
Seraphina.
"Take care of yourselves, and please, don’t do anything foolish again."
"Of course." Lian smiled and then asked.
"What are your plans?"
"Me and the rest of the student council are also going to return to the academy soon." Seraphina added.
"Oh? Something happened?"

"Remember that Special area the federation found? Finally, the entry quotas have been distributed, and the academy has also been given a number of quotas. We have to return to the academy to prepare and for the student council to distribute the quotas."
"I thought it was a Hidden area." Lian nodded, Special areas, as their name suggests, are very special.
If entry quotas are really going to be distributed, then he cannot miss it either.
"It has been confirmed to be a Special area." Seraphina added.
"Then I’ll see you at the academy soon." They then said goodbye.
A few minutes later... they reached the central square of the Base. In the center of the square... the base’s massive portal was located.
A column of blue light stretching dozens of meters into the sky, hundreds of awakened ones were coming and going, some were just entering the Ruined Realm.
Some were returning after completing missions, and many were going to rest.
Lian stopped for the last time, his gaze moving across the base’s massive walls.
Right here, he had been only a few steps away from death. He had been here for a short time, but many things had happened to him.
Then, together with Kain, he stepped toward the portal. The blue light engulfed both of them, and for a few seconds... everything was drowned in absolute whiteness.
When the light faded... the cool and familiar air of the modern world caressed their faces.
They... had finally returned to their own world.

chapters.title: Chapter 167: Ironsoul Forge
paragraphs: The blue light of the portal slowly faded, and a few moments later, Lian and Kain appeared again on the academy’s transfer platform.
Unlike the temporary portals inside the Ruined Realm, this portal was located inside the academy building.
They had not even taken a few steps away from the transfer platform when one of the academy staff members in formal attire came to greet them.
"Please give me your student codes, we need to register your return."
Both Lian and Kain gave their codes, and the staff member entered them into the academy system.
[ Ruined Realm Exit Confirmed ]
[ Exit Successfully Registered ]
The staff member paused for a moment, his eyes shifting several times between the notification and Lian’s face, it was clear that he recognized his name.
"Welcome back... Mr. Lian." His tone was more respectful than usual.
Kain gave a faint smile upon seeing his change in behavior, the news of the Base battle had spread across the entire academy and even a large part of the federation with incredible speed.
Of course, he did not know that it was not just the news of what happened in the Ruined Realm, but Lian had also gained great fame because of the border city.
The students who were waiting for their turn to enter or exit slowly started whispering, currently, the events of the Ruined Realm were on everyone’s lips.
"That’s him..."
"He’s the one they say destroyed a large part of the monster army..."
"I didn’t think it was really him..."
Lian did not even look at them, as if those whispers did not exist at all.
A few minutes later, the two left the transfer building and even the academy, the fresh air of the capital hit their faces.
After a few days in the Ruined Realm, the scene in front of them seemed strange for a moment.
Wide streets full of cars, glass towers reflecting sunlight, massive holographic screens broadcasting the latest news about the Ruined Realms.
In the sky, a few special federation flying vehicles were passing between the buildings.
It bore no resemblance to the world of blood, monsters, and ruins.
Kain took a deep breath.
"We’re finally back, where first?" Then he looked at Lian.
"The blacksmith." Lian did not even think for a moment.
"Then let’s go." Kain smiled.
"Anyway, I never thought I would miss this boring world." He chuckled with a grin.
About an hour later, the two entered one of the oldest neighborhoods in the capital.
Unlike the modern city center, this place had a completely different atmosphere, stone buildings, old metal signs.
Smoke from furnaces rising from the rooftops, this neighborhood was the heart of the country’s craftsmen.
There were no ordinary stores here, every building belonged to one of the great master craftsmen.
Rune Engravers who could carve ancient runes onto equipment.
Artifact Craftsmen who restored legendary items.
Alchemists who made potions worth thousands of dollars per drop.
Jewel Crafters who turned monster cores into jewelry.
In front of most of the stores, several armed guards were standing.
Inside these buildings, materials were stored, some of which were worth more than a multi-story building.
Security here was directly provided by the government and the federation, and these guards, although they looked normal, were professional and very powerful.
Blacksmiths are considered very important people for every country, especially master blacksmiths, of whom there are not many.
After a few minutes of walking, Kain stopped.
At the end of the street, a building larger than all the surrounding buildings stood.
Its walls were made of black steel, and thick smoke was coming out of its massive chimneys.
Above the entrance, a metal sign with raised letters could be seen.
Ironsoul Forge
"We’re here."
Upon entering, a wave of intense heat greeted them.
The sound of hammers hitting metal filled the entire workshop.
Streams of molten metal were passing through stone channels.
Shining runes on the walls were lit, guiding mana throughout the furnaces.

Several apprentices in fireproof clothes were busy making weapons and armor, and in the center of them all... an old man with a tall stature, broad shoulders, and completely white hair, standing behind a massive anvil.
His arms were covered with old burn scars.
While striking a piece of metal without stopping, without even raising his head, he said.
"If you came for an order, turn back."
The sound of the hammer was heard.
"I don’t have time for the next six months."
"Master Magnus, we—" Kain stepped forward, this was not the first time he had come here, he had come a few times before with his father.
But this old man clearly neither recognized him nor cared at all about who he was.
"I said no, I don’t listen to unnecessary words, we have no slots, get lost." The old man did not even let him finish his sentence.
Kain fell silent, even feeling a little embarrassed, and did not know what to say.
Lian did not say anything, this old man was perhaps the grumpiest person he had ever seen, comparable to and maybe even worse than Rhea.
But they did not leave immediately, he wanted to try something before leaving.
He calmly reached his hand into the storage space, the next moment... a massive black skin spread out on the ground.
The entire workshop fell into silence.
The sound of hammers stopped, the apprentices froze in place.
Even the flow of molten metal seemed to slow down, Magnus raised his head for the first time and at first just looked with impatience.
But... he stepped forward two steps, then four more steps, his gray eyes slowly widened, and he placed his trembling hand on the skin.
For a few seconds, he did not even breathe.
"...Impossible." He finally whispered under his breath.
He almost took the skin from Lian’s hands, pulling out several strange tools from the metal drawers.
One was like a crystalline magnifying glass, another a plate covered with golden runes.
The third was a silver needle from which mana was emanating, one after another, the runes were activated, and blue, green, purple, and golden lights moved across the skin’s surface.
Every time a new result appeared, the old man’s face became more serious.
For about five full minutes, no one said anything, in the end... Magnus suddenly held his breath.
"This..." His throat was dry, even he himself could not believe what he was seeing, as if he was dreaming.
"The skin of a World Devourer Giant..."
"Master... that’s impossible..." One of the apprentices said unconsciously.
The old man turned back angrily.
"Shut up." His voice echoed through the workshop like an explosion.
"If you don’t know something, don’t speak."
The apprentice immediately lowered his head, no one else dared to open their mouth.
A few minutes ago... Magnus wanted to throw them out of the workshop.
But now... he brought two chairs himself, poured tea for both of them, and even personally locked the large workshop door.
The sound of the door locking surprised all the apprentices, no one remembered the last time the master had done such a thing for anyone.
So even their master could show special treatment to others?
They did not know whether to laugh or cry, they had not even seen their master treat the President with such behavior.
The old man sat in front of Lian, his gaze still not leaving the skin, and a few moments later he asked.
"This... where did you get it?"
"From the family." Lian answered without any change in his expression.
Magnus stared at his face for a few seconds, did he think he was a fool? Which family could have the corpse of this monster?
If it was a normal giant, that would be one thing... but a damn Unholy?
In the end, he just nodded calmly, he did not ask anything more, in the awakened world, the origin of some treasures is considered a forbidden question.
If the owner did not want to say anything, continuing would be disrespectful.
The old man ran his hand over the skin again, this time he could no longer hide his excitement.
"With this... maybe I can make an Ancient rank armor." A very small smile settled on his face.
No one said anything, even the apprentices held their breath.
"...Ancient?" One of them whispered quietly.
Magnus nodded calmly.
"If I succeed, it will be the masterpiece of my entire life."
Lian stared at the skin for a few moments, this was exactly what he wanted, an Ancient rank armor, and then he asked quietly.
"What do you need? And how much will it cost?"
"The materials?" Magnus answered without taking his gaze off the skin.
He gave a bitter smile.
"No... the materials are not the problem." A few seconds of silence passed, and then he looked at Lian, a look that held both excitement and regret.
"The problem is... I need a hammer... a hammer that can actually work on such skin."

sentences.text: The blue light of the portal slowly faded, and a few moments later, Lian and Kain appeared again on the academy’s transfer platform.
Unlike the temporary portals inside the Ruined Realm, this portal was located inside the academy building.
They had not even taken a few steps away from the transfer platform when one of the academy staff members in formal attire came to greet them.
"Please give me your student codes, we need to register your return."
Both Lian and Kain gave their codes, and the staff member entered them into the academy system.
[ Ruined Realm Exit Confirmed ]
[ Exit Successfully Registered ]
The staff member paused for a moment, his eyes shifting several times between the notification and Lian’s face, it was clear that he recognized his name.
"Welcome back...
Mr.
Lian." His tone was more respectful than usual.
Kain gave a faint smile upon seeing his change in behavior, the news of the Base battle had spread across the entire academy and even a large part of the federation with incredible speed.
Of course, he did not know that it was not just the news of what happened in the Ruined Realm, but Lian had also gained great fame because of the border city.
The students who were waiting for their turn to enter or exit slowly started whispering, currently, the events of the Ruined Realm were on everyone’s lips.
"That’s him..."
"He’s the one they say destroyed a large part of the monster army..."
"I didn’t think it was really him..."
Lian did not even look at them, as if those whispers did not exist at all.
A few minutes later, the two left the transfer building and even the academy, the fresh air of the capital hit their faces.
After a few days in the Ruined Realm, the scene in front of them seemed strange for a moment.
Wide streets full of cars, glass towers reflecting sunlight, massive holographic screens broadcasting the latest news about the Ruined Realms.
In the sky, a few special federation flying vehicles were passing between the buildings.
It bore no resemblance to the world of blood, monsters, and ruins.
Kain took a deep breath.
"We’re finally back, where first?" Then he looked at Lian.
"The blacksmith." Lian did not even think for a moment.
"Then let’s go." Kain smiled.
"Anyway, I never thought I would miss this boring world." He chuckled with a grin.
About an hour later, the two entered one of the oldest neighborhoods in the capital.
Unlike the modern city center, this place had a completely different atmosphere, stone buildings, old metal signs.
Smoke from furnaces rising from the rooftops, this neighborhood was the heart of the country’s craftsmen.
There were no ordinary stores here, every building belonged to one of the great master craftsmen.
Rune Engravers who could carve ancient runes onto equipment.
Artifact Craftsmen who restored legendary items.
Alchemists who made potions worth thousands of dollars per drop.
Jewel Crafters who turned monster cores into jewelry.
In front of most of the stores, several armed guards were standing.
Inside these buildings, materials were stored, some of which were worth more than a multi-story building.
Security here was directly provided by the government and the federation, and these guards, although they looked normal, were professional and very powerful.
Blacksmiths are considered very important people for every country, especially master blacksmiths, of whom there are not many.
After a few minutes of walking, Kain stopped.
At the end of the street, a building larger than all the surrounding buildings stood.
Its walls were made of black steel, and thick smoke was coming out of its massive chimneys.
Above the entrance, a metal sign with raised letters could be seen.
Ironsoul Forge
"We’re here."
Upon entering, a wave of intense heat greeted them.
The sound of hammers hitting metal filled the entire workshop.
Streams of molten metal were passing through stone channels.
Shining runes on the walls were lit, guiding mana throughout the furnaces.

Several apprentices in fireproof clothes were busy making weapons and armor, and in the center of them all... an old man with a tall stature, broad shoulders, and completely white hair, standing behind a massive anvil.
His arms were covered with old burn scars.
While striking a piece of metal without stopping, without even raising his head, he said.
"If you came for an order, turn back."
The sound of the hammer was heard.
"I don’t have time for the next six months."
"Master Magnus, we—" Kain stepped forward, this was not the first time he had come here, he had come a few times before with his father.
But this old man clearly neither recognized him nor cared at all about who he was.
"I said no, I don’t listen to unnecessary words, we have no slots, get lost." The old man did not even let him finish his sentence.
Kain fell silent, even feeling a little embarrassed, and did not know what to say.
Lian did not say anything, this old man was perhaps the grumpiest person he had ever seen, comparable to and maybe even worse than Rhea.
But they did not leave immediately, he wanted to try something before leaving.
He calmly reached his hand into the storage space, the next moment... a massive black skin spread out on the ground.
The entire workshop fell into silence.
The sound of hammers stopped, the apprentices froze in place.
Even the flow of molten metal seemed to slow down, Magnus raised his head for the first time and at first just looked with impatience.
But... he stepped forward two steps, then four more steps, his gray eyes slowly widened, and he placed his trembling hand on the skin.
For a few seconds, he did not even breathe.
"...Impossible." He finally whispered under his breath.
He almost took the skin from Lian’s hands, pulling out several strange tools from the metal drawers.
One was like a crystalline magnifying glass, another a plate covered with golden runes.
The third was a silver needle from which mana was emanating, one after another, the runes were activated, and blue, green, purple, and golden lights moved across the skin’s surface.
Every time a new result appeared, the old man’s face became more serious.
For about five full minutes, no one said anything, in the end...
Magnus suddenly held his breath.
"This..." His throat was dry, even he himself could not believe what he was seeing, as if he was dreaming.
"The skin of a World Devourer Giant..."
"Master... that’s impossible..." One of the apprentices said unconsciously.
The old man turned back angrily.
"Shut up." His voice echoed through the workshop like an explosion.
"If you don’t know something, don’t speak."
The apprentice immediately lowered his head, no one else dared to open their mouth.
A few minutes ago...
Magnus wanted to throw them out of the workshop.
But now... he brought two chairs himself, poured tea for both of them, and even personally locked the large workshop door.
The sound of the door locking surprised all the apprentices, no one remembered the last time the master had done such a thing for anyone.
So even their master could show special treatment to others?
They did not know whether to laugh or cry, they had not even seen their master treat the President with such behavior.
The old man sat in front of Lian, his gaze still not leaving the skin, and a few moments later he asked.
"This... where did you get it?"
"From the family." Lian answered without any change in his expression.
Magnus stared at his face for a few seconds, did he think he was a fool?
Which family could have the corpse of this monster?
If it was a normal giant, that would be one thing... but a damn Unholy?
In the end, he just nodded calmly, he did not ask anything more, in the awakened world, the origin of some treasures is considered a forbidden question.
If the owner did not want to say anything, continuing would be disrespectful.

"With this... maybe I can make an Ancient rank armor." A very small smile settled on his face.
No one said anything, even the apprentices held their breath.
"...Ancient?" One of them whispered quietly.
Magnus nodded calmly.
"If I succeed, it will be the masterpiece of my entire life."
Lian stared at the skin for a few moments, this was exactly what he wanted, an Ancient rank armor, and then he asked quietly.
"What do you need?
And how much will it cost?"
"The materials?" Magnus answered without taking his gaze off the skin.
He gave a bitter smile.
"No... the materials are not the problem." A few seconds of silence passed, and then he looked at Lian, a look that held both excitement and regret.
"The problem is...
I need a hammer... a hammer that can actually work on such skin."

chapters.title: Chapter 168: The Blacksmiths Association
paragraphs: Magnus still had not taken his gaze off the massive skin, a few seconds of silence passed.
Lian and Kain were still waiting for him to explain what he meant by what he said, and then he quietly took a deep breath and said.
"The problem is that my tools cannot even damage it."
"What do you mean?" Kain asked in surprise, he did not expect that one of the country’s greatest blacksmiths would have a problem making armor from this corpse.
Does that really mean making armor from the corpse of an Unholy is that hard?
The old man, without answering, pointed to one of his apprentices.
"Bring hammer number seven."
The apprentice paused for a moment, then quickly ran toward the shelf at the end of the workshop.
A few moments later, he carried a massive hammer with a black steel handle and a silver-colored head with both hands.
Just looking at it was enough for anyone to understand this was not an ordinary tool.
Magnus took the hammer from him.
"With this hammer..."
His gaze fixed on Lian.
"Most of this country’s A Rank armors have been made with this, I have been using it for more than fifteen years."
He stepped forward and spread the World Devourer Giant’s skin on the special anvil.
All the apprentices had left their work, everyone was watching with curiosity.
Magnus wrapped both his hands around the hammer’s handle, the veins on his arms lit up, his muscles contracted, he raised the hammer above his head.
The next moment... BOOOM!
The sound of impact shook the entire workshop.
Sparks of fire scattered around, the metal anvil sank a few centimeters into the ground.
But... the skin did not get even the smallest scratch.
On the contrary... a very faint sound was heard.
Tick...
Magnus calmly raised the hammer, its metal edge... was chipped.
"Master... the hammer..." one of the apprentices whispered in disbelief, that small damage to the hammer could cause millions of dollars in loss for them.
Magnus just sighed and placed the hammer on the table.
"This is exactly what I wanted to show you."
"This skin... cannot be processed at all with my current tools."
"So the skin of an Unholy is that strong?" Kain asked again.

"No, the problem is not just that it is an Unholy, but its race, this corpse belongs to a race of monsters that were known for their defensive power, a defense that is stronger than mountains, penetrating it with normal hammers is not possible."
The workshop fell into silence again.
Even Lian realized for the first time how far the true value of this skin was beyond his imagination.
He knew the skin of this monster was definitely valuable, but not to this extent, to the point that even one of the country’s greatest blacksmiths could not penetrate it.
Magnus went toward one of the old shelves, from among dozens of leather books, he pulled out a thick and worn volume.
He opened it on the table, inside the book, an image of a massive hammer could be seen.
Its head was made of a golden-colored metal, and its entire handle was covered with ancient runes.
"Titan’s Forge Hammer." The old man said with special respect.
"The heritage of the Blacksmiths’ Association, its age goes back to several hundred years ago." He ran his finger over the image.
"Almost all the Ancient Rank equipment recorded in this country... were made with this very hammer."
Lian looked at the image carefully, even from a drawing, one could feel the greatness of that tool.
Their country did not have many Ancient rank treasures, no country had many, and most of such treasures were in the hands of the government or the top five guilds of the country.
And of course, the Vorhelm clan...
Magnus closed the book and sat on the chair.
"Don’t think any blacksmith can use it whenever they want, that hammer belongs to the Blacksmiths’ Association."
Then he started explaining.
Blacksmithing, unlike awakened classes, was a profession.
After the emergence of the Ruined Realms, humans had found thousands of books, tools, maps, and remaining knowledge from destroyed civilizations.
Years of research, testing, and failure caused a group of humans to revive part of that knowledge.
All of them were craftsmen, not awakened ones with special classes, and this had made the number of true masters very small.
The Blacksmiths’ Association was also considered the most powerful organization in this field, almost all the Master Blacksmiths of the country were members.
Even the government did not have direct control over the association.
Even the most powerful awakened ones sometimes waited for months in line to get a proper armor or weapon made, and the problem was that they couldn’t say anything.
Blacksmiths did not have combat power, but they were of extremely high importance and were respected throughout the world.
Some projects carried out inside the association had a value equivalent to fully equipping an army.
"So we’ll just borrow it." Kain said after a few moments of silence.
Magnus gave a bitter smile.
"I wish it were that simple." He looked at the hammer’s image again.
"The Titan’s Forge Hammer is only used for projects that the association’s council approves."
"If they determine the raw materials do not have enough value, permission to use it is not issued."
"Not out of stinginess, but because every time that hammer is used, the cost and depreciation are very high."
"No one is willing to take such a risk for a normal project, even though I don’t have much to do with those idiots, but without their permission, that hammer cannot be obtained.
"Is there a way to talk to them? I’m sure this project is valuable." Lian added this time.
Of course this project was valuable!
they were talking about making an Ancient rank armor, such an armor could become an industrial masterpiece
Anywhere in the world, such a project was valuable and extraordinary.
Magnus did not answer immediately and examined the skin for a few more minutes, sometimes touching it with his hand, sometimes looking at it under the runes’ light.
In the end, he raised his head and looked directly at Lian.
"Of course there is a way, and I will accept this project."
Lian smiled.
But Magnus continued.
"But... first I have to convince the members of the association’s council, if they don’t agree... there’s nothing I can do either."
Lian thought for a moment.
"How long will it take?" he then asked.
"If everything goes well, at least a month, but if the council opposes, maybe never."
A faint frown settled on Lian’s face.
As far as he knew, the leaders of the Blacksmiths’ Association were among the closest people to the President’s circle of advisors.
He knew this because the Blacksmiths’ Association is extremely famous, and its leader and the President are always seen together as allies and friends.
And the President... did not have a very good relationship with the Vorhelm clan.
Of course, he could not take direct action against the Vorhelm clan, he did not have the power, nor would the congress allow such a thing.
Even many cabinet members avoided and feared getting involved with that influential clan.
But... causing trouble for one of the young members of the clan? And without directly breaking the law?
It probably wouldn’t be too hard, this thought passed through Lian’s mind for a moment, but he said nothing, but it was too early to judge pessimistically.
And besides, a month was also a long time, he wanted the armor before entering the Special Areas, but it seemed such a thing was not possible.
At that same moment, the sound of running was heard from outside the workshop.
The door opened hurriedly, one of the apprentices entered breathlessly, sweat dripping from his forehead.
"Master..." he took a few deep breaths.
"The head of the association just entered the building, told me to inform you, he came about the weapon the President requested from us."
A deep frown settled on Magnus’s face, and he said under his breath, with a completely dissatisfied tone.
"...Who does that idiot think he is, coming without an appointment?"
Lian and Kain exchanged a quick look, both had almost simultaneously reached the same conclusion.
It seemed... this old man really did not have special respect for anyone.
