chapters.title: Chapter 169: Chairman Roland Ashcroft
paragraphs: The sound of calm footsteps echoed in the corridor outside the workshop.
A few seconds later, the heavy iron door opened and an elderly man entered.
His silver hair was carefully combed back, and he wore simple gray clothes; clothes that at first glance were no different from an ordinary craftsman’s attire.
But right at that moment, all the apprentices inside the workshop immediately stopped working and all bowed respectfully.
Even a few master craftsmen who were busy making equipment also put down their hammers.
"Chairman."
The atmosphere of the workshop suddenly changed completely.
Without anyone introducing him, Lian and Kain guessed that this man must be the same person the apprentice had been talking about.
Chairman Roland Ashcroft.

The head of the country’s Blacksmiths’ Association, one of the most influential men in the country, he had no direct combat power, but the biggest guilds and awakened ones of the country were all indebted to him and treated him with respect.
Roland gave a quick look around and went straight toward Magnus.
"Magnus, I came about the President’s order, I heard you finally decided to set a time for making that armor."
"Whenever its turn comes, I will make it, not sooner." Magnus sneered with impatience and then added.
"Making the armor he requested is not easy, an armor that can conduct the lightning element’s currents in the smoothest way? It takes time and needs a lot of materials."
"Why does he even want such an armor? He himself doesn’t use the lightning element."
Suddenly, Lian’s eyebrows rose slightly, such an armor would be perfect for a lightning mage... and the President himself was not a lightning mage.
But... suddenly Kael’s face appeared in his mind... could it be for his secret son? A gift?
Roland just gave a faint smile, it was clear that he was used to this old man’s strange temper, but right when he was about to speak again...
His gaze fixed on the massive skin that was on the anvil, his sentence remained half-finished, and a strange silence fell over the workshop.
He calmly stepped forward, then another step, and for a few moments just stared at the skin’s black surface.
He placed his hand gently on it, his eyebrows furrowed, and under his breath, so quietly that only those nearby could hear, he whispered.
"...Where did you find this?"
Without waiting for an answer, he opened a small leather bag from his belt.
He took out several strange tools from inside it, a crystal lens, a silver pen covered with runes, and a metal plate with mana lines carved on it.
He activated the tools one by one, blue and golden lights moved across the skin’s surface.
The runes lit up one after another, for several full minutes no sound was heard, even the apprentices did not dare to breathe loudly.
In the end, Roland calmly put the tools aside, his eyes still on the skin.
"There is no mistake..." He took a deep breath.
"The leader of the World Devourer Giants race.
Those few words were enough for silence to weigh heavily on the workshop again.
Even the chairman himself did not say anything for a few moments, as if his mind was still processing what he had seen, and then he calmly turned toward Magnus.
"How did you find this? Do you want to make something with it? If this is real..." His gaze fell on the skin again.
"This is the biggest project the association has seen in the past few decades." The World Devourer Giants are one of the most famous races.
But it’s not just about the giants themselves, if it was a normal or even a Fallen World Devourer Giant, his reaction would not have been this intense.
However, the corpse here belongs to the most powerful World Devourer Giant, the leader of their entire race, and an Unholy!
Magnus just nodded calmly, this time even he did not object, and then added.
"It’s not mine, it belongs to that young man." And he pointed at Lian.
The chairman finally noticed Lian and Kain’s presence, his gaze moved over the two and finally settled on Lian, for some reason he felt this boy’s face was familiar.
As if he had seen him somewhere before.
"You are the owner of this corpse?"
"Yes." Lian answered calmly.
Roland asked.
"Hmm, your face looks very familiar to me, your name?"
"Lian."
"Family name?"
"Vorhelm." Lian answered without the slightest change in his expression.
Roland’s eyes widened slightly for a moment, he now understood why this boy’s face was familiar.
This was the same young Vorhelm who had been on the headlines of all the country’s news just a week ago.
Magnus also looked at Lian in surprise.
"Vorhelm...?"
Both were silent for a few seconds.
Lian braced himself inside, as far as he knew, the President did not have a good relationship with the Vorhelm clan.
The association’s leaders also had close ties with the government’s decision-making circle, and it was natural for him to think that they would now find an excuse to reject his request.
But... contrary to all his expectations... Roland suddenly laughed, and not a fake laugh, but a real and heartfelt one.
"Haha..." He placed his hand on Lian’s shoulder.
"So this corpse belongs to our young friend?" His smile was still on his face.
"I guess without the Titan Hammer, you can’t do anything with this corpse, right Magnus?"
"That’s right, I was planning to contact you to get the hammer." Magnus answered.
"No problem, the association will help you and is ready to give the hammer."
This time it was Lian’s turn to be surprised, he just looked at the chairman for a few moments, he really did not expect such a reaction, and then added.
"I didn’t expect you to agree so quickly."
Roland answered without any hesitation.
"The reason is very simple, making anything from such raw material is an honor for the association itself, no craftsman would miss such an opportunity." Then his gaze became more serious.
"The second reason is that in these past few days, you have done a great service to this country, the news of the border city’s rescue is still being talked about among the people."
He started counting one by one.
"You defended the Base, you saved hundreds of awakened ones, and more importantly..." His gaze locked directly into Lian’s eyes.
"You captured alive the first registered native human in this new realm."
"This is the least we can do for you."
"I didn’t expect the news to reach you so quickly." Lian said after listening, it seemed news reaches high-level people very quickly.
But this was also something that was expected, and it seemed the matter had reached a point where the head of the Blacksmiths’ Association also wanted to have a good relationship with him.
’Or could it be because of Kael?’ Of course, there was another possibility.
Magnus, who had been silently listening until then, finally could not hide his surprise.
"Wait... this boy... did all that?"
Roland laughed.
"It seems you really have been cut off from the world."
"My job is blacksmithing, not following the news." Magnus shrugged.
The chairman smiled and briefly summarized the events of the past few days.

About the border city operation, about the discovery of the ruin, about capturing the first native human, about the counterattack that broke the siege, and about Lian’s stand against the Abyssal River Drake until reinforcements arrived.
The more he went on... Magnus’s eyes opened wider.
When the talk ended, the old man just looked at Lian for a few seconds.
"Not bad, I knew you were definitely not an ordinary person, but not to this extent." He then said slowly.
"Magnus, the Titan’s Forge Hammer will be in your hands by tomorrow."
"Okay." The old man nodded calmly.
The chairman turned to Lian this time, his face no longer held a smile, it had become completely serious.
"But before starting the construction, there is something you should know." He pointed at the massive corpse of the World Devourer Giant.

"Such an armor is only made once, mistakes can happen, and if we make a mistake, there will be no second chance, and the entire corpse’s value will be lost, as you know, blacksmithing science is not 100 percent and error-free."
"So are you sure that instead of selling it, you want to make an armor from it?"

sentences.text: The sound of calm footsteps echoed in the corridor outside the workshop.
A few seconds later, the heavy iron door opened and an elderly man entered.
His silver hair was carefully combed back, and he wore simple gray clothes; clothes that at first glance were no different from an ordinary craftsman’s attire.
But right at that moment, all the apprentices inside the workshop immediately stopped working and all bowed respectfully.
Even a few master craftsmen who were busy making equipment also put down their hammers.
"Chairman."
The atmosphere of the workshop suddenly changed completely.
Without anyone introducing him, Lian and Kain guessed that this man must be the same person the apprentice had been talking about.
Chairman Roland Ashcroft.

The head of the country’s Blacksmiths’ Association, one of the most influential men in the country, he had no direct combat power, but the biggest guilds and awakened ones of the country were all indebted to him and treated him with respect.
Roland gave a quick look around and went straight toward Magnus.
"Magnus, I came about the President’s order, I heard you finally decided to set a time for making that armor."
"Whenever its turn comes, I will make it, not sooner." Magnus sneered with impatience and then added.
"Making the armor he requested is not easy, an armor that can conduct the lightning element’s currents in the smoothest way?
It takes time and needs a lot of materials."
"Why does he even want such an armor?
He himself doesn’t use the lightning element."
Suddenly, Lian’s eyebrows rose slightly, such an armor would be perfect for a lightning mage... and the President himself was not a lightning mage.
But... suddenly Kael’s face appeared in his mind... could it be for his secret son?
A gift?
Roland just gave a faint smile, it was clear that he was used to this old man’s strange temper, but right when he was about to speak again...
His gaze fixed on the massive skin that was on the anvil, his sentence remained half-finished, and a strange silence fell over the workshop.
He calmly stepped forward, then another step, and for a few moments just stared at the skin’s black surface.
He placed his hand gently on it, his eyebrows furrowed, and under his breath, so quietly that only those nearby could hear, he whispered.
"...Where did you find this?"
Without waiting for an answer, he opened a small leather bag from his belt.
He took out several strange tools from inside it, a crystal lens, a silver pen covered with runes, and a metal plate with mana lines carved on it.
He activated the tools one by one, blue and golden lights moved across the skin’s surface.
The runes lit up one after another, for several full minutes no sound was heard, even the apprentices did not dare to breathe loudly.
In the end, Roland calmly put the tools aside, his eyes still on the skin.
"There is no mistake..." He took a deep breath.
"The leader of the World Devourer Giants race.
Those few words were enough for silence to weigh heavily on the workshop again.
Even the chairman himself did not say anything for a few moments, as if his mind was still processing what he had seen, and then he calmly turned toward Magnus.
"How did you find this?
Do you want to make something with it?
If this is real..." His gaze fell on the skin again.
"This is the biggest project the association has seen in the past few decades." The World Devourer Giants are one of the most famous races.
But it’s not just about the giants themselves, if it was a normal or even a Fallen World Devourer Giant, his reaction would not have been this intense.
However, the corpse here belongs to the most powerful World Devourer Giant, the leader of their entire race, and an Unholy!
Magnus just nodded calmly, this time even he did not object, and then added.
"It’s not mine, it belongs to that young man." And he pointed at Lian.
The chairman finally noticed Lian and Kain’s presence, his gaze moved over the two and finally settled on Lian, for some reason he felt this boy’s face was familiar.
As if he had seen him somewhere before.
"You are the owner of this corpse?"
"Yes." Lian answered calmly.
Roland asked.
"Hmm, your face looks very familiar to me, your name?"
"Lian."
"Family name?"
"Vorhelm." Lian answered without the slightest change in his expression.
Roland’s eyes widened slightly for a moment, he now understood why this boy’s face was familiar.
This was the same young Vorhelm who had been on the headlines of all the country’s news just a week ago.
Magnus also looked at Lian in surprise.
"Vorhelm...?"
Both were silent for a few seconds.
Lian braced himself inside, as far as he knew, the President did not have a good relationship with the Vorhelm clan.
The association’s leaders also had close ties with the government’s decision-making circle, and it was natural for him to think that they would now find an excuse to reject his request.
But... contrary to all his expectations...
Roland suddenly laughed, and not a fake laugh, but a real and heartfelt one.
"Haha..." He placed his hand on Lian’s shoulder.
"So this corpse belongs to our young friend?" His smile was still on his face.
"I guess without the Titan Hammer, you can’t do anything with this corpse, right Magnus?"
"That’s right, I was planning to contact you to get the hammer." Magnus answered.
"No problem, the association will help you and is ready to give the hammer."
This time it was Lian’s turn to be surprised, he just looked at the chairman for a few moments, he really did not expect such a reaction, and then added.
"I didn’t expect you to agree so quickly."
Roland answered without any hesitation.
"The reason is very simple, making anything from such raw material is an honor for the association itself, no craftsman would miss such an opportunity." Then his gaze became more serious.
"The second reason is that in these past few days, you have done a great service to this country, the news of the border city’s rescue is still being talked about among the people."
He started counting one by one.
"You defended the Base, you saved hundreds of awakened ones, and more importantly..." His gaze locked directly into Lian’s eyes.
"You captured alive the first registered native human in this new realm."
"This is the least we can do for you."
"I didn’t expect the news to reach you so quickly." Lian said after listening, it seemed news reaches high-level people very quickly.
But this was also something that was expected, and it seemed the matter had reached a point where the head of the Blacksmiths’ Association also wanted to have a good relationship with him.
’Or could it be because of Kael?’ Of course, there was another possibility.
Magnus, who had been silently listening until then, finally could not hide his surprise.
"Wait... this boy... did all that?"
Roland laughed.

chapters.title: Chapter 170: Making Some Money
paragraphs: A few minutes after the chairman left, the atmosphere of the workshop became calm again.

The only sound that could be heard was the regular striking of the apprentices’ hammers on the anvils around them, but in a corner of the workshop, Magnus no longer paid any attention to those sounds.
All his focus was on the massive skin of the World Devourer Giant, the old man calmly knelt down and once again ran his rough palm over the black and rough surface of the skin.

Sometimes he would tap a part of its fibers with his finger, sometimes he would check the thickness of the layers with his fingernail, and sometimes he would whisper under his breath about different methods of shaping and connecting the armor plates.
As if from this very moment, in his mind, he was already building the armor that might become the greatest work of his entire life.
Lian watched him for a few moments, despite the possibility of failure, he had still agreed to use this monster’s corpse to make an armor.
After all, that was the whole reason he had taken this corpse.
And finally, he raised the question that had been on his mind from the beginning.
"How much will it cost to make?"
Magnus took his gaze off the skin, a short and faint smile settled on his lips, and he answered.
"I can’t answer that question right now."
"Why?" Lian was a little surprised, he thought that like monster corpse prices, there were fixed prices for equipment, or at least a range would be given.
He needed to be sure if he had the money or not, because it could be a billion dollars and he did not have that kind of money.
The old man wiped his hands on his leather apron and said calmly.
"Because I don’t know either, this is the first time I’m going to make an Ancient rank armor from the corpse of an Unholy World Devourer Giant."
"I don’t know how many times I’ll have to change the auxiliary materials, I don’t know how many tools will be destroyed during the work, I don’t even know exactly how long it will take."
His gaze fixed on the skin again.
"When the armor is ready... we’ll talk about the cost then."
"For now, the important thing is to start making it, the rest can be solved later."
"How long will it take now that we no longer need to get permission for the hammer?" Lian did not say more, but he still wanted the armor soon.
"I can’t give you an exact time, but probably one or two weeks."
"Then I leave everything to you." He just nodded, one or two weeks was not a long time.
Magnus smiled.
"I won’t disappoint you, don’t worry, anyway I need some information to make the armor fit you properly." And then he ordered his apprentice to take all of Lian’s measurements.
The apprentice took all his measurements within a few minutes, and then asked questions about his fighting style, the type of battles he engages in, the elements he uses in battles, and his skills.
All of this was for personalizing the armor, they wanted to make an armor in which the user would not only feel safe but also comfortable.
A few minutes later... Lian and Kain left the Blacksmiths’ Association building.
The sun was slowly tilting toward the horizon, and its orange light was shining on the cobblestone streets of the capital.
Kain stretched his arms above his head and gave his body a good stretch.
"Well... what now?"
"The National Awakened Center, we need to examine the treasures we brought from the ruin and sell them."
The massive building of the National Awakened Center was not far from them, and they arrived in ten minutes by taxi, it was still busy even at this hour.
Without wasting time, they went to the equipment trading section.
Upon entering, Lian placed his Silver VIP card on the device, a green light turned on, and the staff member behind the counter immediately stood up.
"Mr. Vorhelm, welcome, please come this way."
Instead of standing in the long line of customers, the two were directly led to a private assessment room.
A few minutes later... Lian took out the ruin’s treasures one by one from his storage space.
The senior expert, a man about fifty years old with thin glasses, frowned after seeing the first item.
"All of these... came from one ruin?"
"Yes." Lian just nodded.
The expert took a deep breath.
"Let’s begin." And the first item was placed on the table.
[ Scroll of Mana Compression ]
[ Rank: B ]
The expert almost excitedly opened the scroll.
"Incredible... it’s still completely intact." Very often, treasures remaining in ruins are damaged and need repair.
That is why most items and treasures obtained that are damaged are bought and sold at lower prices.
He carefully examined the runes on it.
"After learning it, it increases mana control and mana recovery speed, its intact version is almost impossible to find nowadays, we are willing to buy it for $500,000."
"I’ll keep this." Lian said without thinking, this one’s value was so significant that it really could not be sold.
"Are you sure? We are even willing to offer up to one million dollars."
"I’m sure, it’s not for sale."
The expert sighed and just set it aside.
The second item... a small metal cube whose surface was covered with spatial runes.
[ Ancient Spatial Cube ]
[ Rank: B ]
The expert examined it from various angles several times.
"It seems to be one of the technological pieces of the Ruined Realm’s civilizations."
"If I’m guessing correctly, maybe it can be used to upgrade storage space or even build new spatial equipment."

"This is really valuable, for awakened ones of our world, it has no value because we automatically have Storage Space, but imagine if we didn’t have that ability... then this item would be a huge treasure."
"I’ll sell this one, as you said, it’s worthless to us." Lian looked at it and said.
The third item... a golden-colored crystal with a gentle halo of light flowing around it.
[ Halo Crystal ]
[ Rank: C ]
The expert picked it up with respect, and after a few seconds of examination, he said.
"It’s almost unparalleled for making healing equipment, it’s more useful for healers."
"I’ll sell this too." Lian said briefly, he was not a healer for such a thing to be useful to him.
The fourth item...
[ Scripture of Radiance ]
[ Rank: C ]
A thick book whose pages were not made of ordinary paper, but of a white and resistant material.
The expert almost carefully turned its pages.
"Interesting, a book about runes related to light and illumination... universities and research centers will compete to obtain it."
"I’ll sell this too."
The fifth item...
[ Saint’s Prayer Bell ]
[ Rank: B ]
A small bell of white gold, the expert gently shook it, a soft resonance echoed in the room, and for a moment a sacred energy spread in the air, clearly it had healing applications.
But a large part of its function had been lost and weakened, if it was still at its peak, Lian would not have been willing to sell it at all.
But now it did not even have a hundredth of its peak power, and he decided to sell it.
The sixth item...
[ Dawnglass Shards ]
[ Rank: B ]
Transparent crystal pieces with golden light flowing inside them.
"Valuable raw materials for making equipment, but equipment more based on powers related to light and illumination, useful for mages who use light power."
"I’ll sell this too."
The seventh item...
[ Broken Light Altar Fragment ]
[ Rank: C ]
A piece of the main altar of the first temple, it had no magical use, although it was made with magic and valuable materials, but it was more of an ancient artifact.
The expert just stared at it for a few seconds.
"The National Museum would probably be willing to buy it, but it has no other value."
"Add this to the list of sold items too."
The last item...
[ Holy Sunsteel Ingots ×3 ]
[ Rank: B ]
Three golden-colored ingots that had a gentle glow even without mana infusion.
The expert said excitedly.
"The value of these is extremely high, this is the first time I’m seeing such metal, it’s as if they have been blessed by light itself, they can be used very well in making weapons."
"It can give weapons the attribute of light power."
"Sell these too." Lian smiled.
Nearly an hour later... all assessments were finished, and the expert activated the holographic screen on the table.
The numbers appeared one after another, finally.
Total Estimated Value: $3,084,000
Kain unconsciously let out a short whistle.
"I really didn’t think they would be worth this much."
The expert smiled.
"If you hold a private auction yourself, they would probably sell for even more."
After the sale procedures were completed... Lian turned to Kain.
"Half the money for you."
"No." Kain almost without hesitation shook his head.
"Why?"
"I obtained something from that ruin that is worth more than all of this combined." He continued.
"Besides, you were the one who found those treasures, if it weren’t for you... I would have died there, that’s enough for me."
Lian looked at his friend for a few seconds, then did not insist further.
"Okay."
When both left the National Awakened Center building, suddenly a message was sent to both of their phones.
[ Academy Announcement ]
[ The first Special Area discovered by the Federation has officially become available ]
[ Special Area Exploration Slots Distribution Begins Tomorrow ]
"So Seraphina was right, the distribution really starts tomorrow, how many slots do you think there are?" Kain said in surprise.
Lian stared at the screen without a word, Special areas... the same areas he had only heard the name of until today.

chapters.title: Chapter 171: The Special Areas
paragraphs: The next morning... students were returning from the Ruined Realm one by one, and the stone corridors, training grounds, and educational buildings were once again full of activity.
However, unlike normal days, almost no one was talking about classes or exams.
All the discussions revolved around one topic: the Base battle.
"Did you hear a level thirty-five Fallen had attacked?"
"They say the monster army was destroyed."
"Commander Valerian, the commander of Base #5, personally entered the battle too."
"I heard three commanders were killed there."
"No, I heard a student was the reason the base didn’t fall."
Every few meters, a different version of the story was heard.
Some were exaggerating, some were mixing truth with rumors, and some were just guessing.
But many people knew the full truth of that battle, at the time it happened, a lot of people were there, whether on the defensive lines or hiding.
Lian and Kain left the dormitory building and moved toward the academy’s main building.
A few minutes later, several familiar faces approached from the other side of the courtyard. Seraphina was the first to see them, and a small smile settled on her lips.
"Finally we see each other again, of course, sooner than I thought."
"I thought the student council was responsible for distributing the quotas, what are you doing here?" Kain looked at her and asked in surprise.
"Well, normally I thought so too, but the academy made the decision about the quotas, and apparently they didn’t need us."
"Oh? So do you know who was chosen?" Lian asked curiously.
"No, but I’m sure you were chosen."
Kain also nodded, he too was sure his friend had definitely been chosen.
"Hey Lian." Suddenly Cassian, Selina, Liana, and Marcus also approached.
After a few days of missions and rest, everyone was together again.
"I missed you so much." Liana ran toward him and clung to him, grabbing his arm.
Seeing this scene, Seraphina’s eyes turned cold, and she forcefully inserted herself between them and separated them.
"Any kind of intimate touching between students is strictly forbidden!" She then warned.
"Since when?" Liana looked up and asked with hidden sarcasm and hostility.
"From now!" Seraphina said firmly.
"Still alive? I heard you made a lot of noise in the base too, just like in the border city." Seeing the atmosphere and to change it, Marcus gave Lian’s shoulder a light punch with a laugh.
"By force." Lian laughed and then added.
"What’s up? I didn’t see any of you inside the base, except for Cassian of course." He looked at them, Cassian had helped a lot during the Quest.
But there was no news from Marcus, Selina, or Liana.
"Well, about us..." Liana glanced and explained.
During the conversation, it became clear that Selina, Liana, and Marcus were not inside the Ruined Realm at all during the Base siege.
They had returned to the academy to rest exactly one day before the battle started.
For this reason, none of them had participated in the emergency Quest, and naturally, they had not received its reward either.
But Cassian had stayed inside the base until the last moment.
He had not only participated in the battle but had also completed the Quest along with the other defenders and had received that extra Level.
"I see, so you must have made good progress to come out for rest so soon." Lian nodded.
"Of course! Both of us reached level 15." Liana added.
"I also reached level 16... my progress has been a bit slow." Marcus sighed, he should have been at least at Cassian’s level by now.
But unfortunately, as a tank, hunting alone is not easy for him, and he hadn’t found a good group, while Cassian is in the academy’s strongest group, the student council group.
And Liana and Selina always hunt together and don’t need a group.
"I also reached level 18, I should be able to reach my first evolution soon." Cassian then added.

"Where is Claire?" Liana then asked.
"She still hasn’t returned from leave." Cassian answered, and everyone sighed, that girl still hadn’t been able to get over those events.

All first and second-year students moved toward the conference building, the massive conference hall filled up within a few minutes.
A quiet murmur flowed through the space.

"All of you saw yesterday’s academy announcement."
Behind him, a massive holographic screen lit up, showing a limited map of the Ruined Realm, with explored points and several golden points shining on the map.
Aldric continued.
"Many of you imagine that Special Areas are just more dangerous regions of the Ruined Realm." He paused briefly.
"But the truth... is completely different.
The image changed.
On the map, spatial cracks appeared; as if part of the space had been torn open and connected to another world.
"A Special Area is actually... a small world inside the Ruined Realm itself."
A quiet murmur spread among the students, most of them were already aware of this... did they really need to be explained again?
Aldric explained.
"Each of these small worlds has its own rules."
"Independent ecosystems, unique monster species, dungeons and ruins that only exist inside that world, and treasures that cannot be found anywhere else."
He changed the image again.

"These areas are extremely rare, unlike Hidden Areas which are part of the Ruined Realm itself and are found more frequently, that is why whenever one of these areas is discovered... the federation immediately takes full control of it."
No country was willing to miss such an opportunity.
"Normally, it depends on the danger level of the Special Area, and based on that, quotas are given either only to powerful awakened ones or to newcomers." Aldric took a deep breath.
"Fortunately, you are lucky, this one’s danger level was not that high, and our academy’s quota has been announced as ten people."
Then he announced the names one by one.
"First... Lian Vorhelm."
Many looks turned toward Lian, no one objected... with all his achievements, this was a given.
Then the next names were announced, and coincidentally, most of them were Lian’s friends... Seraphina, Cassian, Liana, Selina, Marcus, and then...
Rindo Valcrest... the head of the student council, someone all students knew and was recognized as the current strongest student of the academy.
Nathan Crowe, another member of the student council and a third-year student.
And finally, Roderick Ashen... a brief silence followed, and then... Elena.
The murmurs rose again, and Kain unconsciously looked toward Lian, Elena... his former fiancée.
And as he expected, Lian’s face did not change even slightly.
No frown, no smile, not even a pause, he just calmly looked at Professor Aldric; as if that name no longer held any place in his mind.
Kain stared at his friend for a few seconds.
In truth... Lian had not had any contact with Roderick or Elena for a long time, there was no direct conflict between them.
But... Roderick was the type of person who always needed to prove his superiority.
He almost openly referred to himself throughout the academy as the future king of the academy and one of the most powerful awakened ones of the new generation.
And now... a student whose name had spread across the entire academy and the capital in the past few days... was going to enter the most important mission of the year alongside him.
"With Roderick’s personality... I doubt this will end without trouble..." Kain thought quietly to himself.
At that same moment, Professor Aldric spoke his final words.
"From today... you are the academy’s representatives in the Special Area, and I hope that by next week, you will be ready for one of the most difficult missions you have experienced so far."

chapters.title: Chapter 172: A New Team
paragraphs: After the end of Professor Aldric’s speech, a quiet murmur spread throughout the conference hall.
Students rose from their seats one by one, and as they moved toward the exit, almost everyone was talking about one topic.
The Special Area.
Some spoke with envy about the ten people who had been selected, everyone wished they could enter such a place, and now all ten quotas had been distributed and none of them had been chosen.
Although along with envy, there was also understanding, they knew all the people who had been selected deserved to be selected and could not complain about this matter.
Others guessed what treasures might be hidden in that unknown world and discussed with their friends how much those ten people would progress after returning.
Or even how many quotas the academies and guilds from other countries and different parts of the world had received.
Some were only talking about the Base battle and whether the rumors they had heard these past few days were true or not.
In the meantime, Professor Aldric came back to the podium and said with a calm but firm voice.
"The eight people who are currently inside the academy... please stay here for a few minutes."
A new murmur spread through the hall.
"Eight people?"
"Wasn’t the quota ten people?"
"So where are the other two?"
But no one had an answer, slowly the hall emptied, and only a few people remained among the wide seats.
Kain calmly stood up and was ready to leave, he looked at Lian and gave a faint smile.
"Well, from here on, I’m not with you anymore, I think we should part ways here."
Lian didn’t say anything, he just placed his hand on his friend’s shoulder, and that brief gesture was enough for Kain, and he continued.
"I’m going to the dormitory, I’ll wait for you when the meeting is over."
Lian nodded in confirmation, Kain wasn’t upset at all that he hadn’t been selected, only a few days had passed since his class had evolved to four stars.
He had no fame, no major achievement registered, and no one knew him at the level of the academy’s top students.
It was natural that his name wouldn’t be seen among the limited quotas of the Special Area, but unlike before... this didn’t disappoint him.
Instead, it created more motivation inside him, he now knew he had chosen the right path.
Maybe he hadn’t been selected this time... but next time, he himself would stand alongside the country’s best students, and at that time he would definitely shine.
He just shouldn’t be lazy and should take advantage of all opportunities in his friends’ absence to progress.
With this thought, he smiled, waved to everyone, and left the hall.
A few seconds of silence passed among the group, and then Marcus locked his hands behind his back and said with his usual tone.
"It seems our group is going to come together again." It hadn’t been long since they had separated, and again they were going to enter a Special Area together as a group.
Could it be fate?
"Almost, just this time we have three new members." Cassian gave a short laugh.
His gaze moved respectively to Seraphina, the head of the student council, and the empty seat next to them.
"And of course Nathan when he returns."
"As long as they don’t cause trouble, I have no problem." Liana shrugged.
"I doubt the head and I, the vice head of the student council, are the type of people who cause trouble." Seraphina immediately answered with her usual calm smile.
"I’m still not sure..." Liana whispered under her breath.
Seraphina’s smile didn’t change, but the coldness in the two girls’ gazes was completely obvious, neither of them even tried to hide the hidden hostility between them.
Selina quietly sighed.
Marcus just moved his gaze between the two and preferred to say nothing, intervening in a battle between two ladies was very dangerous and could end in his death.
Cassian also seemed completely unused to such an atmosphere and felt a little awkward, and just pretended to be indifferent.
Only Lian truly didn’t care, as if the conflict between these girls wasn’t because of him at all.
Until that moment, the student council president had been standing a little further away, watching their conversation without interfering.
Finally, he calmly came toward them, he was tall, his neat black hair matched the student council’s formal uniform.
His calm gray eyes revealed no emotion, his posture showed years of training.
No pride or arrogance could be seen in his behavior, but at the same time, the way he walked made those around him unconsciously make way for him.
When he stood in front of the group, he gave a short smile.
"I think first I should introduce myself." And he extended his hand.
"Rindo Valcrest, head of the student council."
Cassian stepped aside with respect.
He was one of the most serious candidates to succeed Rindo after his graduation.
But for now, he still worked as a member of the council directly under his supervision.
Rindo gave a brief look at Cassian and nodded, the two knew each other and there was no need to waste time, and then his gaze fixed on Lian.
"We’ve seen each other before, but this is the first time we have a chance to talk properly." Rindo looked directly into Lian’s eyes.
"Before anything else, I wanted to thank you for what you did for the Base."
"You saved many people’s lives and did a great service to the country."
"You even risked your own life without hesitation."
The atmosphere around fell silent for a moment, being praised by the current strongest student of the academy was a great honor, but not for Lian... he had been praised by much bigger people.
And without any change in his expression, he answered.
"I just tried to do my duty." In fact, it was all his fault that those events had happened at all, but he couldn’t say that, right?
Rindo gave a very small smile.
"There aren’t many students who even know what their duty to their country is."
This sentence made the others lower their heads, especially Liana, Selina, and Marcus who hadn’t been present in the base defense operation.
"He’s not one of those arrogant and stiff leaders, but I feel he’s serious and tough." A few seconds later, Marcus quietly approached Selina and said under his breath.
"Yeah, but it’s exactly what I expected." Selina also nodded very quietly.

Then they also shook hands with the student council president one by one and got to know each other, since they were all more or less the most famous faces of the current academy, they actually knew each other to some extent, so the introduction process wasn’t that long.
"When will the other members arrive?" A few moments later, Lian raised another question.
"Nathan will probably return in a few hours." Rindo answered, but then paused.
"About the last two, Roderick and Elena, honestly I have no information."
Everyone looked at him, Roderick and Elena had gained a lot of fame in their early days at the academy, but it had been a while since there was any news of them, and their fame was gradually fading.
"Those two are still inside the Ruined Realm, I don’t know if the quota notification has reached them or not, and I don’t even know if they intend to return or not."
"Could someone really miss the quota to enter a Special Area?" Liana said quietly, in her view, only fools would do such a thing.
"Unless they found something more valuable." Marcus frowned.
No one answered, this possibility, however unlikely, was not impossible.
"A question." Then Selina took over the discussion.
"As the student council president, do you know anything about the Special Area? For example, what kind of place is it? What monsters are there? Or even what its name is?"
Everyone waited for an answer, but Rindo just gave a bitter smile.
"Honestly, I know about as much as you do, the federation has declared all information about this area classified."
"For now, we have to wait for Professor Aldric’s explanations."
At that same moment... the large door of the hall opened again, the sound of familiar footsteps echoed in the silent space of the hall.
Everyone turned around at the same time, Professor Aldric entered with his usual calmness, without saying even a single word, he stood in front of the eight selected students.
His gaze calmly passed over each of them, a few seconds of silence remained, and then he said with a quiet voice.
"Now let’s talk about the first Special Area you are going to experience in your lives."
And at that same moment, the hall doors behind him quietly closed.

chapters.title: Chapter 173: Before the Journey
paragraphs: The doors of the conference hall closed quietly.
The last students had also left the hall, and now only eight selected students were sitting in silence on their seats.
Professor Aldric looked at them for a few moments without speaking.
His gaze calmly passed over each of them; Lian, Seraphina, Cassian, Liana, Selina, Marcus, Rindo, and Nathan’s empty seat.
The best current students of the academy had gathered here, and talents who could be said to definitely play a big role in the future of the country and maybe the world.
Then he quietly took a deep breath.
"Well... from this moment, the information you are about to hear, must not be shared outside this room."
The atmosphere of the hall immediately became more serious, Aldric raised his hand and a large hologram formed behind him.
First an image of the Ruined Realm appeared, a moment later, several golden cracks lit up in different parts of the map.
"You probably all think that a Special Area is just a more dangerous region of the Ruined Realm." He paused for a few seconds.
"But that is a wrong assumption." The image changed again, this time a spatial crack was displayed that connected to a completely different world.
Forests with unknown colors, mountains floating in the sky, lakes from which blue light rose to the sky.
"A Special Area..."
"Is actually a small world, a world that is located inside the Ruined Realm itself." Aldric continued.
"The rules inside that world might be completely different from the rules of the Ruined Realm."
"The flow of time might be slower or faster, the mana density might be several times higher or even lower than normal."
"Some skills might work weaker there, some skills, on the contrary, might gain several times more power."
He displayed another image, species of plants and metals that no one in the hall had ever seen.
"The monsters of that world only live there, the plants, metals, raw materials, and even the mana resources there are unique."
"Some ancient civilizations only existed inside Special Areas and no trace of them has been found in the Ruined Realm."
His gaze turned on everyone and Aldric said in conclusion.
"If we consider the Ruined Realm as a large world, Special Areas are small worlds that are attached to that continent."
These were explanations he had given before, but he felt the need to explain again, Special Areas are very rare, and most of the time when one is found, its danger level is very high.
So high that only awakened ones above level 40 receive permission to enter.
Although they now had a Special Area that new awakened ones had received the right to enter.
"If you have any questions, ask."
The first person to raise her hand was Selina.
"If we die inside, do we really die? Or are there different rules?"
"Yes, like anywhere else, death inside a Special Area... is real death." Aldric answered without pausing.
Selina said nothing more, but was somewhat disappointed, she had expected that maybe death in such a place was not really real death.
"Can we leave whenever we want?" This time Marcus asked.
Everyone’s ears perked up, this was a very important question directly related to the importance of their decisions and thought process.
Aldric nodded calmly.
"If you find the exit gate... yes, but if you can’t, you have to stay inside that world until the mission ends."
"Sometimes after entering a Special Area, the system issues a Quest, in such conditions, until the Quest is completed, no exit route will be activated."
"Sometimes there is no Quest at all, and in that case, the only way out... is to find the key to that world.
"Every Special Area has at least one exit key, but, finding it is not always simple, and obtaining it is usually even harder."
"Among you, there is one person who is very good at finding keys, you can ask for his help."

Everyone’s gaze fell on Lian, they knew that the professor meant him, Lian was the only awakened one among them who had been summoned as one of the 25,000 victims and had managed to escape by finding a key.
And he clearly had a lot of knowledge in this area, which made them somewhat relieved.
But Lian, seeing how they were relieved, gave a bitter smile, he knew where keys could be found in the Ruined Realm.
But he had no idea about finding keys in Special Areas, information about such places is very limited.
And this made him ask himself whether his ability to enter and exit the Ruined Realm would work there? Could he enter or leave whenever he wanted?
If it worked, then he had no need to worry.
"Could there be native humans living inside?" Liana asked this time.
Aldric was silent for a few seconds.
"It is possible, especially after the discovery and capture of the first native humans in the current realm."
This sentence made everyone look at Lian again for a moment, the news of capturing a native human had spread almost throughout the entire academy.
But no one except the commanders knew more details about it, and the person who had captured that human was sitting next to them.
"But it’s not just humans, there might be other intelligent species living inside that world too."
"Species that are neither human nor monster, but have civilization, have culture, have emotions, and live like us."
This did not surprise them because they were fully aware of the existence of intelligent species, species that currently ruled the Heavenly Realm.
And their numbers are also very significant, fairies, elves, dwarves, and various other spiritual and mythical creatures like phoenixes.
And this made Liana’s face light up, because if there was an intelligent species there, she could obtain one of them as her summon.
"What is the main goal of this mission?" Lian asked quietly, changing the atmosphere a little, he knew that the federation would not just give them permission to enter such a place for no reason.
Aldric gave a small smile.
"For the federation? Or for you?"
"For the federation, exploration, information gathering, discovering new technologies, and obtaining anything that can increase humanity’s power."
He walked a few steps in the hall.
"But for you, this is an opportunity for progress, an opportunity to become stronger, an opportunity to surpass your limits." His gaze became more serious.
"All of you need to know one truth, we are at war with monsters, and we have conflicts and tensions with the Heavenly Realm, and we will definitely fight the Heavenly Realm in the future."
A few people unconsciously frowned, and hatred appeared in their eyes... the Heavenly Realm... an unknown world that wanted to colonize their world.

Lian noticed the hatred in their faces and chuckled inside, he knew the truth about the Heavenly Realm because he is a Vorhelm, he knows that it is they who attacked and want to colonize the Heavenly Realm.
But all the people do not know this truth, the federation and governments have published false narratives that the Heavenly Realm first attacked their world and is trying to colonize them.
"We are quite sure that this is the last Ruined Realm, the existing evidence confirms this, so we must use every single opportunity that exists inside it."
"Become stronger and cleanse the Ruined Realm so that one day we can free both our own world and the Heavenly Realm."
No one said anything, but determination could be seen in their eyes, and Liana asked again.
"What about those other two, Roderick and Elena, are they coming?"
"Official notifications have been sent to both, but the final decision is theirs, if they don’t come, their quotas will be lost and they will miss the entry opportunity." Aldric answered.
Marcus frowned.
"Is it possible that someone would miss such an opportunity? Where are they now?"
Aldric just remained silent, neither confirming nor denying, and this silence created more questions in everyone’s minds.
A moment later, the map image changed again, a point lit up in the northwest.
Base #9
A few people were surprised, Base number nine, which was very far from their Base, and the professor explained.
"The Special Area entrance has been discovered within Base number nine’s range, to get there, you will need to travel for about a week inside the Ruined Realm."
"A week?" Selina said in surprise.
Aldric nodded.
Inside the Ruined Realm, there is no direct transfer between bases, the intense mana interference makes long-range portals completely unstable.
For this reason, all transportation is done with military caravans.
And unfortunately, for this reason, they needed to be on the road for a week.
"For all of you, this will be your first real journey between different bases."
"Is the route safe?" Rindo asked.
Aldric smiled.
"If you had asked me this question three days ago, my answer would definitely have been no." Then he gave a brief look at Lian.
"But now the situation is different." He lit up three areas on the map.
Ironfang Ravagers.
Thunder Spine Serpents.
Ironhorn Marsh Drakes.
"The destruction of these three races has opened the main routes for the first time, the caravan can move almost without major conflicts."
"This is considered one of the country’s greatest recent achievements."
"Of course, don’t think the route is completely safe, the Ruined Realm is never safe." He displayed a few more images.
Unknown monsters and even large herds led by an alpha monster.
"Any of these could appear on your path, so don’t lose your caution even for a moment."
"From this moment, you have only one day to prepare, obtain all the equipment you need."
"Potions, weapons, food, camping equipment, anything you think is necessary, you might be outside the base for several weeks."
No one objected, everyone knew that the mission ahead of them was different from all previous missions.
When the meeting ended, students rose from their seats one by one, but right before the hall door opened, Aldric’s voice stopped them again.
"Don’t forget one thing."
Everyone turned back, and the professor stared at the eight students with a serious look.
"A Special Area... is not a place for foolishness."
"As soon as you enter, you might be separated from each other, there is no guarantee that you will appear next to your friends, so from now on, learn how to survive alone."
"I wish you success."
The hall doors quietly opened.
But this time, no one spoke to anyone else while leaving.
It had become clear to everyone that the Special Area was not a normal mission.
But rather an entry into an unknown world; a world where no one could predict what awaited them.

chapters.title: Chapter 174: A Call to Miranda
paragraphs: A few seconds after Professor Aldric left, a strange silence fell over the conference hall.
The seven selected students were still standing in their places, each lost in their own thoughts.
Special Area...
An unknown world about which even the federation did not have much information, this was no longer a normal mission, any wrong decision could cost them their lives.
On the other hand, there could be opportunities so great inside that it could lead to a huge advancement for all of them.
All of them were not far from reaching level 20 and their first evolution, and maybe this was the opportunity they needed to reach it.
Rindo was the first to break the silence, he turned his gaze among the group with his usual calmness and said.
"It seems our work here is done for now, the student council has a lot of coordination to do for this trip."
"From equipment to exit permits, the caravan, and hundreds of other things."

"I also need to prepare the list of required equipment for the group members, if we are missing something, there might not be a chance to make up for it in the middle of the mission." Seraphina also nodded calmly.
Marcus took a deep breath, locked his hands behind his back, and laughed.
"I’m going to buy food first, God knows what we’ll get in there."
Selina placed her hand on her sword’s hilt.
"I need to upgrade my sword, if we’re going to be outside the base for several weeks, I don’t want my equipment to fail in the middle of a fight."
"I also need to buy potions, light clothes, and a few other items, as well as new equipment for my summons." Liana also said.
"The last thing I want is to run out of supplies in the middle of the road."
Cassian also gave a short smile, he also needed to buy new equipment and a number of potions for this long journey.
Each of them definitely had needs that had to be taken care of, everyone knew how long this trip could be and they had to make a lot of preparations.
According to their world’s time, it could be a few weeks, but what if the time inside was different? What if they got stuck inside for months or years? They had to be prepared for such scenarios.
Gradually, everyone said goodbye to each other, and a few minutes later, the large conference hall was almost empty.
Lian also left the main building and headed toward the dormitory.
His mind was occupied with the upcoming journey, and after reaching the dormitory, Lian opened his room door.
"So? How was it?" Kain smiled lazily upon seeing his friend’s return.
Lian did not answer immediately, he stood in front of the window, then opened his storage space.
Before going to the border city, he still had bought some items, especially healing potions, but all those potions were used on Kain in the ruin.
And now, except for a few monster corpses, some of the items obtained from the ruin, and the Devourer egg, there was nothing else in his storage space.
He was almost out of everything, or had nothing at all.

If he was really going to stay inside the Special Area for several weeks, this amount of equipment was not even enough to start, he needed many other things, potions, and any items that could help him in emergencies.
Especially one-time or multi-use healing items, their group had no healer, and if something happened to him, he could only rely on himself for treatment.
A few moments later, he closed the system window and turned back to Kain.
"Let’s go shopping."
"Where?" Kain raised his head.
"The Black Market." Lian answered without a moment’s thought.
On the way out of the academy, Kain looked at him.
"There again? Don’t tell me you fell in love with that place?" They had been to the Black Market once, and he did not expect his friend to want to go there again.
It was not that it was bad, it was just illegal and extremely dangerous, it could actually be considered a crime and get them into trouble.
Why go there when there were plenty of other options?
"The official federation market is not bad, but for what we need, it’s not a suitable choice." Lian said calmly, without slowing his steps.
"Everything there is legal and controlled, prices are higher, buying and selling rules are stricter, and many items are simply not allowed to be sold."
A few moments later, he fixed his gaze on the busy street.
"But on the Black Market, if you have money, you can find almost anything, rare equipment, special potions, forbidden scrolls, information, monster parts."
"You’re explaining it like you grew up in the Black Market, don’t forget I was the one who took you there." Kain said with a laugh.
"Then stop complaining and let’s go."
Half an hour later... both entered one of the oldest neighborhoods of the lower city.
The modern towers of the capital had given way to worn-out buildings, cracked cement walls.
Rusted signs were hanging from the roofs of abandoned shops.
If someone looked from the outside, they would never believe that one of the country’s largest underground markets was hidden behind these forgotten streets.
At the end of the alley... the same abandoned building they had entered last time stood, with two guards at its entrance.
"The first time I came here... I thought my family was going to sell me, the entrance is really scary." Kain laughed upon seeing the building.
When he had first come here with his father, he was only fourteen years old, of course at that time, seeing such a scary place, he had thought that.
"Don’t worry, if they wanted to sell you, I would buy you myself." Lian couldn’t help but laugh.
"I guess thank you?"
The rusty door of the building opened with a harsh sound, a dark and narrow corridor appeared before them, a few steps ahead... a familiar rune was shining on the ground.
Lian and Kain stepped onto it at the same time, mana moved around them, space rippled, and a moment later... everything changed.
When they opened their eyes again, they were standing in the middle of one of the largest pocket dimension markets.
The Black Market.
Dozens of cobblestone streets extended in different directions, thousands of people were coming and going, no one cared about anyone else’s appearance.
Here, only money mattered.
On the right side, a crowd had gathered around a large platform.
"The auction begins!" the auctioneer shouted loudly.
Inside a massive cage, the carcass of a giant sea monster lay, its blue scales still gleaming.
A few streets away... the heart of a Fallen was on display inside a glass container, and several wealthy buyers were bidding for it.
A little further, a man in a black mask was quietly showing secret contracts to customers.
On the other side of the market, a massive shop filled with ancient Artifacts could be seen; swords, armors, rings, and crystals, each worth the price of a mansion.
"It seems even busier than last time." Kain let out a quiet whistle upon seeing the market’s crowd.
"It’s natural, the Ruined Realm appeared some time ago, and items and monster corpses have filled the market again."
While both were passing through the crowd, Kain looked around and then said with a smile.

"If we’re lucky, maybe we’ll see the Lady of the Market again." Of course, he was talking about Miranda, one of the most beautiful but also one of the most terrifying women who ruled the Black Market.
Lian looked at him in surprise.
"Why lucky? Can’t I call her?"
"...Huh?" Kain stopped right there.
Lian very casually took his phone out of his pocket.
"Actually, it’s better to let her know in advance, maybe she can prepare what we need."
Kain just stared at his phone for a few seconds and then asked in disbelief.
"You... have Miranda’s number?"
"Yeah, she gave it to me herself last time." Lian shrugged without making it seem important.
"She just gave you her number...?! Now I’m really jealous!..." Kain whispered under his breath, having that woman’s number was a great honor.
Even his father could not call her directly and had to contact one of her subordinates or deputies if he had business with her.
But this boy had randomly obtained that scary woman’s number.
Lian dialed the number and after a few rings... a familiar woman’s voice was heard from the other end.
"It’s been a while since I heard from you, Mr. Vorhelm."
"Hello, I missed your voice, hearing it made my day, but I need your help." A very small smile settled on Lian’s lips.
Miranda, with a voice that seemed pleased by the compliment, answered without even a moment’s pause.
"Of course, just tell me what you’re looking for."
Lian answered calmly.
"I’m preparing for a long journey, I need the best equipment possible."
A few seconds of silence passed, and then Miranda’s calm and beautiful voice was heard again.
"Then, come straight to the seventh floor of my tower, coincidentally, I have some things that might be suitable for you."
The call ended, and Kain was still staring at Lian with that surprised look, this boy sometimes acts as if he has no feelings at all.
’I didn’t know he had this side too... can he really talk to girls like that?’

Lian put his phone in his pocket and without giving any more explanation, together with Kain, they went to the deeper layer of the market, they had been announced to the guards and were allowed to pass.
A black tower with seven floors, standing tall in the lower layer of the market center.
And an elevator that only a very few people were allowed to use, quietly opened its doors to the two of them.

On the right side, a crowd had gathered around a large platform.
"The auction begins!" the auctioneer shouted loudly.
Inside a massive cage, the carcass of a giant sea monster lay, its blue scales still gleaming.
A few streets away... the heart of a Fallen was on display inside a glass container, and several wealthy buyers were bidding for it.
A little further, a man in a black mask was quietly showing secret contracts to customers.
On the other side of the market, a massive shop filled with ancient Artifacts could be seen; swords, armors, rings, and crystals, each worth the price of a mansion.
"It seems even busier than last time." Kain let out a quiet whistle upon seeing the market’s crowd.
"It’s natural, the Ruined Realm appeared some time ago, and items and monster corpses have filled the market again."
While both were passing through the crowd, Kain looked around and then said with a smile.

"If we’re lucky, maybe we’ll see the Lady of the Market again." Of course, he was talking about Miranda, one of the most beautiful but also one of the most terrifying women who ruled the Black Market.
Lian looked at him in surprise.
"Why lucky?
Can’t I call her?"
"...Huh?" Kain stopped right there.
Lian very casually took his phone out of his pocket.
"Actually, it’s better to let her know in advance, maybe she can prepare what we need."
Kain just stared at his phone for a few seconds and then asked in disbelief.
"You... have Miranda’s number?"
"Yeah, she gave it to me herself last time." Lian shrugged without making it seem important.
"She just gave you her number...?!
Now I’m really jealous!..." Kain whispered under his breath, having that woman’s number was a great honor.
Even his father could not call her directly and had to contact one of her subordinates or deputies if he had business with her.
But this boy had randomly obtained that scary woman’s number.
Lian dialed the number and after a few rings... a familiar woman’s voice was heard from the other end.
"It’s been a while since I heard from you, Mr.
Vorhelm."
"Hello, I missed your voice, hearing it made my day, but I need your help." A very small smile settled on Lian’s lips.
Miranda, with a voice that seemed pleased by the compliment, answered without even a moment’s pause.
"Of course, just tell me what you’re looking for."
Lian answered calmly.
"I’m preparing for a long journey, I need the best equipment possible."
A few seconds of silence passed, and then Miranda’s calm and beautiful voice was heard again.
"Then, come straight to the seventh floor of my tower, coincidentally, I have some things that might be suitable for you."
The call ended, and Kain was still staring at Lian with that surprised look, this boy sometimes acts as if he has no feelings at all.
’I didn’t know he had this side too... can he really talk to girls like that?’

Lian put his phone in his pocket and without giving any more explanation, together with Kain, they went to the deeper layer of the market, they had been announced to the guards and were allowed to pass.
A black tower with seven floors, standing tall in the lower layer of the market center.
And an elevator that only a very few people were allowed to use, quietly opened its doors to the two of them.

chapters.title: Chapter 175: A Meeting with the Lady
paragraphs: The metal door of the elevator closed with a quiet sound.
The runes carved on the inner walls lit up one after another, and a faint blue light filled the entire cabin space.
Unlike normal elevators, this one had no buttons.
Only after the identity was confirmed by someone at the destination, the runes would activate and the transfer path would open.
A few seconds later, the cabin began to move smoothly.
"I never thought I’d be able to go above the third floor." Kain looked around with a curious gaze and said.
This was not just any tower, but a place known in the Black Market among customers and members as an organization.
And each floor had its own uses, more precisely, it was reserved for Lady Miranda’s special clients.
Lian gave a short smile but said nothing, the quiet sound of the elevator system echoed in the enclosed space.
The market floors passed by one after another.
The first to third floors were the public market; where most customers, hunters, and adventurers came and went.
All the buying and selling done here had profits going into Miranda’s pocket.
The fourth floor was for VIP customers; higher-value transactions, rarer equipment, and more security.
The fifth floor was dedicated to private transactions; where many large contracts, buying and selling of level 40+ Fallen monsters, or private auctions took place.
The sixth floor hosted secret auctions; where sometimes only a few people in the entire country were allowed entry.

There, auctions were held where the most powerful people of the continent would send anonymous representatives to participate, and their values were in the billions to even tens and hundreds of billions of dollars.
And finally, the seventh floor, the office of one of the Black Market’s directors, Lady Miranda.
With a quiet sound, the elevator doors opened, the seventh floor, unlike the busy market below, was submerged in absolute silence.
A wide corridor with dark marble floors, crystal chandeliers, and walls covered with old paintings lay before them.
At the end of the corridor, a large door of black wood could be seen.
Two guards in formal attire, without saying even a single word, opened the door for them.
Miranda’s office looked more like a noble’s room than the office of the director of the country’s largest Black Market.
Floor-to-ceiling windows showed a view of the entire market, a massive library housed hundreds of old books.
On one wall, a very large map of the Ruined Realm was installed, with dozens of colored marks on it.
In another corner, several historical weapons were kept inside glass cases; spears, swords, and axes that just from their appearance one could tell belonged to a very distant era.
Miranda stood up from behind her desk upon seeing the two, and a gentle smile settled on her lips.
"You returned sooner than I expected, Mr. Vorhelm."
"Every time I come here... I feel more and more that the Black Market directors are richer than half the country’s ministries." Kain was still looking around with a surprised gaze.
The value of all the collection pieces here was above hundreds of millions and maybe billions of dollars.
Who exactly was this woman? How had she managed to reach such power and position in the Black Market? This was a question that now made him curious too.
"Please, have a seat." Miranda calmly told them, and after a brief greeting, Miranda went straight to the point.
"The news of Base #3 has spread everywhere these past few days." She gave a brief look at Lian.
"Your name has been heard a lot, it seems your journey to the Ruined Realm was not very peaceful, Mr. Vorhelm."
"Trouble always finds a way to get close to the Vorhelms." Lian just gave a faint smile.
Miranda gave him a calm look, but deep in her eyes there was a sign of satisfaction, as if she was truly happy with the decision she had made to establish a friendly relationship with this boy.
"So, what are you looking for this time?"
"I’m preparing for a long journey, I need suitable equipment." Lian said without introduction.
"Destination?" Miranda asked calmly.
"Special Area."
Her gaze became a little more serious, currently only one sample had been discovered, and its information was not hidden from her or the Black Market.
"Mission duration?"
"Not clear."
"Threat level?" The questions being asked, aside from gathering information, were for the lady to understand exactly what she should bring for her client.
"No one knows yet, but it shouldn’t be that high." Lian shrugged.
"So we are talking about something more dangerous than I thought."
She was silent for a few moments and then said calmly.
"A Special Area is different from the Ruined Realm."
"There, you might not find a base for weeks, and most people who enter for the first time run out of supplies, not their lives."
Lian listened carefully.
Miranda continued.
"Lack of food, lack of water, running out of healing equipment, tents, fuel, or even proper clothing, these things kill people more than monsters."
Awakened ones who had not yet passed their first evolution still needed food and water to survive, and even sleep was still necessary.
"So what you need is not weapons, it’s preparedness, and I think I know what would be useful for you." Miranda contacted her staff and ordered that certain equipment be brought immediately.
It did not take long for all the equipment she had ordered to be brought to her office by a number of staff members and placed in front of them.
Several locks were opened one after another, and then she brought out a few small metal boxes and arranged them on the table.
The first box opened, and inside it was a scroll with a golden seal.
"Scroll of Sanctuary."
"Rank: B."
"After activation, it creates a hemispherical Barrier, lasts about one minute, and can withstand a few direct hits from level 30 creatures."
She placed the scroll on the table.
"It’s made to save a life, not for battle, it’s a one-time use and then it’s gone, based on the possible threat level, I doubt you’ll face anything above level 30."
The second box opened, and inside it was a white scroll.
"Scroll of Sacred Restoration."
"Rank: B."
"Bone fractures, organ tears, severe bleeding, it heals all without consuming mana, but only once."
"I want several of these, as many as you can sell." Lian said without hesitation, both this and the previous one were extremely useful.
The third box.
"Scroll of Purification.
"Rank: C."
"Removes poison, curses, and mana corruption and contamination, of course it depends on their power level, but based on the possible threat level, it should be enough."
The fourth box, a transparent crystal with a calm blue light flowing inside it.
"Emergency Mana Crystal."
"If your mana is completely exhausted... this can restore a large amount of mana within seconds, but only once."
Lian also ordered a large number of these, one of the problems he might face was exactly this, but unfortunately, only five were available for purchase.
The previous item also had limited stock, but he only bought two, with his poison resistance, he didn’t need it that much and only bought it to reduce risk.
The last box opened, and inside it was a small cylinder of silver metal.
"Emergency Beacon."
"If you activate it, a column of light rises several kilometers high, both for requesting help and for your teammates to find your location."
Lian stared at it for a few moments, this one was also useful, if the group got separated in the Special Area, such a device could save everyone’s lives.
"I want eight of these." He said calmly.
"Ten?" Miranda raised an eyebrow.
"For all group members, if someone gets lost... at least we can find them." He planned to give one to each of the eight group members.
About those other two members... that’s not his concern, if they need it, they can buy it themselves.
"A good decision."
After that, Lian said.
"I also want a few of the others."
Then he listed them one by one, also ordering a significant amount of monster meat known for its excellent taste.
Along with a device they could use for cooking, an item that took up little space and cooked food quickly.
Miranda took notes without stopping, and when the list was complete, she closed the notebook.
A few moments of silence followed, and then the lady said.
"I also have a free piece of advice, if your destination really is Base #9, it’s better to buy information about that area too, or even a map of the areas explored so far."
"Information?" Kain asked in surprise, was it really necessary? After all, Lian and the others were supposed to enter the Special Area as soon as they arrived there.
Miranda nodded.
"Monsters are dangerous, but ignorance is more dangerous."
She pointed to the large map on the wall.
"Every caravan that returns from that route discovers something new, safe routes, monster territories, rivers, and even monster settlement locations."
"Before entering the Special Area, buy any report you can, sometimes a piece of information is more valuable than a legendary sword."
"And finally, all your orders will be ready within an hour."
Lian nodded.
"Thank you." He thought for a few seconds and then said again.
"I agree with your suggestion, actually, I was going to ask the same thing, about Base #9, do you have any information that might be useful to me?"
