chapters.title: Chapter 176: The Base #9
paragraphs: After hearing Lian’s question, Miranda looked at him in silence for a few moments.
Then she picked up the phone and made a call, asking one of her other employees to bring her a file containing all the information related to Base #9.
It took no more than a few minutes until an employee arrived with a file with the name of one of the Ruined Realm’s bases engraved in golden letters.
After that, the employee respectfully said goodbye and left the place.
On its cover, only a few words could be seen.
Confidential Exploration Report
Base #9
Miranda placed the folder on the table and pushed it toward Lian.
"This is the latest report we have from that area."
She pointed to the date on the report.
"Most of its information is from the past three or four days. The Ruined Realm is still very new, so new information is recorded every day."
Lian opened the folder, the first page was a large map of the area around Base number nine, the number of pages was not large and clearly did not contain much information.
But it was expected, this base was only three weeks old and there shouldn’t be much information.
Miranda explained.
"Base #9 belongs to the North American coalition."
"It wasn’t built by a single country, many countries sent forces to build it, from the very first days, they deployed a large number of military forces and awakened ones there."
In every accessible point of the Ruined Realm, countries, organizations, and coalitions build bases to be able to control those points.
Bases built by coalitions were still open to most awakened ones and had public use, but the question was which countries hosted portals to this base.
For now, only a few weeks had passed and most countries only had portals to one or two bases, but the numbers would gradually increase.
"For this reason, their advancement speed has been higher than most other bases."
On the map, dozens of colored lines extended from the center of the base in various directions.
Each line showed the path of one of the exploration caravans.
Miranda continued.
"So far, they have managed to explore about two thousand kilometers around the base, of course, exploration is different from complete cleansing."
She pointed to a few red routes.
"These routes are still considered unsafe."
"Caravans have passed through them, but the presence of powerful monsters or Alpha Monsters has meant they haven’t been declared safe routes yet."
Lian carefully memorized the routes.
If he was going to take longer journeys after the Special Area mission ended, such information would be very valuable.
Miranda opened the next page, and this time the map was divided into four sections.
She pointed to the north.
"North of the base, the stone forests." Aerial images of the area appeared on the screen.
Massive trees whose trunks looked more like stone pillars than wood.
"The density of plant monsters there is very high, new groups are still being sent for cleansing every few days."
Then she placed her finger on the east of the map, tall mountain ranges covered a large part of the image.
"East, the high mountains, several Alpha Monsters have been seen there, and for this reason, entry to that area is currently forbidden.
Alpha Monsters was a concept used to refer to monsters that led a herd of monsters.
Then it was the west’s turn.
Vast and almost unobstructed plains.
"West, the current safest route, most caravans travel through this route, if you also move toward Base #9, you will probably pass through this route."
Finally, the south, a network of rivers and small lakes covered the entire area.

"That is the territory of aquatic monsters, a large part of the area still remains unknown, every time a team has entered it, they have brought back different reports, and more importantly, the river water is completely poisonous, and the deeper you go, the more deadly the poison becomes."
Miranda turned a few more pages, and this time images of three registered dungeons appeared.
"So far, three confirmed dungeons have been identified around the Base."
First page.
Dungeon #1
Stone Giant Mine
"This dungeon was cleared about a week ago, stone creatures lived inside it, and it is now completely under the control of the North American forces."
Next page.
Dungeon #2
Crimson Spider Nest
An image of a massive cave full of red webs appeared on the screen.
"This one is still being cleansed."
"The final Boss is still alive."
"A new operation is carried out there every few days."
Then the last page.
Dungeon #3
Whispering Catacombs
There was no image, only a few lines of report.
Entry Forbidden
Multiple Casualties
Unknown Invisible Entities Detected
"Just around one base... three dungeons?" Kain unconsciously whistled under his breath, dungeons were not rare, but around their base, there wasn’t even one.
Dungeons could be anywhere and weren’t specific to just one area.
The problem here was that dungeons had conditions, if they failed to clear them more than three times, all the monsters in that dungeon could enter their world and cause a disaster.
Miranda nodded.
"Three identified dungeons, there is no guarantee that these are the only ones, the actual number is probably higher."
After a few minutes of studying, Lian asked the next question.
"How far is the Special Area entrance from the base?"
Miranda zoomed in on the map slightly, and a golden point lit up in the northwest of the base.
"About one hundred and eighty kilometers, completely within Base #9’s controlled range." She paused briefly.
"That is why the federation was able to determine the country quotas without trouble, if the area was still unsafe, no student would be allowed to enter.
Lian nodded calmly, at least until reaching the entrance, there was relative safety.
But after that, everything was unknown.
Lian closed the folder and pushed it back toward Miranda.
"This information is enough for now."
Miranda also took the order notebook and checked the last items, and after a few minutes, the final invoice appeared on the table.
All the equipment, defensive scrolls, healing scrolls, Emergency Beacons, potions, camping equipment, and information reports.
All were recorded in one list, and at the bottom of the page, the final number could be seen.
Total Cost
2,487,000 Dollars
Kain just stared at the number for a few seconds.
"...Just to prepare for a trip?" He really had not expected such an amount, for experienced awakened ones, this amount was not much.
It was an amount that could easily be earned over a few months to a year, but for new awakened ones, it was really a high amount.
Lian, however, without the slightest change in expression, took out his bank card and placed it on the device.
A few seconds later, the payment confirmation sound echoed in the room, the transaction was successful, and a digital receipt appeared on the table.
More than two million dollars for equipment.
"Proper equipment really is terribly expensive." He quietly whispered under his breath.
But almost immediately, he pushed the thought aside.
If even one of those scrolls, one of those Beacons, or even one potion, saved his life or one of the group members’ lives one day... it would be worth more than all that money.
Besides, for him, it wasn’t a lot of money.
Miranda gave a calm smile.
"All your orders are ready, you can take the receipt to the third floor and collect them."
"Thank you." Lian nodded.
"Good luck, if you find anything valuable there and want to sell it, I’m here." Miranda said with her usual calm tone.
A few minutes later, Lian and Kain left Miranda’s office.
The private elevator took them back down from the seventh floor to the third floor, they handed over the receipt, and after receiving their orders, they left the tower.
After passing through the busy market and exiting the pocket dimension, they entered the same abandoned building again, from there they left and headed toward the academy.
The cool evening air hit their faces.
The capital’s sky was slowly taking on orange and purple colors, and the streetlights were turning on one after another.
People were moving on the sidewalks, cars were moving on the city’s wide streets.
Kain locked his hands behind his back and said with a calm smile.
"Tomorrow you finally set off, if I say I don’t really want to come, I’d be lying, so explore that place on my behalf too."
Lian fixed his gaze on the city’s horizon, this time their destination was no longer the Base, their caravan had to head to Base #9.
"For sure."

"East, the high mountains, several Alpha Monsters have been seen there, and for this reason, entry to that area is currently forbidden.
Alpha Monsters was a concept used to refer to monsters that led a herd of monsters.
Then it was the west’s turn.
Vast and almost unobstructed plains.
"West, the current safest route, most caravans travel through this route, if you also move toward Base #9, you will probably pass through this route."
Finally, the south, a network of rivers and small lakes covered the entire area.

"That is the territory of aquatic monsters, a large part of the area still remains unknown, every time a team has entered it, they have brought back different reports, and more importantly, the river water is completely poisonous, and the deeper you go, the more deadly the poison becomes."
Miranda turned a few more pages, and this time images of three registered dungeons appeared.
"So far, three confirmed dungeons have been identified around the Base."
First page.
Dungeon #1
Stone Giant Mine
"This dungeon was cleared about a week ago, stone creatures lived inside it, and it is now completely under the control of the North American forces."
Next page.
Dungeon #2
Crimson Spider Nest
An image of a massive cave full of red webs appeared on the screen.
"This one is still being cleansed."
"The final Boss is still alive."
"A new operation is carried out there every few days."
Then the last page.
Dungeon #3
Whispering Catacombs
There was no image, only a few lines of report.
Entry Forbidden
Multiple Casualties
Unknown Invisible Entities Detected
"Just around one base... three dungeons?" Kain unconsciously whistled under his breath, dungeons were not rare, but around their base, there wasn’t even one.
Dungeons could be anywhere and weren’t specific to just one area.
The problem here was that dungeons had conditions, if they failed to clear them more than three times, all the monsters in that dungeon could enter their world and cause a disaster.
Miranda nodded.
"Three identified dungeons, there is no guarantee that these are the only ones, the actual number is probably higher."
After a few minutes of studying, Lian asked the next question.
"How far is the Special Area entrance from the base?"
Miranda zoomed in on the map slightly, and a golden point lit up in the northwest of the base.
"About one hundred and eighty kilometers, completely within Base #9’s controlled range." She paused briefly.
"That is why the federation was able to determine the country quotas without trouble, if the area was still unsafe, no student would be allowed to enter.
Lian nodded calmly, at least until reaching the entrance, there was relative safety.
But after that, everything was unknown.
Lian closed the folder and pushed it back toward Miranda.
"This information is enough for now."
Miranda also took the order notebook and checked the last items, and after a few minutes, the final invoice appeared on the table.
All the equipment, defensive scrolls, healing scrolls, Emergency Beacons, potions, camping equipment, and information reports.
All were recorded in one list, and at the bottom of the page, the final number could be seen.
Total Cost
2,487,000 Dollars
Kain just stared at the number for a few seconds.
"...Just to prepare for a trip?" He really had not expected such an amount, for experienced awakened ones, this amount was not much.
It was an amount that could easily be earned over a few months to a year, but for new awakened ones, it was really a high amount.
Lian, however, without the slightest change in expression, took out his bank card and placed it on the device.
A few seconds later, the payment confirmation sound echoed in the room, the transaction was successful, and a digital receipt appeared on the table.
More than two million dollars for equipment.
"Proper equipment really is terribly expensive." He quietly whispered under his breath.
But almost immediately, he pushed the thought aside.
If even one of those scrolls, one of those Beacons, or even one potion, saved his life or one of the group members’ lives one day... it would be worth more than all that money.
Besides, for him, it wasn’t a lot of money.
Miranda gave a calm smile.
"All your orders are ready, you can take the receipt to the third floor and collect them."
"Thank you." Lian nodded.
"Good luck, if you find anything valuable there and want to sell it, I’m here." Miranda said with her usual calm tone.
A few minutes later, Lian and Kain left Miranda’s office.
The private elevator took them back down from the seventh floor to the third floor, they handed over the receipt, and after receiving their orders, they left the tower.
After passing through the busy market and exiting the pocket dimension, they entered the same abandoned building again, from there they left and headed toward the academy.
The cool evening air hit their faces.
The capital’s sky was slowly taking on orange and purple colors, and the streetlights were turning on one after another.
People were moving on the sidewalks, cars were moving on the city’s wide streets.
Kain locked his hands behind his back and said with a calm smile.
"Tomorrow you finally set off, if I say I don’t really want to come, I’d be lying, so explore that place on my behalf too."
Lian fixed his gaze on the city’s horizon, this time their destination was no longer the Base, their caravan had to head to Base #9.
"For sure."

chapters.title: Chapter 177: Farewell for Now
paragraphs: A layer of gray fog had wrapped around the massive walls of the Base and had given a cold and heavy view to the surroundings.
However, unlike the apparent calm of the weather, the inside of the base had been awake for hours.
The sound of armors hitting each other, the closing of metal boxes, the shouts of officers coordinating the forces, and the quiet roar of pack monsters were echoing throughout the central square.
The large carts were being loaded one after another.
Barrels of water, boxes of food, ammunition crates, emergency medicine, camping equipment, and dozens of other items were being placed inside the caravan in an orderly manner.
Every soldier had a specific duty, no one was wandering aimlessly.
Everyone knew their destination was one of the farthest known bases in the Ruined Realm, and the smallest mistake could endanger the lives of dozens of people.
This was no longer a simple training mission, this was the beginning of a journey that might take weeks.
Of course, it was not just the ten selected people who were going to Base #9, a whole caravan was supposed to come with them, and all these preparations were being made for this caravan.
A few minutes later, the selected students also entered the central square one by one.
The first person was Lian.
Shortly after, Seraphina arrived in the student council’s formal uniform, after her, Cassian, Liana, Selina, and Marcus also entered the square.
Everyone had prepared their new equipment, some had upgraded their armors, and some had brought new weapons.
Three people were still absent from the group, but before anyone could say anything, a tall young man approached from among the crowd.
His dark brown hair was short and neat, and he was carrying a long spear on his back.
Unlike many spearmen, his armor was designed to be light; suitable for speed and maneuver.
He had a calm face, and his gaze showed he was more about action than words.
He stood in front of the group and bowed his head slightly with respect.
"I am Nathan," his voice was calm but firm.
"One of the members of the student council and one of the people who received the quota, I am glad we finally have a chance to get to know each other."
He shook hands with each member of the group without any arrogance, his behavior was formal, polite, and completely controlled.
"Lian." Lian also said after shaking hands.
Nathan gave a short smile.
"I have heard your name a lot more than before these past few days."
Lian just shrugged, Marcus laughed under his breath at that moment.
"The missing member has finally arrived." Everyone smiled and for a moment the group’s atmosphere became more friendly.
Fortunately, the personalities of all the group members were respectful and polite, there was no arrogant, proud, or self-satisfied person among them to ruin the atmosphere and cause trouble.
But this closeness soon gave way to silence.
Liana looked around.
"We are still missing two people.
Everyone noticed at almost the same time.
Roderick and Elena, there was no news of those two.

Rindo, who had been monitoring the situation from the beginning, said: "We will wait for them until the last moment." Although his tone was calm, it was clear from his gaze that he himself did not have much hope of those two coming.
A brief silence fell among the group, it was truly strange, almost no student would be willing to miss the opportunity to enter a Special Area.
Unless... they were really involved in something more important, but no one knew the answer to this question, and more importantly, it did not matter to any of them.
If they did not come, then they did not come, these eight people were not going to lose anything, and it was those two who would be making the biggest loss.
At that same time, Kain came toward them from among the crowd, he was wearing simple combat clothes, there was no change in his equipment, and he had his same previous armor and weapon.
He and Lian had returned to the base this morning along with the other selected members and had helped with the caravan preparations.
Unlike the others, his destination was not Base #9, his gaze paused for a moment on Lian’s new equipment and then scanned each member of the group.
In these few days, many things had changed, he himself was no longer the weak awakened one of the past, and his class had been upgraded to four stars.
He had gained new abilities but still... he was far from the position he wanted.

For this reason, he had decided to stay around the Base during this time, explore the newly liberated areas, get familiar with his new skills, hunt alone, and never put himself in a position again where he would have to wait for others to save him to survive.
His goal was simple, when Lian and Seraphina returned from this mission... he wanted to be able to truly fight alongside his friend, not behind him.
Kain smiled.
"Take care of yourselves." His gaze fixed on Lian.
"When you come back, I hope you haven’t fallen behind me."
"You better be more worried about yourself falling behind." Lian laughed quietly.
"You too, don’t be careless, next time we see each other, I expect you to be safe." Seraphina stepped forward and said.
"Don’t worry." Kain nodded confidently.
A few minutes later, a heavy silence fell over the central square, Commander Elizabeth entered, her silver armor shining under the morning light.
Although the marks of the recent battle could still be seen on part of her armor, her posture remained firm and her gaze held the same authority as always.
All her own wounds and injuries had been treated and she had no problems, she stood in front of the caravan and her gaze passed over everyone.

This caravan was not made up of only students, several experienced officers, two healers, three specialist scouts, and about fifteen awakened ones between levels twenty and twenty-eight were also accompanying the caravan.
Their duty was clear, to protect the route, deal with possible threats, and safely deliver the students to Base #9.
The route was unfortunately unknown and could be very unsafe, and this caravan contained some of the country’s greatest talents.
They had to be protected no matter what, especially Lian, who was expected to be one of the country’s future pillars.
"From the moment you leave this gate, anything can happen." Elizabeth said with a firm voice.
"No one is allowed to leave the caravan column, not even one step, without the permission of the officer in charge." Everyone nodded seriously.
"I wish you success, take care of yourselves, Special Areas can be very dangerous."
The quiet roar of the monsters that were going to pull the caravan was heard, the massive gate of the Base slowly began to open.
The golden light of the sun poured into the square through the gap in the gate, and the caravan started moving.
The pack monsters took the first steps, the heavy carts moved behind them, the country’s flag waved in the morning breeze.
The soldiers moved on both sides of the column.
The students also took their places inside the caravan.
Before leaving, Lian turned back for the last time, Kain was still standing there, both nodded calmly, and then his friend turned and left.
Lian was also thinking about his riding monster, of course he had not forgotten it and it was in its special stable, he had paid the accommodation staff to take care of it.
And then the caravan passed through the gate.
A few hours passed.
Contrary to expectations, the route was calm, the semi-ruined forests were being left behind one after another.
Sometimes a few weak monsters could be seen from a distance, but upon seeing the large military column, they did not dare to approach.
"If the whole trip is this calm, I won’t complain." Marcus even said with a laugh.
A few people laughed, the past few hours had really passed calmly and there was no problem.
They joked with each other occasionally and tried to get to know each other better and become closer.
But right at that moment... a shadow quickly came down from the top of the hill.
It was one of the level 25 scouts, his breathing was a little short, without wasting time he went straight to the caravan’s security commander.
He said a few short and quiet sentences in his ear, those few words were enough, the commander’s face immediately changed.
"Caravan, stop!"
His command echoed across the plain, in less than a few seconds, all the carts stopped.
The guards drew their weapons, the mages activated their mana circles.
The calm atmosphere of a few moments ago turned into full alert in the blink of an eye.
Lian fixed his gaze on the direction the scout had pointed.
On the horizon... a massive column of black smoke was rising into the sky, this smoke was not from a fire, but the result of an intense battle.
"That direction... is the direct route to Base #2."
A few seconds of silence followed.
"Commander... I think another caravan was attacked before us." Then the scout said with a serious voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 178: Attack On A Caravan
paragraphs: "Caravan, Stop!"
The escort commander’s voice echoed across the plain like thunder.
In less than a few seconds, the caravan’s exemplary discipline showed itself.
The pack monsters stopped moving as their reins were pulled, and the heavy carts stopped one after another.
No one asked questions, no one panicked, everyone knew exactly what to do in such situations.
The front-line soldiers immediately raised their large metal shields and formed a defensive wall in front of the caravan.
The mages stepped forward a few steps, and mana began to slowly rotate around their hands.
Magic circles appeared beneath their feet one after another, and they became more ready by the moment to release the first offensive or defensive spells if necessary.
At the same time, three scouts climbed the slopes of the surrounding hills with incredible speed and occupied the high points to monitor the environment.
Several level twenty to twenty-eight awakened ones also immediately changed their formation.
Without anyone giving them a direct order, they formed a protective ring around the students.
If an attack occurred, the first ones who needed to stay alive were the country’s future talents.
The escort commander, a burly man with dark-colored armor and a golden commander rank insignia on his chest, stepped forward.
He was one of the most powerful people present in this caravan and a level 28 awakened one.
His gaze fixed on the scout who had come down from the top of the hill moments ago.
"Full report."
The scout took a few deep breaths to steady his breathing.
"About eight to ten kilometers ahead..." He pointed toward the massive column of black smoke.
"The smoke is still fresh, besides the smoke, I also saw several mana explosions."
A few of the guards frowned, mana explosions only indicated one thing, and that was a conflict, and the scout continued.
"The conflict probably started only a few minutes ago."
He paused for a moment, and what he was about to say was even more concerning than the smoke itself.
"Inside the smoke... I saw several flashes of different skills several times."
The commander’s gaze sharpened.
"What do you mean?"
"Those flashes were not from monster attacks, it seemed like several people were using different skills."
A brief silence followed, everyone understood the meaning of this, if different skills were seen... then the opposing side was not just a few wild monsters.
The possibility of awakened ones being present... or even intelligent creatures... seemed more real than ever.
They had traveled a significant distance from their base, and there shouldn’t be other awakened ones around here... unless they were caravans from other bases.
The air around the caravan, which had been calm until a few minutes ago, suddenly became heavy.
The commander took the route map from one of the officers and stared at it for a few seconds without speaking.
This route was the most direct way to reach Base #9, if they continued on this path right now, they might walk directly into the heart of the battle.
But if they decided to go around the route... several days would be lost, and there was no guarantee that the alternative route would be safer.
A few moments later, he made his decision.
"Reconnaissance group."
Two scouts stepped forward, along with two warriors, one mage, and five people stood before the commander.
"Scout the area, direct engagement only if forced, whatever information you obtain, return immediately."
Everyone bowed their heads at the same time, the next moment, five shadows disappeared into the grassland at high speed.
A few of the students unconsciously stepped forward, they were also curious to know exactly what had happened there.
Although they expected insecurity on the route, they did not expect it from other awakened ones.
"No student is allowed to accompany." But the commander said without even looking at them.
No one objected.
Waiting... was sometimes harder than the battle itself.
The caravan remained stopped in complete silence.
The sound of wind was passing through the grasslands, and sometimes the distant roar of monsters could be heard from deep within the forest.
Marcus, who was always the most talkative member of the group, was not saying anything this time, his usual smile had faded.
Selina silently locked her fingers around her sword’s hilt.
Liana looked around several times, Rindo still stood calmly, his eyes constantly scanning the surroundings; as if his mind was already analyzing dozens of different possibilities.
A few meters away, Nathan held his long spear in his hand, his stance looked more like a veteran soldier than a student.
He did not stop guarding the surroundings for even a moment.
All the students felt the sense of danger and were ready for any possible conflict, they were far from the base, but if they ran at full speed, they could return within an hour or two.
They hoped the situation would not become so urgent that such a thing would be necessary.
Seraphina stood quietly next to Lian, her gaze still fixed on the smoke column.
"What do you think happened?"

Lian stared at the horizon for a while without answering, the smoke was still rising calmly into the sky, from his view, it also seemed like a conflict between several awakened ones, and then he said slowly.
"I hope I’m wrong, but that smoke... is not from a normal conflict."
About twenty minutes passed, and suddenly one of the scouts stationed on the hill shouted.
"They’re coming back!" All eyes turned toward the distance.
Several shadows were approaching the caravan at high speed, but... one of them was clearly limping.
When the reconnaissance group got close, everyone noticed that one of them had been wounded in the shoulder.
A deep cut had split his metal armor, and blood was still slowly flowing down from the crack in the armor.

The faces of each member of the group were much more serious than when they had left, upon seeing that something had happened to the reconnaissance group members, the sense of danger inside them became even stronger.
"Report."
The lead scout took a deep breath.
"A caravan has indeed been attacked."
The commander said nothing and waited for the continuation of the report.
"Several carts were completely destroyed, many awakened ones were killed or wounded." His voice was calm, but each sentence made the surrounding atmosphere heavier.
Then...
"But the attackers were not monsters."
"Then what were they?" The commander frowned, aside from monsters, what could attack a caravan? ... The natives of this world?
Did that mean they had encountered the natives so soon...
The scout was silent for a few seconds, as if he himself still did not believe what he had seen and did not know how to explain it.
In the end, he sighed and said quietly.
"Only... five people."
For a moment, no one reacted, then a few guards looked at each other in disbelief.
"Five people? Are you sure?" The commander asked with a heavy voice.
The scout nodded without the slightest hesitation.
"Yes, only five people." He took a deep breath.
"But... all of them were extremely strong." His eyes still held traces of disbelief.
"The caravan’s guards couldn’t even hold their ground against them, we were also attacked by one of them and were forced to retreat... that was also when they left the place."
This time even the commander fell silent.
The scout continued.
"Stranger still, they didn’t seem to have come for looting or killing, it was as if... they were looking for something." He paused for a moment.
"Or... looking for someone."
No one said anything, all eyes once again fixed on the smoke column that was still rising on the horizon.
If only five people had been able to dismantle a military caravan... how great was their true power? And why would they attack a caravan?
If that caravan had been sent by a country, then attacking it could be considered an act of war.
What sane creature would dare to do such a thing? ... Perhaps a creature that is not from their world?
So could they finally encounter the first group of natives? And could this mean that the natives have decided to carry out large-scale attacks against them? Anything was possible...
No one knew the answer to this question.
But everyone, from experienced soldiers to young students, had clearly understood one truth.
From this moment on... this journey was not going to remain peaceful.

This route was the most direct way to reach Base #9, if they continued on this path right now, they might walk directly into the heart of the battle.
But if they decided to go around the route... several days would be lost, and there was no guarantee that the alternative route would be safer.
A few moments later, he made his decision.
"Reconnaissance group."
Two scouts stepped forward, along with two warriors, one mage, and five people stood before the commander.
"Scout the area, direct engagement only if forced, whatever information you obtain, return immediately."
Everyone bowed their heads at the same time, the next moment, five shadows disappeared into the grassland at high speed.
A few of the students unconsciously stepped forward, they were also curious to know exactly what had happened there.
Although they expected insecurity on the route, they did not expect it from other awakened ones.
"No student is allowed to accompany." But the commander said without even looking at them.
No one objected.
Waiting... was sometimes harder than the battle itself.
The caravan remained stopped in complete silence.
The sound of wind was passing through the grasslands, and sometimes the distant roar of monsters could be heard from deep within the forest.
Marcus, who was always the most talkative member of the group, was not saying anything this time, his usual smile had faded.
Selina silently locked her fingers around her sword’s hilt.
Liana looked around several times, Rindo still stood calmly, his eyes constantly scanning the surroundings; as if his mind was already analyzing dozens of different possibilities.
A few meters away, Nathan held his long spear in his hand, his stance looked more like a veteran soldier than a student.
He did not stop guarding the surroundings for even a moment.
All the students felt the sense of danger and were ready for any possible conflict, they were far from the base, but if they ran at full speed, they could return within an hour or two.
They hoped the situation would not become so urgent that such a thing would be necessary.
Seraphina stood quietly next to Lian, her gaze still fixed on the smoke column.
"What do you think happened?"

Lian stared at the horizon for a while without answering, the smoke was still rising calmly into the sky, from his view, it also seemed like a conflict between several awakened ones, and then he said slowly.
"I hope I’m wrong, but that smoke... is not from a normal conflict."
About twenty minutes passed, and suddenly one of the scouts stationed on the hill shouted.
"They’re coming back!" All eyes turned toward the distance.
Several shadows were approaching the caravan at high speed, but... one of them was clearly limping.
When the reconnaissance group got close, everyone noticed that one of them had been wounded in the shoulder.
A deep cut had split his metal armor, and blood was still slowly flowing down from the crack in the armor.

The faces of each member of the group were much more serious than when they had left, upon seeing that something had happened to the reconnaissance group members, the sense of danger inside them became even stronger.
"Report."
The lead scout took a deep breath.
"A caravan has indeed been attacked."
The commander said nothing and waited for the continuation of the report.
"Several carts were completely destroyed, many awakened ones were killed or wounded." His voice was calm, but each sentence made the surrounding atmosphere heavier.
Then...
"But the attackers were not monsters."
"Then what were they?" The commander frowned, aside from monsters, what could attack a caravan? ...
The natives of this world?
Did that mean they had encountered the natives so soon...
The scout was silent for a few seconds, as if he himself still did not believe what he had seen and did not know how to explain it.
In the end, he sighed and said quietly.
"Only... five people."
For a moment, no one reacted, then a few guards looked at each other in disbelief.
"Five people?
Are you sure?" The commander asked with a heavy voice.
The scout nodded without the slightest hesitation.
"Yes, only five people." He took a deep breath.
"But... all of them were extremely strong." His eyes still held traces of disbelief.
"The caravan’s guards couldn’t even hold their ground against them, we were also attacked by one of them and were forced to retreat... that was also when they left the place."
This time even the commander fell silent.
The scout continued.
"Stranger still, they didn’t seem to have come for looting or killing, it was as if... they were looking for something." He paused for a moment.
"Or... looking for someone."
No one said anything, all eyes once again fixed on the smoke column that was still rising on the horizon.
If only five people had been able to dismantle a military caravan... how great was their true power?
And why would they attack a caravan?
If that caravan had been sent by a country, then attacking it could be considered an act of war.
What sane creature would dare to do such a thing? ...
Perhaps a creature that is not from their world?
So could they finally encounter the first group of natives?
And could this mean that the natives have decided to carry out large-scale attacks against them?
Anything was possible...
No one knew the answer to this question.
But everyone, from experienced soldiers to young students, had clearly understood one truth.
From this moment on... this journey was not going to remain peaceful.

chapters.title: Chapter 179: A Duty to Help
paragraphs: The caravan was still standing in complete silence in the middle of the plain.
The gentle wind was moving the tall grass, and the massive column of black smoke was still rising on the horizon.
No one was joking anymore, even the pack monsters had become restless and were occasionally letting out short roars.
The escort commander stared at the smoke for a few moments and then turned to the senior officers.
"Everyone here."
In less than a few seconds, five senior officers, the commander of the guards, the commander of the scouts, and two senior mages gathered around the map.
The students were standing a little further away, although the meeting was for the commanders, no one pushed them away.
After all, they were the main members of this caravan, the entire reason for the guards’ presence was to protect their safety, and every decision also concerned them.
Any decision made would directly change the fate of their mission.
The commander turned his gaze among the people, his voice calm but firm.
"First, we need to understand... who the enemy is."
A few seconds of silence followed, finally one of the officers, a middle-aged man in heavy armor, stepped forward and placed his finger on the approximate location of the conflict.
"If the attackers are the natives of the Ruined Realm, then the matter is completely clear." He continued.
"They attacked one of the World Alliance’s caravans, this means the first direct attack by a native force against humans."
His words made the surrounding atmosphere heavier, until this moment, most of the conflicts between humans had been with monsters.
If the native civilizations had really decided to directly attack human caravans... then the situation would completely change.
The World Alliance had very strict rules, and if an intelligent native force attacked them, it would be considered a declaration of war.
"In that case, our mission is not just to protect the students."
"Rescuing survivors and gathering information about the enemy becomes equally important."
A few people nodded in silence.
But another officer disagreed, he was a thin man in a gray robe who looked more like a strategist than a warrior.
"No, it is still too early for such a conclusion." He turned to the wounded scout.
"You said you only saw five people."
"Yes, and I only saw them using different skills." The scout nodded.
"What if those five people are not natives at all?" The officer said slowly.
A few people looked at him in surprise, and he continued.
"Until this moment, no one has seen the attackers’ faces, no one has heard their language, and there is no evidence to prove they were really natives."
He opened the map on the ground.
"Caravans from different countries have set out from different routes toward Base #9, the nearest base to us is Base #2, and the attacked caravan is most likely them."
"According to the rules, no caravan can attack another, but..." His gaze became more serious.
"There is no guarantee that all humans abide by the World Alliance’s rules." He raised several possibilities one by one.
"It could be an independent group, it could be an illegal organization, or even mercenaries who do anything for money, or a few thieves."
A few people listened in silence.
"Looting equipment, stealing resources, hunting powerful awakened ones, or even settling old scores... all of these could be reasons for the attack."
The atmosphere fell into silence again, this possibility was just as dangerous, in fact, maybe even more dangerous than the possibility of a native attack.
Because this way, they would be caught up in a scenario for which there were no clear rules.
Federation rules say that two bases should not enter a conflict, but if it does happen, there is no clear rule to stop it.
And now, if two groups from their own world are fighting each other, if they intervene, they will also get caught up in this chaos.
The commander did not say anything for a few moments, his gaze shifting between the distant smoke and the map.
In the end, he took a deep breath.
"If the enemy is the natives of the Ruined Realm, then helping the Base #2 caravan is our duty."
No one objected, Base #2 belonged to one of the member countries of the World Alliance.
According to military protocols, if a member of the alliance was attacked by an external force, the nearest forces were obliged to take action to help.
Aside from that, their humanity and morality were also reasons that forced them to intervene to save people from their own world.
But the commander continued.
"But, if the attackers are humans, the matter is completely different."
He turned his gaze to the officers.
"It could be an internal conflict there, it could be that Base #2 itself started the conflict, or even that both sides are members of the World Alliance." His words were logical.
If they entered the field without knowing the truth, they might unintentionally interfere in a war that had nothing to do with their mission.
A few moments later, the commander asked for the opinions of those present, especially the students, Marcus was the first to break the silence.
"If someone is still alive, we shouldn’t abandon them." His tone was serious, unlike usual.
"If we pass by a damaged caravan today... tomorrow it might be our turn."
"The main goal of this caravan is to deliver the students to Base #9, we shouldn’t let an unexpected event endanger the entire mission." Nathan said quietly.
Everyone looked at him, clearly they did not expect a member of the student council to have such a mindset.
"Before any decision, we need to understand the truth, without information, any choice could be wrong." Rindo, who had remained silent until then, said.
"If there is still a wounded person alive there, every minute of delay might cost their life." Seraphina also said quietly.
Liana and Selina also agreed with Seraphina and Marcus, they also did not want to abandon people who needed help.
"They are also our people, and we must help them." Cassian also had the same opinion.
Everyone was silent for a moment.
The only person who did not give any opinion was Lian, he was just staring at the smoke column, his mind, unlike the others, was elsewhere.
He did not care what decision they made, it made no difference to him and had no effect on him, but he also preferred that they go to see the situation.
Because if it was the work of looters, then this route was very dangerous, and this matter needed to be reported, otherwise even more casualties would occur in the future.
A few minutes later, the commander announced the final decision.
"The caravan will continue moving, but from this moment, in full battle formation."
All the guards answered at the same time.
"Yes, Commander!"
"If it becomes clear that the attackers are natives or any hostile external force, we will immediately take action."
"But if there are signs of a conflict between humans... we will assess the situation first, no one will enter the battle without orders."
The decision was clear, they would continue on this path, helping awakened ones from other bases was a duty, and they could not close their eyes to such a matter, even if it was dangerous.
No opposition was heard, this was the most logical decision possible.

Of course, this did not mean they would risk their own lives. As the commander, his duty was to protect the students, and if necessary, if something happened, he would buy them time to escape with his life.
A few minutes later, the caravan started moving again, but there was no longer any sign of the calm from a few hours ago.
The mages kept their defensive spells active from the start, the guards held their weapons in their hands.
The scouts changed their positions every few minutes to ensure no blind spots remained.
Even the pack monsters seemed to have sensed the presence of danger and were walking with restlessness.
The further they went... the thicker the smell of smoke became.
Shortly after... the smell of iron... and blood, and the gray fog slowly became thicker.
Everyone fixed their gaze ahead.
Suddenly... from within the fog, something became visible, a broken wheel, a few burnt wooden planks, and then... the first overturned cart slowly emerged from the fog.
No one said anything, the caravan... had finally reached the battlefield.

chapters.title: Chapter 180: The Black Vultures
paragraphs: The thick fog, like a gray curtain, had swallowed the entire road.
The caravan was moving at a much slower speed than before, no one even dared to speak anymore.

The only sounds heard in the heavy silence of the plain were the quiet clinking of the cart chains, the heavy steps of the pack monsters, and the sound of metal armor hitting each other with every movement of the soldiers.
All the guards had drawn their weapons from their sheaths.
The mages had gathered their mana in their palms and were ready to release their spells at any moment.
Even the students no longer had any trace of their initial excitement, everyone felt they had entered a place that death had not yet left.
A few meters... a few dozen meters... and suddenly... the first cart emerged from the fog.
But it bore no resemblance to a simple broken cart, its massive wooden body had been split in half from the middle.
The cut was so clean that it seemed as if a skilled carpenter had cut it with the largest saw in the world, no trace of explosion or burning could be seen.
Only... one cut and one strike.
"...Everyone be ready." The caravan commander said in a quiet voice without taking his gaze off the cart.
They had entered the danger zone and had to raise their guard to the highest level, the smallest mistake could end in their death.
The guards tightened the defensive ring, the caravan started moving again.
A few moments later... the massive body of one of the pack monsters became visible.
A gigantic creature over ten meters long that was responsible for carrying heavy equipment, its body lay on the ground.
But its head... was about twenty meters away, lying among the tall grass.
Even after death, its yellow eyes remained open.
"That... was at least level twenty-six..." one of the guards whispered quietly under his breath.
No other wounds could be seen on the monster’s body, only... one strike and death.
A tamed level 26 pack monster, even though it was a normal monster, in any case, it was not something anyone could kill with just one strike.
The defense of such a creature is very powerful, and to be able to kill it so easily, the attacker must be at least level 40.
The further the caravan went... the more the real battlefield revealed itself.
Giant trees, some with a diameter of two meters, had been cut in half.
Massive rocks that had been in the same place for decades had been cracked with unbelievable force.
Several large craters could be seen on the ground; as if small meteors had struck that point.
A little further away... the ground surface was completely black.
Fire magic.
A few meters away, a layer of thick ice had still not melted.
Ice magic.
On the trunk of one of the trees, a perfectly round hole could be seen, showing that a spear had passed through it at terrifying speed.
Several bodies, with clean and deep wounds, screamed the power of a master swordsman.
And on the bodies of some others... several precise arrows, lodged right between the eyes or in the heart.
Five fighting styles.
Five people, but the destruction was on the scale of an army.
Lian looked around in silence, his eyes moving over every trace of the battle, putting the attack marks together.
He measured the distances, examined the angles of the strikes, and only one question repeated in his mind.
"...Was this really done by five people?" Even for him, it was hard to believe.
If it was only five people, then they had to be at least level 40, meaning even more powerful than Commander Elizabeth.
Most base commanders are between levels 35 and 40, and now they were witnessing an attack carried out by awakened ones with that level of power on a caravan from an official base.
And it was clear that those responsible for these scenes were extremely ruthless.
Suddenly... a weak sound broke the silence.
Everyone turned toward the sound at the same time, several guards ran without delay, behind one of the overturned carts... a group of survivors had taken shelter.
About fifteen people.
Most were covered in blood, some were unconscious, and others were only still sitting by leaning on their spears or swords.
Two of the caravan’s Healers immediately stepped forward, the green light of mana lit up the surrounding space.
The wounds were closing one by one, the bleeding was stopping, and among those people... a man with half-broken golden armor was leaning against the cart’s wall.
The entire left part of his armor was soaked in blood, and where his left hand should have been... there was only a bloody piece of cloth tied.
His hand had been severed from the elbow, despite the severe paleness of his face, he was still conscious.
His eyes calmly fixed on the caravan commander, the escort commander knelt down, expecting this survivor to ask whether the attackers had left or about the number of survivors.
But the wounded man did not even look at him, and his dry lips moved with difficulty.
"...Beacon..."
The commander frowned, what was this man trying to say?
The man breathed with difficulty.
"Ancient Beacon..."
It took a few moments for him to speak again.
"...Is it here...? Did you find it?"
Everyone around fell silent.
"No. What is it?" The commander answered calmly, he also did not understand what this man was talking about.
A few seconds... no sound was heard, and then... the face of the Base #2 escort commander completely collapsed.
As if his last hope had been destroyed at that very moment, he quietly closed his eyes, a bitter smile settling on his lips.
"...Then... everything is over..."
After the Healers stopped his bleeding, the commander looked at him and asked.
"Now can you tell us exactly what happened to you? What is this situation? Who carried out such a ruthless and brutal attack on you?"
"Inside one of the ancient Ruins in the eighth Ruined Realm, we found an Artifact." The man started speaking again, his voice was still weak, but each word sounded heavier than before.
"What does this have to do with anything?" Marcus grumbled.
But the commander signaled for him to let this man continue speaking.
"At first, no one knew what it was, but after numerous examinations, its name was determined... Ancient Beacon." He fixed his gaze on the sky.
"This Artifact was not meant to make anyone stronger, it didn’t give combat power, but, it gave a strategic advantage that was worth more than thousands of Skills." Everyone listened in silence.
But to some extent, everyone was curious to know what this item had to do with the current situation? Wouldn’t it be better to talk about the attackers and what had happened?
However, with the following sentences, they understood what the matter was...
"According to the information we got from the system, when the Ancient Beacon is activated inside a Special Area..."
"All monsters, even the strongest ones, will ignore the one carrying it."
A few people looked at each other in disbelief.
The commander continued.

"Not that they run away, not that they die or anything like that, they just don’t consider its presence a threat, meaning one could reach the depths of areas that exist in Special Areas without unnecessary conflicts and take the best treasures." He calmly let out his breath.
The members of Base #3’s caravan looked at each other, such an artifact was truly valuable.
It could practically protect them from monsters and give them freedom of action.
"We wanted our country’s expedition forces to the Special Area to use it... but those damn vultures attacked us and stole it."
A frown appeared on everyone’s faces.
Vultures? Only one group of awakened ones was called Vultures!
"How are you sure it was them?" one of the officers who had remained silent until then asked.
The Base #2 commander gave a bitter laugh.
"Because they told us themselves."
Everyone looked at him.
"Their leader didn’t even try to hide his identity." He said quietly.
A few minutes before the battle started... five people, standing right in the middle of the road.
They all wore matching black clothes, their faces hidden behind dark masks.
Their long cloaks were moving in the wind, but what caught everyone’s attention...
Was the emblem sewn on the back of their cloaks, a black vulture with fully spread wings, as if ready to land on a fresh corpse.
Their leader stepped forward, his voice calm, without anger, without threat, as if he was just stating a simple fact.
"Black Vultures."
A few of the guards lost their color at that same moment, and he continued.
"Hand over the chest, and continue on your way."
A few seconds of silence followed, then... he said his last sentence.
"Otherwise, all of you will die right here."
After remembering that scene, the Base #2 commander opened his eyes.
"We... thought we could resist." He gave a bitter smile.
"It was the biggest mistake of our lives." With his remaining hand, he pointed at the battlefield.
"All this destruction took less than ten minutes."
"Five people, only five people... took down more than dozens of awakened ones."
"The guards, the mages... the archers... even the pack monsters... none of them could stop them."
A few of the students unconsciously swallowed.
Marcus had clenched his fists, Seraphina was silently looking at the surrounding bodies.
And Lian... sighed.
Power.
Ruthlessness.
And humans who did not care the slightest about others’ lives to achieve their goals.
"Wait... wasn’t the existence of the Ancient Beacon a secret? Because we had no knowledge of such a thing." one of the officers suddenly said.
The Base #2 commander slowly raised his head, this time... only anger could be seen in his eyes.
"It was, only our country’s officials and the World Alliance central headquarters knew of its existence."
No one said anything, he struck the ground with his remaining strength.
"The Black Vultures went straight for that same chest, they didn’t even look at the rest of the cargo."
"No gold, no mana crystals, no equipment, only that same chest." His breathing had become heavy, the veins in his neck were bulging from the intensity of his anger.
"That means someone inside the World Alliance or among our country’s officials sold the information to the Black Vultures."
A heavy silence fell over the entire battlefield, no one was looking at the bodies on the ground anymore.
Even thinking about such a thing was terrifying.

The Black Vultures are one of the most notorious organizations in the world, an organization famous for murder and plunder, and practically their slogan was that wherever there is death, there will also be profit.
There have been times when they have slaughtered several small towns just to kill one person...
It is unknown where their central headquarters is, who their leader is, how many members they have.
But their power is completely known and recognized, a power that is not less than some powerful guilds...
Even thinking that such a dirty and terrorist organization has a spy in the World Alliance or a country is terrifying...

A tamed level 26 pack monster, even though it was a normal monster, in any case, it was not something anyone could kill with just one strike.
The defense of such a creature is very powerful, and to be able to kill it so easily, the attacker must be at least level 40.
The further the caravan went... the more the real battlefield revealed itself.
Giant trees, some with a diameter of two meters, had been cut in half.
Massive rocks that had been in the same place for decades had been cracked with unbelievable force.
Several large craters could be seen on the ground; as if small meteors had struck that point.
A little further away... the ground surface was completely black.
Fire magic.
A few meters away, a layer of thick ice had still not melted.
Ice magic.
On the trunk of one of the trees, a perfectly round hole could be seen, showing that a spear had passed through it at terrifying speed.
Several bodies, with clean and deep wounds, screamed the power of a master swordsman.
And on the bodies of some others... several precise arrows, lodged right between the eyes or in the heart.
Five fighting styles.
Five people, but the destruction was on the scale of an army.
Lian looked around in silence, his eyes moving over every trace of the battle, putting the attack marks together.
He measured the distances, examined the angles of the strikes, and only one question repeated in his mind.
"...Was this really done by five people?" Even for him, it was hard to believe.
If it was only five people, then they had to be at least level 40, meaning even more powerful than Commander Elizabeth.
Most base commanders are between levels 35 and 40, and now they were witnessing an attack carried out by awakened ones with that level of power on a caravan from an official base.
And it was clear that those responsible for these scenes were extremely ruthless.
Suddenly... a weak sound broke the silence.
Everyone turned toward the sound at the same time, several guards ran without delay, behind one of the overturned carts... a group of survivors had taken shelter.
About fifteen people.
Most were covered in blood, some were unconscious, and others were only still sitting by leaning on their spears or swords.
Two of the caravan’s Healers immediately stepped forward, the green light of mana lit up the surrounding space.
The wounds were closing one by one, the bleeding was stopping, and among those people... a man with half-broken golden armor was leaning against the cart’s wall.
The entire left part of his armor was soaked in blood, and where his left hand should have been... there was only a bloody piece of cloth tied.
His hand had been severed from the elbow, despite the severe paleness of his face, he was still conscious.
His eyes calmly fixed on the caravan commander, the escort commander knelt down, expecting this survivor to ask whether the attackers had left or about the number of survivors.
But the wounded man did not even look at him, and his dry lips moved with difficulty.
"...Beacon..."
The commander frowned, what was this man trying to say?
The man breathed with difficulty.
"Ancient Beacon..."
It took a few moments for him to speak again.
"...Is it here...?
Did you find it?"
Everyone around fell silent.
"No.
What is it?" The commander answered calmly, he also did not understand what this man was talking about.
A few seconds... no sound was heard, and then... the face of the Base #2 escort commander completely collapsed.
As if his last hope had been destroyed at that very moment, he quietly closed his eyes, a bitter smile settling on his lips.
"...Then... everything is over..."
After the Healers stopped his bleeding, the commander looked at him and asked.
"Now can you tell us exactly what happened to you?
What is this situation?
Who carried out such a ruthless and brutal attack on you?"
"Inside one of the ancient Ruins in the eighth Ruined Realm, we found an Artifact." The man started speaking again, his voice was still weak, but each word sounded heavier than before.
"What does this have to do with anything?" Marcus grumbled.
But the commander signaled for him to let this man continue speaking.
"At first, no one knew what it was, but after numerous examinations, its name was determined...
Ancient Beacon." He fixed his gaze on the sky.
"This Artifact was not meant to make anyone stronger, it didn’t give combat power, but, it gave a strategic advantage that was worth more than thousands of Skills." Everyone listened in silence.
But to some extent, everyone was curious to know what this item had to do with the current situation?
Wouldn’t it be better to talk about the attackers and what had happened?
However, with the following sentences, they understood what the matter was...
"According to the information we got from the system, when the Ancient Beacon is activated inside a Special Area..."
"All monsters, even the strongest ones, will ignore the one carrying it."
A few people looked at each other in disbelief.
The commander continued.

"Not that they run away, not that they die or anything like that, they just don’t consider its presence a threat, meaning one could reach the depths of areas that exist in Special Areas without unnecessary conflicts and take the best treasures." He calmly let out his breath.
The members of Base #3’s caravan looked at each other, such an artifact was truly valuable.
It could practically protect them from monsters and give them freedom of action.
"We wanted our country’s expedition forces to the Special Area to use it... but those damn vultures attacked us and stole it."
A frown appeared on everyone’s faces.
Vultures?
Only one group of awakened ones was called Vultures!
"How are you sure it was them?" one of the officers who had remained silent until then asked.
The Base #2 commander gave a bitter laugh.
"Because they told us themselves."
Everyone looked at him.
"Their leader didn’t even try to hide his identity." He said quietly.
A few minutes before the battle started... five people, standing right in the middle of the road.
They all wore matching black clothes, their faces hidden behind dark masks.
Their long cloaks were moving in the wind, but what caught everyone’s attention...
Was the emblem sewn on the back of their cloaks, a black vulture with fully spread wings, as if ready to land on a fresh corpse.
Their leader stepped forward, his voice calm, without anger, without threat, as if he was just stating a simple fact.
"Black Vultures."
A few of the guards lost their color at that same moment, and he continued.
"Hand over the chest, and continue on your way."
A few seconds of silence followed, then... he said his last sentence.
"Otherwise, all of you will die right here."
After remembering that scene, the Base #2 commander opened his eyes.
"We... thought we could resist." He gave a bitter smile.
"It was the biggest mistake of our lives." With his remaining hand, he pointed at the battlefield.
"All this destruction took less than ten minutes."
"Five people, only five people... took down more than dozens of awakened ones."
"The guards, the mages... the archers... even the pack monsters... none of them could stop them."
A few of the students unconsciously swallowed.
Marcus had clenched his fists, Seraphina was silently looking at the surrounding bodies.
And Lian... sighed.
Power.
Ruthlessness.
And humans who did not care the slightest about others’ lives to achieve their goals.
"Wait... wasn’t the existence of the Ancient Beacon a secret?
Because we had no knowledge of such a thing." one of the officers suddenly said.
The Base #2 commander slowly raised his head, this time... only anger could be seen in his eyes.
"It was, only our country’s officials and the World Alliance central headquarters knew of its existence."
No one said anything, he struck the ground with his remaining strength.
"The Black Vultures went straight for that same chest, they didn’t even look at the rest of the cargo."
"No gold, no mana crystals, no equipment, only that same chest." His breathing had become heavy, the veins in his neck were bulging from the intensity of his anger.
"That means someone inside the World Alliance or among our country’s officials sold the information to the Black Vultures."
A heavy silence fell over the entire battlefield, no one was looking at the bodies on the ground anymore.
Even thinking about such a thing was terrifying.

The Black Vultures are one of the most notorious organizations in the world, an organization famous for murder and plunder, and practically their slogan was that wherever there is death, there will also be profit.
There have been times when they have slaughtered several small towns just to kill one person...
It is unknown where their central headquarters is, who their leader is, how many members they have.
But their power is completely known and recognized, a power that is not less than some powerful guilds...
Even thinking that such a dirty and terrorist organization has a spy in the World Alliance or a country is terrifying...

chapters.title: Chapter 181: A Different Kind of Monster
paragraphs: No one suggested continuing the journey.
No one even talked about the lost time. After what they had seen on the battlefield... everyone knew that leaving those bodies behind would be an insult to those who had fought until the last moment.
The caravan stopped right there, and the commander gave only one order.
"Before we leave, we gather the dead."
Two hours later... the entire plain had turned into a silent cemetery.
Dozens of people were moving among the bodies in silence, no sound of laughter could be heard.
No conversations, only the sound of shovels hitting the soil and sometimes the sound of heavy armors being dragged on the ground.
Even the students were not exempt, they also had to help.
One was responsible for collecting identification tags, another was gathering personal items from beside the bodies.
Watches that were still working... necklaces that were probably family heirlooms... small notebooks... rings...
All were placed in separate boxes to be delivered to their owners’ families later.
A few others were collecting intact swords, spears, and shields.
Not for looting... but so that these equipment would not be destroyed among the monsters.
Lian, along with a few guards, lifted the body of one of the Awakened ones.
The man was about forty years old, his hand was still firmly locked around his sword’s hilt, so firmly... that even after death, his fingers were hard to open.
"Leave it... bury him like that." The guard next to him said quietly.
Lian said nothing, just nodded.
A little further away, Liana suddenly fell to her knees while gathering bodies.
Her face had turned completely white, and a few seconds later... she vomited all the contents of her stomach onto the ground.
No one laughed at her, no one scolded her, a few guards just glanced at her briefly... and went back to work.
For them... this was not the first time, but for most of the students... it was.
Until yesterday... becoming an Awakened one seemed like a dream.
Powerful classes, magical skills, fame, wealth, but today... they had seen the other side of this world.
Bodies that would never return home, families that were probably still waiting for their loved ones.
And men and women who had fought until their last breath... but in the end, all that remained of them was a metal tag and a bloody sword.
What had happened here was a massacre, almost 99 percent of this caravan had been killed and butchered, without any mercy and completely brutally.
It was clear those bastards Vultures could have just taken what they wanted and left... they could have carried out their looting without such a crime.
But no, a simple looting had no benefit for them, and they committed such a sick crime just for pleasure...
Until sunset... dozens of large graves had been dug side by side, on each grave, only a simple stone was placed.
Without names, because the identities of many of the dead had not yet been determined, their faces had been destroyed, or many had been completely torn apart.
The caravan commander stood in front of the graves for a few moments, then quietly gave a military salute, all the guards did the same.
No speech was given, no grand ceremony was held, only... a few seconds of silence and then... the caravan started moving again.
It was a horrifying scene, but except for the students, for the others, it was a scene they might have witnessed more than once in their lives.
With the difference that in most cases, such scenes are created by monsters... not other humans...
The fifteen survivors from Base #2 also joined them.
Most of them still could not walk and were placed inside the carts, two Healers constantly checked their condition.
The Base #2 commander, despite the insistence of others, refused to rest.
He sat on one of the carts, his left hand was no longer there, but his gaze... was still that of a commander.
When the escort commander asked him to rest for a few more days, he only said one sentence.
"The report about the Ancient Beacon must reach Base #9 as soon as possible, if we are even one day late, it might be too late." That base belonged to the North American continental coalition.
The officials there held more authority and power and could help.
No one objected anymore.
That night, the caravan set up camp in a vast plain, dozens of small fires were lit in various places.
But no sound of laughter could be heard, no one talked about hunting monsters, and no one spoke about the future.
All the conversations... were only about one name.
Black Vultures.
Marcus threw a piece of wood into the fire, and sparks flew into the sky.
He stared at the flames for a few moments and said.

"I heard that three years ago, they looted and destroyed a border town in one of the southern European countries, just because one of the town’s wealthy businessmen had bought an Artifact from an auction and they wanted that Artifact."
One of the guards gave a bitter sigh.
"That’s nothing, six years ago, a medium-sized Guild in one of the Caribbean countries had taken a multi-million dollar contract to protect a merchant."
Everyone looked at him, and he continued.
"The Black Vultures only wanted that merchant, when the Guild refused to hand him over..."
"They killed all the Guild members, over four hundred Awakened ones, no one survived."
A heavy silence fell around the fire.
"So... why doesn’t the World Alliance destroy them?" Selina asked hesitantly.
This was a thought that had been in her, Liana’s, and Marcus’s minds for several hours, they could not understand why a coalition wouldn’t form to destroy such an evil organization.
This time the caravan commander answered.

"Destroying a monster is easy, but destroying an organization that has bases in dozens of countries, whose members have fake identities, and who are willing to do anything for money, is not that simple."
"Besides, who knows what they would do if they faced an existential threat?" He paused briefly and then continued more quietly.
"For the Black Vultures, humans... are just numbers, if killing a hundred people brings a profit of ten billion, a hundred people will die."
"If killing ten thousand people brings a profit of a hundred billion, ten thousand people will also die."
"It makes no difference to them, so think about what they would do if their existence was in danger."
No one said anything more, the flames of the fire were the only sound heard in that silence.
That night... Lian could not sleep, he lay in the tent for a few minutes.
He looked at the fabric ceiling, but every time he closed his eyes, the image of the battlefield appeared before him again.
He sighed, quietly left the tent, the night air was cold, a gentle wind was blowing among the grass.
Without any specific destination, he moved away from the camp.
A few minutes later... he stood on a short rock, from there he could see the entire camp.
The light of the fires... the guards patrolling in silence... and the sky full of stars.
Lian calmly raised his head, his gaze lost among the stars.
Today’s scene was unbearable for any normal human, but what occupied his mind...
Was not the bodies themselves, but the fact that he had seen that same scene again.
The last time he had seen such a scene was back to his first days in the Ruined Realm.
When he was just one of thousands of victims summoned here, he had seen a scene similar to today in the village of the Dreadmaw mutants.
It was still vivid in his mind with all its details, that same basement of those abandoned houses and hundreds of humans who did not even find a chance to escape and all had been butchered and hung.
He thought he would never have to see such a scene again, but today everything had repeated itself.
The only difference was that this time, the killers were not monsters but humans.
His gaze did not leave the stars, in his heart, only one sentence repeated.
Sometimes he forgets that monsters are not the only danger, and how cruel the world can be.

Selina, Liana, and Marcus did not know why a coalition was not formed to destroy that organization, but he knew, not only him but he also noticed that Rindo and Nathan also seemed to have information or guesses.
Seraphina also naturally knew, the main reason is that this organization is secretly supported by some of the most powerful figures in the world to do their dirty work.
Not everyone has this information and awareness, except for people like him who are born into clans that are among the rulers of the world...
After a while, he returned to the tent and finally fell asleep.
The next morning... the caravan set off again.
Five days later.
The route gradually became smoother, paved roads replaced forest paths.
The number of caravans passing by them increased more and more.
Pack monsters, exploration groups, trade caravans, military units, and even caravans like theirs that had come for the Special Area.
All were moving in one direction, toward Base #9.
An hour later... the caravan crossed the last hill, the commander suddenly raised his hand.
"Stop."
Everyone stopped, the students came forward in surprise, and then... they saw it.
No one breathed, no one spoke, because in front of them... was Base #9.
No...
This was no longer a base, a massive city, in the middle of endless plains, stone walls whose height exceeded a hundred meters, like an artificial mountain, had surrounded the entire city.
Dozens of watchtowers rose from the walls at regular intervals, and on each one, mana artillery and giant catapults were ready to fire.
Flags from different countries were waving on top of the towers in the wind.
In front of the main gate, a long line of caravans had formed, hundreds of pack monsters, thousands of Awakened ones, merchants, soldiers, and exploration groups all coming and going.
Even from this distance, the commotion of that military city could be heard.
Marcus, with eyes wide open, stared at the scene for a few seconds and then whispered under his breath.
"Damn..." His gaze still hadn’t left the massive walls.
"...Is this a base?"
And the caravan... slowly, continued moving toward one of the largest human fortresses in the tenth Ruined Realm.
