chapters.title: Chapter 182: In Base #9
paragraphs: The caravan, after crossing the last hill, slowly moved toward the massive gates of Base #9.
From close range, the grandeur of this base was even greater than what it had seemed from a distance.
Walls reaching over a hundred meters in height stood like an artificial mountain in the middle of the gray plains of the Ruined Realm.
Dozens of watchtowers were built on top of the walls, and on each tower, mana catapults, magical artillery, and dozens of armed awakened ones were ready to face any threat.
At the top of the walls, flags from different countries were waving gently in the wind alongside the World Alliance flag.
Just by seeing this scene, everyone understood that this was no longer an ordinary base.
This was the heart of humanity’s operations in one of the most important areas of the Ruined Realm.
Compared to their own base, Base #3, the difference was very noticeable, to the point that they were not even comparable at all, this base was at least ten times larger than their base.
Just in terms of defense, it could easily not only withstand the siege and battle they had experienced but also resolve it within a few minutes.
Of course, this base was also one of the best of its kind, currently it could probably be considered among the five largest bases in the Ruined Realm.
After approaching the main gate, the caravan stopped, unlike their Base, entering here was not done just by opening the gate.
Several inspection teams were already waiting, first the identity of all individuals was checked.
ID cards were scanned one by one, and everyone’s names were registered in the base, after that, it was time for the mana scan.
Several mages, using special Artifacts, examined the mana waves of all individuals to make sure no unknown creature, curse, or mana contamination entered the base.
After that, the class type and level of all awakened ones were recorded.
The number of people in each caravan, the number of pack monsters, the amount of equipment, the quantity of ammunition, and even the number of carts were also registered in the base’s central system.
All these steps were done with surprising speed, there was no chaos.
Every officer knew exactly their duty, and hundreds of people, like the gears of a massive machine, worked in harmony with each other.
Lian looked around in silence, until today, Base #3 had seemed large to him, but now he understood that base was nothing but a small border fortress compared to this.
This place... was a massive war machine.
This also made him curious about the main bases, how large were they?
After the inspection ended, the second gates also opened, the caravan entered Base #9, at that same moment, almost all the students involuntarily stopped for a few seconds.
Behind the massive walls was a complete city.
Wide stone streets, multi-story buildings, command towers, massive warehouses, and thousands of humans moving without a moment’s pause.
No part of the city was quiet, on the right side, the military zone was located.
Dozens of training grounds were built next to each other, thousands of soldiers and awakened ones were training.
Swords clashed, spears split the air.
Mages were activating mana circles one after another, and explosions of fire, ice, wind, and lightning lit up the sky.
In another corner, several groups were training with live monsters.
Commanders were shouting orders loudly, the entire area smelled of steel, sweat, and mana.
On the other side of the city, the sound of hundreds of hammers striking could be heard.
The craftsmen’s zone, dozens of blacksmiths working side by side, mana metals were melting in massive furnaces.
Heavy hammers landed on shining ingots, and each strike scattered blue and golden sparks in the air.
Swords were polished on special tables, damaged armors were repaired, spears, shields, arrows, and even special equipment for mages were coming out of the production lines one after another.
Of course, most of them were only blacksmiths who could make weapons below B rank, but for the soldiers and to ensure they never faced a shortage of weapons, it was enough.
A few streets ahead was the market, but this was no longer a small market like the Base.
Dozens of commercial streets were built next to each other, the large signs of the shops could be seen from a distance.
Artifact Shop.
Skill Book Shop.
Potion Shop.
Monster Core Exchange.
Auction House.
Mercenary Board.
Guild Recruitment Center.
The shouts of vendors, the bargaining of customers, and the movement of hundreds of awakened ones had created an atmosphere that looked more like the big cities in online games than a military base.
Every few steps, an item could be seen that in normal cities, its name might not even be heard.
Cores of high-rank monsters, skins of rare creatures, bones of various monsters, rare plants that only grew in the Ruined Realm.
Everything was available for buying and selling, but at prices that were not easy to imagine.
In another part of the city, the massive medical center building was located.
In front of it, a long line of wounded could be seen, some had lost an arm, some had lost a leg.
Some with burned faces were being carried on stretchers.
Healer mages, without a moment’s rest, were activating healing spells one after another.
Green and white lights had almost covered the entire building.

Some carried the flag of the Northern Federation, another caravan was entering from the Eastern Coalition.
Several caravans from European countries, groups from Central Asia, and even forces from North African countries were entering the base one by one.
Their clothes, armors, and equipment styles were different, but everyone’s destination was the same.
The Special Area.

As expected, the federation had distributed many quotas among different countries of the world, and each country’s government decided how many of the quotas they received would be given to their guilds and organizations.
Naturally, each country that was higher in the ranking of power and influence received more quotas.
It seemed the entire Base #9 was preparing for the largest operation of the past few weeks.

A few seconds later, a man’s voice spread throughout the base through the mana communication system.
"All caravan commanders, report to the command hall within two hours."
"I repeat... all caravan commanders, report to the command hall within two hours."
A few officers immediately separated from the caravans, the escort commander also turned to the students.
"You are free until the end of the meeting, but do not leave the base’s limits, we will gather here again in two hours."

No one knew what threats they might face, and having one or two spare shields was not a bad idea.
Nathan, after a brief look around, headed toward the Arena, he intended to do a few practice fights before the mission began.
Seraphina went toward the potion market.

Selina and Liana also decided to check out the light equipment market.
Cassian and Rindo went to the information center to check the mission boards and the latest news.

Every street showed a new image of humanity’s power, this also created another curiosity for him, were the seven regions of the native humans of this world on the same level as this base?
Or were they even larger and more advanced? How advanced and powerful were their civilizations?
"Hmm?" But a few minutes later, his steps suddenly stopped.
A bad feeling came over him, and he felt... someone was watching him.
He calmly turned around, the crowd, the shops, the soldiers... nothing unusual could be seen.
He walked for a few more seconds, and the same feeling returned, but much stronger! He felt killing intent directed at him!
He was sure! This was killing intent that was directly targeting him.
This time, he raised his head faster, and on the rooftop of a distant building, a human shadow was standing, the distance was great, and his face could not be seen.
The only thing that was clear was a dark cloak moving in the wind.

As if it had never existed in the first place, Lian stood there for a few more moments.
"Who was that?" A deep frown appeared on his face.
He was sure he had felt killing intent, and that intent was not a joke, but who could have such intent toward him?
"Could it be...?" A possibility came to his mind, but he was not sure at all, but if it was correct, then it seemed he had entered their list...
Then without saying anything, he continued on his way.
But this time, his senses were fully alert.

Unlike before, his face and the other officers’ faces were completely serious, he looked at the students for a few moments, then said with a firm voice.
"All students, tomorrow at eight in the morning, the opening ceremony of the Special Area will be held."
He was silent for a few seconds, and his gaze passed over each of them.
"After that, once you enter, there will be no turning back."

chapters.title: Chapter 183: The Final Countdown
paragraphs: Dawn had not fully settled over Base #9 when the base’s massive bells began to ring one after another.
Their heavy resonance passed through the hundred-meter walls and echoed throughout the military city; a sound that had a very clear meaning for the residents of this base.
The day of the operation had arrived.
The streets, which had not been quiet last night either, were now even busier than before.
Hundreds of caravans were loading their final equipment, and pack monsters were carrying carts full of ammunition, supplies, and magical equipment toward the southern gate.
In the blacksmiths’ zone, the sound of hammers did not stop for a moment.
Blacksmiths were repairing the last cracks on armors, sharpening sword edges again, and placing mana crystals into weapons.
In the market, long lines had formed in front of the Potion shops.
Some were buying dozens of healing potions, some were choosing their last Skill Books.
A few were standing in front of Artifact stalls and looking at the prices in disappointment.
No one was laughing loudly, no one was talking about the future, the atmosphere of the city was heavy, and everyone knew one truth.
Today, a large number of people would enter the Special Area, but a large part of them were not going to return alive.
The caravan commander took Lian’s group to a building near their quarters.
It was not a large room, just a simple stone hall with a long wooden table in the center and a few benches around it.
He closed the door and then turned to the group and said.
"We move in one hour, before that... final preparations." Everyone sat around the table, and without any extra words, each person opened their storage space.
One after another, items were placed on the table.
Bottles of healing potions, mana recovery potions, consumable Skill Scrolls.
Magic traps, dried food, mana crystals, throwing knives, and even a few small anti-poison pills.
A few minutes later, almost the entire table surface was covered with equipment.
Marcus looked at the items and gave a short laugh.
"If people outside saw this many potions on a table..." He pointed at the bottles with his finger.
"They would think we are starting a world war."
A small smile appeared on the faces of a few people, the heavy tension that had cast a shadow over the group for the past few days faded away.
Just by looking at all the items they had bought and prepared for this trip, it showed how ready they were.
With all this equipment, they could survive for months even in the harshest conditions and stay alive without problems.

Apart from this, they had all learned the necessary lessons for the conditions they were about to enter, and during the past few days of travel, the commanders had passed on all their experience to them.
The commander placed both his hands on the table.
"Well, let’s see if you learned anything or not." His gaze moved over each member of the group.
"If you are surrounded by flying monsters, what do you do?"
"Attack, before they fully surround us, we break through one direction." Marcus answered almost without thinking.

The commander nodded, neither confirming nor rejecting, it was definitely not a bad strategy and could work, if of course all the flying monsters did not surround them at the same time, but it had its weaknesses too.
"You?" Then he looked at Nathan.
"Form a defensive formation, mages in the center, close-range fighters around, first we have to repel their first attack." Nathan thought for a few seconds.
The commander said nothing again and his gaze fell on Seraphina.
"If one of the group members is wounded?"
"First the wounded, if we don’t treat them, the group’s power decreases." Cassian answered without hesitation.
Their group, although strong offensively, had many shortcomings, they did not have a healer, and there was no news of two of their members, and they seemed to have decided not to participate.
So each member was of high importance and had to be treated immediately.
"Correct." The commander said quietly, and then... his gaze fixed on Lian.
"If the group gets separated from the very beginning?"
"First, we don’t waste all our attention and mindset searching for each other." Lian answered without rushing.
A few people looked at him in surprise, but he continued.
"First we get out of the danger zone, we try to choose the most eye-catching point that draws attention, and everyone moves toward that point, this way we can find each other."
"If someone faces a threat they cannot handle, it is better to just run toward that point with all their power."
The commander gave a very faint smile.
"Correct." Then he asked the last question.
"If you see a powerful intelligent species monster, what do you do?"
This time no one answered, and a few seconds of silence followed.
"Flee." Then Lian said quietly.
"That’s it?" Nathan frowned, as if he had seen this answer as cowardly.
Lian looked at him.

"A powerful intelligent species has the ability to think and reason and can plan, if you have no information about it, the best way is to flee, unless you are sure you can overpower it with pure power."

"If you fight an enemy you have no chance against, that is not courage, it is stupidity, the best thing is that if we are together, we first get information about that species, and if we are separated, we just find each other and then deal with it."
Of course, all the words he was saying were only for the others, he himself, if he saw an intelligent species, would definitely do the same as long as he was sure he could handle it.
By killing it, he could also gain a lot of information from it, and also his strategy in the Special Area was not going to be about finding the others.

The commander stared at him for a few moments, deep down, he involuntarily accepted something. Among all these students, Lian was the only one whose answers did not smell of books, but smelled of survival.
At that same time, Lian took something out of his storage space, everyone thought he was going to take out an item.
But... six small and transparent crystals were placed on the table.
The crystals were the size of a fingertip, and in the center of each, a calm blue light was pulsing.
All eyes were fixed on them, Marcus was the first to whisper.
"...Emergency Beacon?"
Even the commander raised his eyebrow, this device... was one of the most expensive rescue Artifacts.
Lian pushed them toward the group members one by one.
"Everyone take one."
No one reached out, and a few seconds of silence followed.
Finally, Marcus picked up the crystal, he still could not believe it.
"...Where did you get it?" Aside from their price, these were extremely rare, he had wanted to buy a few but had not found any in the market.
"From the market." Lian answered without even raising his head.
That was it.
He did not give more explanation, nor did he allow another question, and when everyone took their Beacon, Lian said quietly.
"Listen to my words carefully."
Everyone fell silent.
"Only activate it when you are sure you are about to die, not when you are scared, and not when the mission gets hard, only... when you are sure there is no other way."
"When they are activated, they make a lot of noise and can attract the attention of all the monsters."
He paused for a few moments, and then his gaze passed over each member of the group.
"If someone activates the Beacon, we abandon the entire mission."
No one said anything, and Lian continued.
"No one is left alone, and we must make sure everyone returns alive."
This time even Nathan could not say anything.
A few minutes later, the base’s bells rang again.
All participants moved toward the outside of the base and the location of the rift, the closer the group got to the rift, the larger the crowd became.
Thousands of awakened ones, tens of thousands of people, commanders, famous Guilds.
Military squads, exploration groups, and flags of different countries were waving in the wind, and a massive stone platform had been built in the center of the square.
A few minutes later, the head of Base #9 stepped forward, he was a middle-aged man in black armor with the golden emblem of the World Alliance shining on his chest.
He did not smile, did not give a speech, and just said directly.
"In the last Special Area discovered in the previous Ruined Realm..." His voice, with the help of sound-amplifying Artifacts, echoed across the entire square.
"Fifty-four percent of the participants never returned, if anyone still wants to withdraw, now is the time."
A few seconds passed, but not even one person stepped back.
The head just nodded.
"Very well, then you may enter."
Finally... everyone stood in front of a massive rift.
As if a part of the world had been cut away.
The mist that was calmly spinning seemed to lead to another world.
Anyone who stared at it felt that the darkness was also staring back at them.
Suddenly... the entire rift trembled with a blinding blue light, and a massive wave of mana spread in the air, everyone’s hair moved from the intensity of the energy.
"Move!"
At that same moment, the first groups entered the rift, one after another, Guilds, military squads, exploration caravans, all those who had entry quotas.
The commander looked at Lian’s group.
"It is our turn."
Lian took a deep breath, stepped forward, and then, together with the group members, moved toward the ancient rift.
The moment his foot passed the rift’s border... the blue light swallowed everything.

Lian took a deep breath, stepped forward, and then, together with the group members, moved toward the ancient rift.
The moment his foot passed the rift’s border... the blue light swallowed everything.

chapters.title: Chapter 184: The Nest of Giants
paragraphs: Everything... was white.
There was no sky, no ground, no sound, and no direction, but only an endless sea of light that had swallowed the entire world.
Lian felt no sense of falling, his body was neither light nor heavy, and he didn’t even feel like he was moving.
It was as if time had stopped flowing for a few moments.
This experience of entering an interdimensional rift reminded him a little of the portals, it had significantly the same feeling and experience.
This made him curious about the origin of both, portals were set up with the help of magic and arrays and connected two points in one world.
The exact mechanism behind it was not clear, but it was said that it bends the space between these two points, like black holes.
But what about interdimensional rifts?
They were cracks between different dimensions of the world, how was their mechanism?
Did they work like portals and only at a higher level?
However, before he could think more about it, the light slowly began to fade.
The first thing he felt... was the wind.
A cold and powerful wind that passed by his face and violently fluttered his clothes.
The next moment... the sound of rustling leaves reached his ears.
After that, the smell of old, damp wood, along with the scent of unknown plants, filled the space around him.
In the distance, the sounds of creatures could be heard that had no resemblance to the monsters of the Ruined Realm.
Some sounds were like singing, some others were more like roars, and some were so strange that it was impossible to tell what creature they belonged to.
Lian calmly opened his eyes and at that same moment... for a few seconds, his mind was unable to process what he was seeing.
"My god... what the hell is this place?"
He was standing on a branch.
No... on a tree, but only a few seconds were enough for him to realize he was wrong.
This... was not a tree at all... at least... not what humans called a tree.
The branch beneath his feet was so wide that if one of the capital’s main and large streets was built on it, there would still be empty space on both sides.
The surface of the branch was not completely smooth.
Its bark, like an ancient rock, was full of massive cracks and stone-like protrusions.
In these same cracks, mosses had grown, some of which were taller than multi-story buildings.
Other plants were also living on that same branch.
Shrubs with green leaves and flowers the size of a carriage, and roots of plants that moved like massive snakes on the tree’s bark and sank back into it.
If someone without knowing the truth saw this place... they would probably imagine they had entered an unknown forest.
But that entire forest... had grown on just one branch.
Lian took a deep breath, just one branch of this tree alone was larger and more massive than any structure he had ever seen in his life.
In front of such greatness, one could only feel emptiness and worthlessness.
His eyes calmly scanned the surroundings, he had not yet grasped the true size of this tree.
But his instinct was screaming... this place was different from everything he had seen until today.
He decided to follow the path of the branch.
Every step made a dry sound from under his shoes, the wind was constantly blowing among the giant leaves, even the wind’s power alone was so strong that it could move him with one gust.
After walking a few hundred meters... his steps suddenly stopped.
His eyes slowly widened, in front of him, there was something that at first glance looked more like the remains of an abandoned city.
Thousands of massive branches were stacked on top of each other, some as thick as several buildings, and some so large that dozens of houses could be built on them.
The branches were arranged in a complex and tangled way; as if an unknown architect had carefully placed them together.
Lian looked for a few moments, then slowly whispered.
"A nest?"
At first glance, everything was so massive that it was impossible to guess what this place exactly was.
But with a look at the structure, it reminded him of birds’ nests, only on an unimaginably larger scale... much larger...
He carefully moved forward, the closer he got... the more he realized its greatness, and when he passed through the first branches... he again felt how small he was.
Every branch inside this nest was thicker than the watchtowers of Base #9.
Feathers had fallen among the branches, but they could no longer be called feathers.
Each one was the size of a warship, golden veins on them were still shining under the light.
Despite the passage of time, no signs of decay could be seen.
A few steps away, bones could be seen, bones that did not belong to any familiar creature.
A skull taller than a three-story building, a tooth as long as the trunk of a normal tree.
A claw that, if placed on the ground, could crush several cars at the same time.
Lian stood next to one of those bones, if he compared himself to it, he was not even the size of an ant.
He understood the true meaning of the word "gigantic" here, every other creature and thing that had ever called itself giant looked like an ant compared to anything that was here.
In the center of the nest... four eggs were placed.
Lian involuntarily stepped forward a few steps, each egg was between thirty to fifty meters tall.
The shell of one was silver-white, another was golden-colored, the third was dark blue, and the fourth was a combination of white and gold.
Their surfaces were not completely smooth, veins, like shining rivers, were moving on the shells.
Every few seconds, a gentle light passed through the eggs, as if something was breathing in their depths.
Lian stared at them without moving for a few minutes.
His mind was full of questions, finally, he quietly whispered under his breath.
"...What kind of monster’s nest is this?"
If the eggs are this gigantic... then how big is their mother?
He felt a bad feeling, such a creature could probably crush him like an ant with just a random movement.
At that same moment, several blue windows appeared before his eyes.
[You have entered the Special Area.]
[Area Synchronization Complete.]
[Special Rules Applied.]
[Communication with the outside world has been blocked.]
[Survive.]
That was it.
There was no mission, no explanation, no map, no goal, and only...
"Survive."
This simplicity also had its own terror, now he practically had no goal in this small world, and to leave, he had to look for the key.
But if all the parts of this world were as gigantic as where he was now, he doubted finding the key would be easy.
Lian calmly closed the windows, an unpleasant feeling had formed in his heart, but unfortunately, there was nothing he could do.
This was his first experience in a Special Area, and he could only go with the flow and keep his guard up.
After a few minutes, he moved toward the edge of the branch, if he was going to go down, he had to find a way.
When he reached the edge, he calmly looked down.
There was nothing, only a sea of clouds, as far as the eye could see... clouds.
Lian frowned, he waited a few more seconds, at that same moment, a strong wind blew.
A layer of clouds slowly moved aside, and what was hidden behind it made him hold his breath for a moment.
The tree... had passed through the clouds, not just a little, but kilometers above, and the branch he was standing on was probably several kilometers from the ground.
But even now, the ground could not be seen.
Below... only fog and clouds could be seen, even the tree’s trunk could not be seen completely.
It was so massive that from Lian’s angle, only a part of its bark could be seen; a brown wall that, like an endless mountain range, continued into the depths of the darkness.
At that same moment... Lian understood a painful truth, he had no way to go down.
No rope, no rock, no other path, only a fall... that would probably last a long time, and he doubted he could survive it.
He didn’t even know what could be down there, anything could be down there!
"Maybe I can use the claws."
He thought for a moment, it was not like there was no way.
He could activate Glacial Reaper Claw and strike the claws into the tree trunk, with this, maybe he could go down safely.
But the question was whether it was possible?
Looking at the tree trunk, it seemed much too resistant for the claws to penetrate.
The wind suddenly became stronger, one of the giant feathers that was lying next to the nest moved slowly on the branch.
The sound of it rubbing against the wood was like a ship being dragged on the ground.
Then... a sound was heard.
Very far away, so far that it could be kilometers away.
But... that one sound... shook the entire air.
It was like the screech of a bird, but so massive... that even Lian’s bones vibrated with its tremor.
The small birds around all fled from among the branches and leaves at the same moment, it was clear that the owner of the nest was returning!
And this did not seem like a good thing at all...
The wind changed direction for a few seconds, Lian calmly turned his head and his gaze fixed on the four massive eggs.
He was silent for a few moments and then a bitter smile settled on his lips and he whispered under his breath.
"I just hope the owner of this nest is hospitable."
( The Nest’s Visualization )

chapters.title: Chapter 185: The Owner Returns
paragraphs: The sound of that massive screech was still echoing in Lian’s mind.
Although the sound had come from an unbelievable distance, the tremor it had created in the air was enough for him to fully understand one truth.
Whatever creature owned this nest was not something that could even be imagined fighting against.
Lian stepped back from the edge of the branch. He didn’t even look down again.
The first rule he had learned over years of training in schools slowly repeated in his mind.
"Before understanding the environment... do not move." In an unknown environment, rushing equals death.
Let alone the fact that the environment he was in at this moment was one he had never even seen a sample of in simulations.
Just a while ago, he had tested and trained in various environments in the academy’s simulations, exactly to prepare for conditions like this.
But the environment he was in now had no sample, he had not even thought of recreating and training in it himself.
He calmly scanned his surroundings to find a place to hide.
A few meters away, one of the giant feathers that had fallen inside the nest was leaning on a few large branches.
For the owner of this nest, it might have been just a fallen feather, but for Lian, it was a natural wall dozens of meters high.
Without making the slightest sound, he got behind it.
Then he sat cross-legged and took a deep breath.
"If the owner of this nest returns, the slightest mana leak or presence could expose me." He calmly closed his eyes.
And activated one of his skills.
The next moment, a very faint black aura, like a thin mist, came out of his body and settled back on his skin.
[Abyss Veil]
The black mist slowly twisted around his body, not thick enough to be seen.
Not so thin that it was ineffective.
Within seconds...
The feeling of mana presence that always flowed around his body almost disappeared.
Even he himself could barely feel the flow of his own mana, his breathing became quieter, and his heartbeat strangely slowed.
For a moment, he felt like part of this tree itself, as if his existence had merged with the surrounding space.
This skill had high mana consumption, but right now, safety was the most important thing for him, and only this skill could hide his presence in the best way.
However, there was one problem, he was not sure if he could hide from the monster that owned this nest, he did not know how powerful that monster was.
Abyss Veil could hide him even from a level 35 Fallen, but higher? He didn’t know, he had never tested it before.
He sighed and got up from his place, now that he had found a hiding spot, it was better to look around more to get familiar with this place.
Maybe he could find a way down or anything to help his current situation.
A few minutes later... Lian was moving calmly among the massive branches of the nest.
He took every step carefully, and the further he went, the more he felt he had entered a world with its own rules.
Aside from the greatness and magnitude of everything, the air and oxygen were working much stronger than normal, if he was a normal human, his lungs might have exploded due to the excess oxygen.
He could only endure it because of his physical strength.
A little further ahead, a skeleton was lying on a branch.
Lian stopped at that moment, the skull of that creature was the size of a two-story house, its ribs, like stone pillars, were scattered around.
Even after death, the majesty of that creature had not faded.
Lian calmly passed by the bones, a few meters ahead, he saw a piece of a broken eggshell.
Just one piece of it was thicker than their base’s walls, on its surface, traces of dried mana could still be seen.
A little further away, a claw mark could be seen on the tree’s bark.
He stood next to it, his entire body could easily fit inside one of the grooves of that same claw mark, he looked around for a few moments.
In silence, a question formed in his mind.
"...Is this whole world like this? Or is it just the area I landed in?"
This was a question that had come to his mind before.
But now it made him think about it more seriously.
He had seen large monsters until today, but here... everything was on a scale that was hard to even imagine.
Just one look at this nest showed that the creature living here was probably larger than any building Lian had ever seen in his life.
He first considered the possibility that only the nest and this monster were massive, but the skeletons he saw here belonged to different monsters, and they were also massive.
So he was getting more and more sure that maybe this entire world was gigantic.
Among one of the nest’s cracks, something caught his attention.
He carefully jumped down, moved a few branches aside, and then his eyes fixed for a moment.
Another skeleton, but this time almost intact, unlike the previous scattered bones, this creature was lying on the ground almost in the same state it had died in.
Its height was about fifteen meters, even after decay, one could tell it had once been a very powerful monster.
Lian calmly approached and touched one of its bones.
At that same moment, his eyes widened slightly, a wave of energy was still emanating from inside the bone, weak but completely noticeable.
"After all these years, there is still mana inside it?" He was no expert, but he could see that months or even years had passed since this monster’s death.
His gaze became serious, if this bone still had energy, its value was unimaginable.
Maybe armor could be made from it, maybe weapons, or even raw materials for making Artifacts, this was a bone that could hold mana.
Its value was definitely high, and in any case, no blacksmith would be willing to lose such a thing.
Lian glanced at his storage space and pulled out sharp B-rank knives made from monster horns.
Normally, they certainly couldn’t damage this bone, but if he used lightning power, the bone’s resistance would also be broken.
He struck one of the thinner bones a few times with gentle blows, the metal hit with a dry sound, and a few cracks appeared on the bone.
After a few minutes of effort, he finally managed to detach a piece about a meter long.
He gave a faint smile, with the help of storage space, the bone piece disappeared.
Then the second piece.
Third.
Fourth.
He only took pieces that were possible to carry, if he ever got out of this place alive, even these few pieces might be useful to him.
But at the same time, his mind was occupied with another question.
"If even a dead monster here is fifteen meters..."
"Then how can the threat level of this Special Area be logical for awakened ones below level twenty?"
The more he looked around, the less answer he found, he doubted that the federation had plotted or made a mistake.
So it was only possible that he had spawned in an extremely dangerous location.
At that same moment, the light around him suddenly dimmed.
"Huh? What happened?" Lian frowned, for a moment he thought a cloud had passed in front of the sun.
But... the wind... changed direction.
All the massive leaves around bent at the same time, the branch he was standing on began to tremble.
Not a small tremor, but a tremor as if a massive earthquake was occurring.
His eyes immediately looked up.
A shadow had covered the entire nest.
Suddenly, a terrible sense of danger overwhelmed his entire being, he felt death approaching, and without thinking, he returned to the hiding place he had found.
Drops of sweat settled on his forehead.
Then something passed over the top of the nest.
Not itself, just its shadow, a shadow so massive that it started from one side of the horizon and continued to the other.
For a few seconds, all the surrounding light disappeared... then the tip of a claw passed over the top of the nest.
Lian only saw that one claw, but that was enough, each of its fingers was larger than the tall buildings of Capital
Its nails, like curved mountains, were shining under the sunlight, he still could not see the creature’s body.
Only...
He heard the sound of its wings flapping, every time its wings moved, the clouds in the sky split apart.
Massive air currents, like storms, passed through the tree’s branches.
He didn’t even dare to breathe, his entire body remained motionless.
The owner of the house had returned!

The more he looked around, the less answer he found, he doubted that the federation had plotted or made a mistake.
So it was only possible that he had spawned in an extremely dangerous location.
At that same moment, the light around him suddenly dimmed.
"Huh?
What happened?" Lian frowned, for a moment he thought a cloud had passed in front of the sun.
But... the wind... changed direction.
All the massive leaves around bent at the same time, the branch he was standing on began to tremble.
Not a small tremor, but a tremor as if a massive earthquake was occurring.
His eyes immediately looked up.
A shadow had covered the entire nest.
Suddenly, a terrible sense of danger overwhelmed his entire being, he felt death approaching, and without thinking, he returned to the hiding place he had found.
Drops of sweat settled on his forehead.
Then something passed over the top of the nest.
Not itself, just its shadow, a shadow so massive that it started from one side of the horizon and continued to the other.
For a few seconds, all the surrounding light disappeared... then the tip of a claw passed over the top of the nest.
Lian only saw that one claw, but that was enough, each of its fingers was larger than the tall buildings of Capital
Its nails, like curved mountains, were shining under the sunlight, he still could not see the creature’s body.
Only...
He heard the sound of its wings flapping, every time its wings moved, the clouds in the sky split apart.
Massive air currents, like storms, passed through the tree’s branches.
He didn’t even dare to breathe, his entire body remained motionless.
The owner of the house had returned!

chapters.title: Chapter 186: Giant Sky Bird
paragraphs: Lian did not even dare to move.
His entire body was hidden, and Abyss Veil was active at maximum power, mana was quickly leaving his body.
But he did not even think about turning off the skill, in such a place, only one mistake was equal to death.
He did not remember the last time he had been forced to hide like this, in fact, he did not remember at all that he had ever needed to hide.
Even against the Dreadmaw Sovereign, although he was in a very bad situation, he had not chosen the option of hiding and had gone straight into the danger.
But the current situation was so bad that anything other than hiding was pure suicide.
Suddenly, the entire tree trembled.
Not just the branch he was standing on, but the entire giant tree...
A deep tremor rose from the depths of the trunk and moved its countless branches one after another, leaves that were each the size of a house, shook from the intensity of the tremor.
At that same moment, a sound like thunder, but continuous and regular, was heard from the sky.
Wooooooom...
Wooooooom...
Wooooooom...
Every time that sound repeated, the air pressure changed.
The clouds above the tree, like a white cloth, split in the middle.
Massive wind currents passed through the branches and moved the giant feathers around the nest.
Lian slowly raised his head, at first he only saw the shadow.
A shadow that covered the entire nest.
Then... two wings, wings so massive that their ends were lost among the clouds.
Every time it flapped its wings, masses of clouds were pushed hundreds of meters away.
Then the claws appeared, claws covered with black scales, curved and shiny nails, like spears of black metal, shining under the sunlight.
A few moments later, two bright golden eyes became visible from among the clouds.
Eyes that each were larger than the capital’s central square, their vertical pupils were calmly scanning the surroundings.
Lian felt that if that creature’s gaze fell on him just once, he would not even have time to think.
And finally, its entire body became visible.
He held his breath, that bird’s body was several hundred meters long.
The distance between its two wings was several kilometers, its black feathers were shining under the light, like blades of polished metal.
Even its feathers were larger than humans, its massive beak was covered with natural golden lines; runes that seemed to have been carved on it from the moment of birth.
No creature that Lian had seen until today could even compare to one finger of this monster.
At that same moment, a blue window appeared before his eyes.
[Species: Giant Sky Bird]
[Level: 50]
[Rank: Fallen]
Only that, but those three lines made Lian’s body freeze.
Level 50.
Until today, the highest creature he had seen was not even close to such a number.
He involuntarily thought to himself, level 16, against level 50, a gap that was impossible to even imagine.
For a more precise comparison, this monster is even more powerful than the Dreadmaw Sovereign, which was an Unholy, without a doubt, this giant monster is the most powerful monster he had ever seen.
Today, just being able to survive would be an achievement in itself...
The massive bird calmly opened its left claw, and three objects fell from its grip.
Almost like three small rocks, but they were not rocks, they fell with a muffled sound on the nest’s branches.
Lian sharpened his gaze, three living creatures, all of them were covered from head to toe in a clear and sticky liquid that was the bird’s saliva.
A thick liquid that, like spider webs, had stuck their hands and feet together.
Every small movement stretched the elastic strands of saliva more, escaping was impossible.
Without even looking at them, the bird gently pushed the three toward the eggs with its massive beak.
A completely normal movement, like a human putting food in the refrigerator to eat later.
It had not kept them for itself, but for its chicks, it had brought fresh and living food.
Lian felt a coldness rise up his spine, this creature did not even bother to kill its prey, and if he got caught, he would have exactly the same fate.
Now he could see those three more clearly.
Two females and one male, their height was almost equal to humans, but they were not human.
Their skin was like human skin, but a long tail, resembling a lizard, had come out from the back of their bodies.
Two thin and segmented horns, like cricket antennae, had grown from both sides of their heads.

Six small eyes, arranged in two rows on their faces, and their pointed ears were constantly trembling with fear, and despite their different appearance, it was completely clear that they were intelligent creatures.
The massive bird looked at its eggs for a few moments, then calmly gathered its giant body inside the nest.
It laid its wings over its body, its golden eyes slowly closed.
Its breathing was heavy, and every inhale and exhale, like a massive storm blowing, shook the surrounding branches.
A few minutes later, one of those creatures said something.
But its language was completely unknown.
"Shir... Aka... Neri..."
Lian did not understand even one word, but at that same moment another notification appeared.
[Translation Active.]
Immediately, the next voice became understandable for him.
"...We... are going to die..." the first girl said with a trembling voice.
"Calm down..." the boy answered calmly, was silent for a few seconds, and then slowly continued.
"If it thinks we are awake... it will eat us sooner..."
The second girl lowered her head, her voice was so quiet that it could barely be heard.
Silence covered everything again, none of them were crying, they were just terrified, a terror mixed with the shock of people who knew they would soon die.
About an hour passed.
The massive bird was still asleep, its breathing had become regular, those three would occasionally talk quietly with each other.
Sometimes they would whisper unknown prayers under their breath, sometimes they would examine escape routes.
But there was no way, death was on every side.
Lian was looking at them in silence, his mind was stuck between two choices, should he communicate with them or not?
There was no doubt that these three were from the native and intelligent species of this small world, or more precisely, the Special Area.
They had the ability to speak, think, and reason, and even their body structure had similarities to humans.
Although they had features of lizards, crickets, and spiders, but aside from that, they were clearly intelligent and smart species like humans.
And this meant they could be a very large source of information.
If he showed himself, they might scream in fear, if they screamed, everyone would die.
But if he did nothing, he would lose his only clue about this strange world.
He calmly let out his breath, his gaze fixed on those three creatures again.
"If these are really intelligent creatures like humans, maybe they are the only ones who can tell me something about this world." He needed information to find a way out of this hell.
Lian looked at the massive bird once more, its eyes were still closed, its breathing was deep and heavy.
He made his decision and calmly moved toward them...
( Giant Sky Bird’s Visualization )

chapters.title: Chapter 187: The Lacerians
paragraphs: His gaze remained fixed on the giant bird, and only the sound of that creature’s heavy breathing broke the silence of the nest.
Every inhale, like a massive storm, bent the surrounding branches.
Every exhale sent masses of mist through the nest and made the giant feathers dance.
Without taking his eyes off the monster, Lian counted the time in his mind.
One...
Two...
Three...
With each exhale, the wind was pushed outward, and right after that, a few seconds of silence followed.
Only those few seconds, that short gap, were enough for the sound of his steps to be lost in the roar of the wind.
Sometimes the line between life and death was only one step, and sometimes only one breath, exactly like now.
Lian slowly came out of his hiding place, he had made his decision to reveal himself and talk to those three, but to reach them, he had to maintain caution.
It is true that his concealment skill was still active, but he did not want to take any risks, and it was better to move carefully to eliminate any risk.
At that same moment, the bird’s next exhale filled the surrounding space.
He moved.
Three steps, stop, silence again, move again, each time, his body clung to the shadows.
Even Abyss Veil was still active and had reduced his presence to almost zero.
A few minutes later, he was only a few meters away from those three captives, they still had not noticed his presence, all their attention was on the bird that was sleeping a few steps away.
Of course, they still could not see him, Lian had already checked their information and realized that they were from a species called Lacerians, and all three of them were below level 20.
They posed no threat to him, so there was no need to worry, if something went wrong, he could kill them in the blink of an eye.
And then he deactivated his skill.
At that same time, one of the girls quietly raised her head, and her eyes fixed on Lian.
All six of her eyes opened at the same time, fear surged across her entire face, her mouth opened, she was about to scream.
But before that, Lian placed his index finger in front of his lips.
"Quiet." His gaze was completely calm, and just that, one word, neither loud nor quiet, but so firm that the girl froze at that moment.
The boy also quickly turned his head, when he saw Lian, his body tensed, fear also surged on his face.
As if he was looking at another monster.
Even though his hands and feet were still trapped in the sticky saliva, he pulled himself forward and placed himself between Lian and the two girls.
His body was trembling, he was scared, but he did not step back, and with a voice that could barely be heard, he said.
"...Please..." His throat was dry, it took a few moments for him to continue.
"If... if you want to kill us..." His gaze fell for a moment on the two girls behind him.
"...Just kill me."
Lian was silent for a few seconds, there was fear in that boy’s eyes, but more than fear, a kind of habit could be seen, as if this was not the first time he was facing death.
And more importantly, even though he was scared, he had no problem sacrificing his life to protect his sisters.
This was an admirable act, not everyone could put others’ lives above their own in such a tense atmosphere that smelled of death.
Lian calmly let out his breath.
"If I wanted to kill you, you would already be dead."
Without waiting for a reaction, he knelt down and pulled out his knife.
The boy immediately tensed up, but the blade did not land on his body, it sank into the sticky strands of saliva.
Lian carefully cut the thick strands, the elastic liquid separated with a quiet sound.
The boy’s right hand was freed, then the other hand, then his legs, the boy just stared at his freed hands for a few moments.
As if he still could not believe it, he had been freed? This strange creature had saved him and his sisters?
Lian, without speaking, went to one of the girls, a few more cuts, and she was also freed.
The third one too.
The three of them just stared at him, fear was still in their eyes, but now surprise had also been added to it.
They had not lowered their guard, but they seemed ready to form a relationship of trust and familiarity.
"...What... What are you?" The first girl said quietly.
But she did not finish her sentence, Lian put his knife away into his storage space.
"I saved you, so first you have to answer my questions, tell me about yourselves and your species." There was no time to waste.
Any moment, that monster could wake up, and his only chance to get information and find a way out would be lost, so he went straight to the point.
The three looked at each other, a few seconds of silence followed, and finally, the same boy answered.

"We are from the Lacerian species, one of the three lizard species of the Forest of Giants, because of the drought, food has become scarce, and we came out to find something to eat, but that giant bird caught us."
Lian looked directly into their eyes, so the place he was in was called the Forest of Giants, with what he was seeing, such a thing seemed normal.
But the concept of three lizard species intrigued him a little.
"So giant monsters are common in this forest? If so, why do creatures as small as you live around here?"

"We have no choice... the only place where there is still water is the three forests that receive rivers from the Forgotten Tree... the other two forests are dangerous for us, at least here, as long as we are at home, the giants do not come after us."
’The Forgotten Tree? Water shortage? And three forests, huh?’ He got a general view of this small world’s structure.
But he still did not have enough information, he needed to hear more about the lizard species, the other two forests, and even this Forest of Giants.
The rest of his group members were probably somewhere in one of the three forests, and if his guess was correct, contrary to what this boy said, the other two forests should be safer for them.
Also, those two forests could be the reason why the federation had not assessed the threat level of this Special Area as that high.
And only he had been unlucky enough to spawn in the most dangerous place from the start.
’Is it really fair that I always fall into the most dangerous places?’ He sighed.
"...You... came from outside?" While Lian was thinking, the boy asked with a little hesitation.
Lian did not answer, but looked at them in surprise, and this silence and look were enough for them.
The first girl quietly moved her lips, her voice was more like a whisper.
"So... the legendary gate... has opened again..."
Then... no one said anything.
Even Lian, his mind was full of questions, did these three know about the rift? Did they know that there are places beyond their world? And how did they realize that he also came from outside?
And again? Does that mean this was not the first time the rift between the Special Area and the Ruined Realm had opened?
Had others from outside entered this world before? And if so... who? Could they have been natives?
Just as he was about to ask the next question...
A very quiet sound echoed in the nest.
Click... all four turned their heads at the same time.
One of the massive eggs had trembled, and on its white and golden shell, a very small crack had appeared.
Only a few centimeters, but for the four people standing there...
That same crack was terrifying! Because it could cause the giant bird to wake up!
Lian slowly turned his gaze toward the giant bird, its golden eyes were still closed.
Not much time remained until one of this bird’s chicks was born...
An event that can cause the awakening of the monster...
( The Lacerians’s Visualization )

chapters.title: Chapter 188: The Cycle Continues
paragraphs: The sound of the eggshell cracking, although very quiet, echoed like a massive rock breaking in the heavy silence of the nest.
All four of them remained motionless at that same moment, Lian did not even blink.
His gaze shifted between the white and golden egg and the giant bird that was sleeping on the other side of the nest.
The crack that had appeared on the shell was only a few centimeters long, but in such conditions, that same small crack could be the beginning of a disaster.
The Giant Sky Bird’s breathing became irregular for a few moments.
It took a deeper breath than before, and its massive chest rose. The airflow passed through its black feathers with power and dragged a few loose feathers around the nest across the branch’s surface.
Then one of its claws moved slightly.
Its black and curved nail scraped against the wood and a rough and heavy sound echoed throughout the nest; a sound like a massive blade being dragged on stone.
The three Lacerians held their breath at the same time.
The younger girl involuntarily wrapped her long tail around her legs and tightly closed her six eyes.
The boy slightly moved his body forward, as if even in such conditions, he wanted to place himself between his two sisters and the bird.
Lian just watched, a few seconds passed, the bird did not raise its head, its golden eyes remained closed, and after a few irregular breaths, its breathing became calm and deep again.
The crack on the egg also did not grow larger.
It was clear that the monster could feel any crack on the egg, as if there was some kind of mechanism between the mother and the child.
The air trapped in the three Lacerians’ lungs was slowly released.
Lian waited a few more moments and then, after making sure nothing worse had happened, took his gaze off the egg.
During the previous short conversation, he had learned the names of all three; not because they had formally introduced themselves, but because when they spoke, they called each other by name.
The boy’s name was Ravian.
The older girl, who seemed calmer than the other two and even in the peak of fear tried to remain logical, was named Sera.
The younger girl was Nemi; the same girl who, from the moment she fell into the nest, had shown the most fear and still kept looking at the bird every few seconds.
Lian registered these three names in his mind, if he wanted to get information from them and possibly stay with them for a while, it was better to at least know their names.

"A few moments ago, you said the gate has opened again. Does that mean creatures from outside have entered this world before?" He asked without any extra introduction, with a voice so low that it did not go beyond a few meters.
He needed information, the more information the better, only this way could he get familiar with this small world and find his way.
Ravian did not answer immediately.
His six eyes turned toward Sera for a moment.
That brief look showed that he himself was not sure if he should talk about such a matter with a stranger or not.
They had just seen this stranger and had no knowledge of him, and they had not heard good stories about Otherworldly ones until now.
But the reality was that this same stranger had saved all three of their lives.
A few seconds later, Ravian moved slightly closer to Lian so he would not have to raise his voice.
"We ourselves have never seen anyone who came from outside this world. Even the tribe elders only know stories.
"What stories?" Lian asked.
Ravian gave a brief look at the bird and then carefully continued:

"They say every twenty-five years, for a short time, a gate opens in one of the parts of the world. No one knows where it will appear, who opens it, or why it even opens. The only thing repeated in the legends is that creatures that do not belong to this world can pass through it."
"Some stories say they come from lands beyond the sky," Sera said quietly while keeping her gaze down.
"Places that have different suns and whose people live under skies with unknown colors." She paused for a moment and then added:

"But some other legends say strangers come from dead worlds; worlds whose rivers have dried up, whose cities have collapsed, and only war and monsters remain in them. No one knows which story is true."
Nemi, who had remained silent until then, quietly moved her lips.
"Our grandmother said whenever the gate opens, strangers bring war with them. She said some of them come to save this world and some others come to destroy it."
Ravian immediately gave her a warning look, Nemi understood she had said more than she should and fell silent again.
But Lian was no longer looking at them, only one number was repeating in his mind.
Twenty-five years.
Every Ruined Realm also appeared in their world in twenty-five-year cycles.
From the moment each realm appeared, humans had twenty-five years to complete its main mission, obtain the necessary crystals, and close the path of monster invasion.
If they failed, the wall between the two worlds would collapse, and the monsters of that realm would invade Earth.
And now, the native creatures of this world were also speaking of a gate that opened every twenty-five years.
’This can’t be a coincidence.’ Lian was completely silent for a few moments.
The gate’s opening cycle in this world was exactly the same as the Ruined Realms’ appearance cycle.
But what could that mean? Was every Ruined Realm truly an independent world that temporarily connected to Earth?
Had this realm experienced similar cycles before humans entered?
Or maybe there was something behind all these twenty-five-year cycles; a being, a power, or a law that connected different worlds at specific times.
Lian’s gaze passed over the nest and fell on the endless branches that were lost among the clouds.
He had no answer.
But he considered the possibility that the appearance of realms on Earth was not a natural or accidental disaster.
Maybe something was choosing them.
Maybe something, every twenty-five years, opened specific gates between worlds.
And if that was the case, the main question was not why the Ruined Realms connected to Earth.
The main question was who or what benefited from this connection.
Could it be the work of the system known as The Will? The same system that gave them classes, talents, and skills?
Was its purpose to destroy worlds? Or to save them? These were questions that, after 9 Ruined Realms, still had no answers.
Lian temporarily put these thoughts aside.
The current information was not enough to reach a conclusion, and drowning in guesses, especially in the nest of a Fallen Level 50, was not a wise thing to do.
"You said this place is called the Forest of Giants. How big is this forest?" He asked a few moments later.
Ravian slowly shook his head.
"We don’t know. None of our people have gone to its end. Even the tribe’s most skilled hunters, who have been away from home for weeks, still haven’t been able to find the forest’s border."
"So you have no map of the entire forest?" Lian raised an eyebrow slightly.

"Only of the areas near the tribe. The hunters record the river routes, monster lairs, and the borders of known territories, but the further you go from the tribe, the more incomplete the maps become. Some areas have never been placed on any map, because whoever went there, never returned."
Lian gave a brief look at the Giant Sky Bird, considering what he had seen, the reason for this was not very strange.
If every monster in this forest was that gigantic, it was natural that not everyone could freely explore in such a hell.
The danger level was so high that no sane human would dare to do such a thing, and then he asked.
"And the other two forests?"

"To the south, there is the Emberroot Forest. The soil there is always warm, and some parts of the ground even smoke during rain. The tree roots absorb fire energy, and most of its plants are either poisonous or burn when you touch them."

"The monsters of Emberroot are usually not as large as the giants of this forest, but they are faster and more deadly. Some of them have poisons that our healers don’t even know the names of, and some others can throw fire from a distance."
"And the third forest?" Lian asked, from the description, the southern forest did not seem to be more terrifying and dangerous than the Forest of Giants.
At least he did not have that feeling about it.
"To the east, there is the Glassthorn Forest. Its trees grow from a glass-like material, but harder than ordinary glass." This time Sera spoke.
"Their branches are so sharp they can break bone armor, and if there is a storm, pieces of branches scatter in the air like hundreds of blades."
"At night, the entire forest glows. Mana moves inside the roots and crystals, and from a distance, it looks like the ground is full of stars." Nemi completed the explanation.

For a brief moment, a trace of excitement could be seen in Nemi’s voice, as if she loved that forest, but as soon as the sound of the bird’s breath echoed in the nest again, that excitement disappeared.
"And all three forests get water from the Forgotten Tree?" Lian then went to the main topic.
Which seemed to be the deepest and most central point of this small world.

And in forest areas, according to experiences and recorded information, keys are always in the deepest and most central point, in other words, when he finally wanted to leave this place, he probably had to go there.
Ravian nodded.
"Yes. The main rivers come out from the roots of the Forgotten Tree and then split among the three forests. Some rivers flow on the surface, and some pass under the roots."

"When the flow of the Forgotten Tree’s rivers weakens, all three forests slowly dry up. Hunting decreases, plants die, and monsters come closer to other territories to find food. That is exactly what is happening now."
Lian looked for a moment at the massive tree they were standing on.
Its trunk was so wide that even from this height, he could not see its full curve.
The branch the nest was on was alone several times wider than Base #9’s main streets.
"Is this Forgotten Tree even larger than this tree?" He asked.
All three nodded at almost the same time, and Sera said.
"No. This is only one of the large trees of the Forest of Giants, compared to the Forgotten Tree, it is like a newly born tree..."
"Just one of the large trees?" Lian was silent for a few moments.

All four of them remained motionless at that same moment, Lian did not even blink.
His gaze shifted between the white and golden egg and the giant bird that was sleeping on the other side of the nest.
The crack that had appeared on the shell was only a few centimeters long, but in such conditions, that same small crack could be the beginning of a disaster.

chapters.title: Chapter 189: A Civilization Among Giants
paragraphs: "That’s right, all the trees in this forest are this massive, some might even be larger." Sera said as if it were a normal matter.
Of course, for them it was a normal thing, they had grown up here and such trees were normal for them, but not for Lian.
"The Forgotten Tree is much farther and larger than anything you can see from here. Even the mountains near its roots look small compared to its trunk." Ravian answered with a more serious tone.
"You’ve seen it yourselves?"
Ravian shook his head.
"No. Only the old Elders and some hunters from past generations have gone as far as the main rivers. None of them reached the tree itself."
Sera added.
"Some say if someone reaches the highest point of the Forgotten Tree, they can see all three forests from above. They even say from there you can see the edge of the world."
"And no one has tried?" Lian asked, from its description, this tree seemed like the heart of this world.
"Many people have tried. None of them returned." Ravian made a very short and joyless laugh.
Lian looked again at the branch beneath his feet.
The tree he was now standing on was so massive that a bird several hundred meters long had built a nest on it and placed four giant eggs inside it.
However, for the people of this world, such a tree was considered just one of the large trees of the Forest of Giants.
If the Forgotten Tree really was even larger than this, imagining its dimensions was difficult even for Lian, then he asked after a few moments.

"You said you are one of the three lizard species of this region. How exactly do you live? Is your tribe just a few houses, or something larger?" He had obtained the necessary information about the Forgotten Tree.
Now it was time to understand the civilizations of this world and their level of development and advancement.

"Our tribe is not small. Several hundred families live there. We built our homes among the roots of a Stone Tree; a tree whose bark and roots are almost as hard as stone." Ravian answered this time without hesitation.
"The roots of that tree naturally formed a large ring, and our people built homes, storage, and workshops among those roots. There are also wooden and stone walls around the tribe."
"Against these monsters, do wooden walls really help?" Lian asked, he couldn’t imagine any civilization surviving in this forest.
Ravian gave a brief look at the Giant Sky Bird.

"Against something like that, no. But the giants usually don’t come close to the tribe’s location. The walls are for smaller monsters, hunting packs, and creatures that come looking for food at night."
"Do you have farming?"
Sera nodded.
"Yes, but not much. Near the river, we grow root fungi, swamp grains, and a few resilient plants. Most of our food comes from hunting, fishing, and gathering forest fruits."

"Each family usually does several tasks, but we also have specific groups. Hunters find food outside the tribe, guards protect the walls, craftsmen make weapons and tools, and healers treat the wounded."
Lian’s gaze moved over their equipment.
Their tools were not primitive, but they also didn’t resemble the federation’s industrial equipment.
Their light armors were made of several layers of monster leather, reinforced with bone plates on sensitive parts of the body.
These parts were connected with root-like strings, and on some of them, small and complex marks were carved.
This showed that their craftsmanship was not bad, but not at the level of theirs, and it seemed they could also use runes...
"Are these marks for directing mana?" Lian asked, pointing at them.
"You can understand that?" Ravian looked at him with real surprise.
"Just guessed." Of course he could guess, guessing about it wasn’t hard.
Runes were magical symbols that contained various powers, and craftsmen gave them different but limited powers by inscribing them on armors and weapons.

"The craftsmen carve marks on weapons to make mana flow through them more easily. Some marks make the blade harder, some make the weapon stay sharp longer, and some are used to store a small amount of mana." Sera said.
"Don’t you have metal?" Lian asked, because it seemed their equipment was made of leather and at best bone.
"We do, but very little. Most metals are either found in the territory of dangerous monsters or have to be extracted from stones that are hard for us to break." Ravian said and sighed.
"That’s why metal is usually only used in important tools, the tips of strong spears, or the guards’ weapons."
"And your government system? Do you have a tribe chief?"
"We have a Chief, but he doesn’t make important decisions alone. There are five Elders who decide about war, water, migration, trade, and punishments." Ravian nodded.

"The Chief is the commander of the hunters and guards, but if most Elders disagree with his decision, he can’t force the people. The Mother Healer also has a separate position, and even the Chief can’t interfere in the healers’ work." Sera added.
Lian looked at them, they had an organized civilization, not at the level of the complex and advanced civilizations of their world, but still a civilization.
But this still made him curious to know how these civilizations trained their forces and soldiers? Did they have an academy system like them?
He had become so engrossed in curiosity about a new civilization that he had completely forgotten the main topic.
"How do they train?"

"When they reach the age of seven warm seasons, training begins. First, we learn to recognize tracks, identify poisonous plants, memorize river routes, and hide when monsters approach." This time Nemi answered cautiously.

"Then, those who have more mana are trained according to their talent. Some become hunters, some healers, some craftsmen, and some guards. Not everyone needs to fight, but every person must be able to defend themselves in times of danger." Sera continued.
"Do you also know how to write?"

"Yes. The tribe’s history, river routes, territorial borders, and main laws are recorded on wooden tablets or dried skins. Most people can read simple signs, but old writings are only understood by the Elders and memory keepers." Ravian said.
Lian nodded calmly, their civilization was not backward.

They did not have industrial cities, machines, or advanced technology, but they had built an organized society. They had limited farming, group hunting, mana weapon crafting, division of labor, a governing structure, and a written language.
For a species living among giant monsters, this level of progress was remarkable.
After a few moments, Lian turned his head toward the edge of the nest, beyond the branch, only clouds could be seen.
No ground was visible, no tree trunk, and no way down.
Even though he wanted to learn more and more about this civilization, he had to return to the main topic, and he asked.
"Is there a way down from here?"
The three Lacerians just stared at him for a moment.
Ravian said with an expression that seemed to say the answer should be completely obvious:
"There is no way."
Lian raised his eyebrow slightly, he had expected this answer, and it seemed these three were also hopeless, he had to think for himself.
Sera explained more quietly:

"No one can survive a fall from such a height. Even if you find a way not to fall, many flying creatures live among the lower branches. Some of them are small, but they can smell blood and fear from a great distance."
"From the moment this bird caught us, we knew our fate was sealed. We didn’t expect to get out of here alive." Ravian looked around the nest, fear was clear in his tone.
But it was still clear that he had also accepted his fate and knew there was no way out...
"I understand." Lian sighed briefly.
From the moment he had seen the tree’s true height, he had understood that normal descent was almost impossible.
There was no rope of the necessary length, no clear path on the trunk or branches.
And even if he could climb down the tree’s surface, moving at such a height and through the territory of flying creatures without attracting attention was difficult.
But one path being impossible didn’t mean all paths were nonexistent.
Lian was still sure there had to be a way.
Before thinking about it, he asked another question, and his gaze fixed on the bird’s massive body.
"Is this Giant Sky Bird the most powerful monster in this part of the forest?"
For a few seconds, Ravian was completely silent, then a very faint smile appeared on his face, and Sera also, despite their deadly situation, made a short and quiet laugh.
That laugh was not out of mockery, it was more like the reaction of someone who had heard a question very far from reality.
"Of course not. This bird is powerful in its own territory in the sky, but it doesn’t even dare to go far from its nest and hunting grounds." Ravian said.
"Why?" Lian’s eyes narrowed slightly, if a Fallen level 50 is not the strongest in this forest, then how the hell did the federation allow awakened ones below level 20 to enter?
The smile disappeared from Ravian’s face.

"Because in this forest, every powerful monster has its own territory. They mark their borders with smell, mana, sound, or the corpses of their prey. Most of them don’t cross their territory borders even when food is scarce."
"They’re afraid of the other monsters?"
"Not exactly." Sera answered with a lower voice.
She paused for a few moments, her six eyes unconsciously turned toward the distance, somewhere behind the wall of clouds.
"They might fight each other. One of them might be stronger and take over another’s territory. But the main reason they don’t go far from their own territory is not fear of each other."
Sera pressed her lips together, and Ravian lowered his gaze, Nemi wrapped her tail tighter around her legs, and all six of her eyes trembled for a moment.
"Because they might encounter it." The surrounding air became heavier for a moment.
Even the sound of the Giant Sky Bird’s breathing no longer seemed as important as before.
"What is it?" Lian asked immediately, he couldn’t understand why these three were speaking so fragmented.
No one answered, Ravian fixed his gaze on the nest’s surface, and Sera avoided looking at Lian.
Nemi unconsciously placed both her hands on the antennae above her head, as if even hearing the question frightened her.
"It’s better not to ask its name." A few seconds later, Ravian only said.
"You don’t know its name, or you don’t want to say it?"
"It doesn’t matter, just it’s better not to ask its name..." Sera raised her head, this time fear was visible in all six of her eyes.
