"We have a Chief, but he doesn’t make important decisions alone.
There are five Elders who decide about war, water, migration, trade, and punishments." Ravian nodded.
"The Chief is the commander of the hunters and guards, but if most Elders disagree with his decision, he can’t force the people.
The Mother Healer also has a separate position, and even the Chief can’t interfere in the healers’ work." Sera added.
Lian looked at them, they had an organized civilization, not at the level of the complex and advanced civilizations of their world, but still a civilization.
But this still made him curious to know how these civilizations trained their forces and soldiers?
Did they have an academy system like them?
He had become so engrossed in curiosity about a new civilization that he had completely forgotten the main topic.
"How do they train?"
"When they reach the age of seven warm seasons, training begins.
First, we learn to recognize tracks, identify poisonous plants, memorize river routes, and hide when monsters approach." This time Nemi answered cautiously.
"Then, those who have more mana are trained according to their talent.
Some become hunters, some healers, some craftsmen, and some guards.
Not everyone needs to fight, but every person must be able to defend themselves in times of danger." Sera continued.
"Do you also know how to write?"
"Yes.
The tribe’s history, river routes, territorial borders, and main laws are recorded on wooden tablets or dried skins.
Most people can read simple signs, but old writings are only understood by the Elders and memory keepers." Ravian said.
Lian nodded calmly, their civilization was not backward.
They did not have industrial cities, machines, or advanced technology, but they had built an organized society.
They had limited farming, group hunting, mana weapon crafting, division of labor, a governing structure, and a written language.
For a species living among giant monsters, this level of progress was remarkable.
After a few moments, Lian turned his head toward the edge of the nest, beyond the branch, only clouds could be seen.
No ground was visible, no tree trunk, and no way down.
Even though he wanted to learn more and more about this civilization, he had to return to the main topic, and he asked.
"Is there a way down from here?"
The three Lacerians just stared at him for a moment.
Ravian said with an expression that seemed to say the answer should be completely obvious:
"There is no way."
Lian raised his eyebrow slightly, he had expected this answer, and it seemed these three were also hopeless, he had to think for himself.
Sera explained more quietly:
"No one can survive a fall from such a height.
Even if you find a way not to fall, many flying creatures live among the lower branches.
Some of them are small, but they can smell blood and fear from a great distance."
"From the moment this bird caught us, we knew our fate was sealed.
We didn’t expect to get out of here alive." Ravian looked around the nest, fear was clear in his tone.
But it was still clear that he had also accepted his fate and knew there was no way out...
"I understand." Lian sighed briefly.
From the moment he had seen the tree’s true height, he had understood that normal descent was almost impossible.
There was no rope of the necessary length, no clear path on the trunk or branches.
And even if he could climb down the tree’s surface, moving at such a height and through the territory of flying creatures without attracting attention was difficult.
But one path being impossible didn’t mean all paths were nonexistent.
Lian was still sure there had to be a way.
Before thinking about it, he asked another question, and his gaze fixed on the bird’s massive body.
"Is this Giant Sky Bird the most powerful monster in this part of the forest?"
For a few seconds, Ravian was completely silent, then a very faint smile appeared on his face, and Sera also, despite their deadly situation, made a short and quiet laugh.
That laugh was not out of mockery, it was more like the reaction of someone who had heard a question very far from reality.
"Of course not.
This bird is powerful in its own territory in the sky, but it doesn’t even dare to go far from its nest and hunting grounds." Ravian said.
"Why?" Lian’s eyes narrowed slightly, if a Fallen level 50 is not the strongest in this forest, then how the hell did the federation allow awakened ones below level 20 to enter?
The smile disappeared from Ravian’s face.
"Because in this forest, every powerful monster has its own territory.
They mark their borders with smell, mana, sound, or the corpses of their prey.
Most of them don’t cross their territory borders even when food is scarce."
"They’re afraid of the other monsters?"
"Not exactly." Sera answered with a lower voice.
She paused for a few moments, her six eyes unconsciously turned toward the distance, somewhere behind the wall of clouds.
"They might fight each other.
One of them might be stronger and take over another’s territory.
But the main reason they don’t go far from their own territory is not fear of each other."
Sera pressed her lips together, and Ravian lowered his gaze, Nemi wrapped her tail tighter around her legs, and all six of her eyes trembled for a moment.
"Because they might encounter it." The surrounding air became heavier for a moment.
Even the sound of the Giant Sky Bird’s breathing no longer seemed as important as before.
"What is it?" Lian asked immediately, he couldn’t understand why these three were speaking so fragmented.
No one answered, Ravian fixed his gaze on the nest’s surface, and Sera avoided looking at Lian.
Nemi unconsciously placed both her hands on the antennae above her head, as if even hearing the question frightened her.
"It’s better not to ask its name." A few seconds later, Ravian only said.
"You don’t know its name, or you don’t want to say it?"
"It doesn’t matter, just it’s better not to ask its name..." Sera raised her head, this time fear was visible in all six of her eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 190: Three Days to the Tribe
paragraphs: Their reaction had given him information more than any answer could.
This silence was not just the result of a simple superstition, and it made Lian think deeply and think more about the danger level of this Special Area.
He was powerful right now, he was stronger than any awakened one below level 20, even awakened ones and monsters up to level 25 could not match him.
If he used all his power, he could defeat normal monsters up to level 30 and maybe even 32.
In the entire history of awakened ones, there has been no known awakened one who, like him, had such a level of power at level 16.
But even now, he did not feel safe here at all.
Even a creature at the Fallen Level 50 did not dare to move freely in the Forest of Giants.
And based on that, the matter was even worse for him.
And there was something in this forest that the massive monsters kept their territories for, not just to control hunting grounds, but perhaps to stay away from it.
Lian did not know what that creature was, but for now, he preferred it to stay that way, not every truth needed to be discovered on the very first day.
"How far is your tribe from here?" He changed the subject after a few seconds.
Ravian thought for a moment.

"From where we went to find food to the tribe, it was about a day’s journey. But this bird brought us much further. We don’t know exactly where we are in its territory." He gave a brief look at the sun’s position and the wind’s direction.
"If we somehow get back to the ground and find the right path, at our normal speed, it might take us three days to reach the tribe."
"Is it definitely safe there?" Lian asked.

"Compared to here, yes. The tribe was built outside this Giant Sky Bird’s territory, and the walls are enough to handle smaller monsters." Ravian answered this time without hesitation and with a slight hint of pride.

"The large giants usually don’t come close to that area. Not because of us, but because the tribe is located on the border of several territories. The smell and mana of several large hunters interfere with each other in that area, and none of them are willing to stay there for long." Sera added.
"So you used a point that no monster fully owns." Lian said with admiration, this was a clever move.
Even though they were weak compared to the forest’s monsters, they had still managed to preserve their civilization with the intelligence and wisdom they had.
This was admirable ingenuity.

"Our elders say the tribe’s first Chief found that place after years of running. The area is not good for hunting, its soil is also not the best forest soil, but it is safe enough for people to survive." Sera nodded.
"And if one of the giants decides to enter it?"

"The guards will sound the root bells, and the people will enter the underground shelters. We cannot fight the real giants. The only thing we can do is hide and pray until they pass." Ravian answered.
Three days of travel, a relatively safe area, and hundreds of families who knew this world.
Maps of the rivers and surrounding territories, for now, their tribe was the best possible destination for Lian.
If the members of his group had appeared in this same forest, access to local information and the tribe’s maps could multiply his chances of finding them.

Of course, he doubted that everyone was as unlucky as him to appear in the most dangerous point from the start, and if they really were that unlucky, he doubted any of his group members could survive.
Maybe Rindo and Seraphina could have such a chance, but with his knowledge of the others, it seemed unlikely.
Even if they had landed in the Emberroot Forest or the Glassthorn Forest, the tribe’s people might know a way to communicate with the other species or cross the forest borders.
But one fundamental problem remained.
They were still thousands of meters above the ground, trapped in the nest of a Fallen Level 50.
And the egg that had cracked only a few minutes ago could hatch at any moment.
Lian wanted to ask another question about possible ways down, the smaller flying creatures, and the tribe’s tools, when suddenly a faint sound was heard from inside the egg.
This time it was not the sound of cracking.
It was a sound like a nail or a small beak scratching on the inner surface of the shell.
Khish... khish...
All four of them immediately fell silent, something from inside the egg struck the shell a few times.
Tap.
Tap.
Tap.
The visible crack trembled slightly, but still did not spread further, at that same moment, the Giant Sky Bird moved in its sleep.
Its massive head rose a few meters from the nest’s surface, all four of them almost simultaneously threw themselves flat on the branch’s surface.
Lian lowered his presence as much as possible, and Ravian pressed Nemi to the nest’s surface with both hands to keep her from moving out of fear.
One of the bird’s golden eyes opened, only to a narrow slit, a faint golden light shone from between its eyelids.
Its gaze slowly moved over the eggs, for a few seconds, that same eye remained fixed on the egg that had cracked.
Then its gaze passed across the nest’s surroundings, Lian remained completely still, he did not take a deep breath, did not blink, and did not allow the slightest wave of mana to leave his body.
Those three others were so terrified that they did not even dare to breathe, as if the gaze of death could fall on them at any moment and take their lives.
The bird’s golden eye remained open for a moment longer, then its eyelid lowered again.
Its head slowly rested on the edge of the nest, and its heavy breathing returned to normal after a few seconds.
But none of the four moved immediately, Lian waited for almost a full minute, and when he was sure the bird had fallen back asleep, he fixed his gaze on the crack on the egg.
The scratching sound from inside was still continuing softly.
Not much time remained.
After making sure the bird had fallen back asleep, they finally put aside their caution and breathed a sigh of relief.
"I’m scared... I want to go home." Nemi said, tears of fear streaming from her eyes, as she buried her head in her brother’s arms.
Ravian could only sigh, he couldn’t do anything and felt helpless...
"Before this egg hatches, I have to find a way to leave this nest." Lian thought without moving.
And this time, it was not just about his own survival.
Three guides were beside him who could lead him to the first civilization of this world.
If he wanted to find the answers to his questions, find his group members, and find the best opportunities for progress in this small world, he had to get all three of these natives out alive.
He had a feeling that the path to his first evolution was hidden in this world...

chapters.title: Chapter 191: The Crazy Plan
paragraphs: The sound of scratching from inside the egg was becoming clearer moment by moment.
Tap...
Khish...
Tap...
Every few minutes, the white crack on the shell would grow a little larger, and every time that sound echoed in the nest’s space, the hearts of all four people beat heavier than before.
Lian said nothing for a few moments, just silently looking around.
His mind was analyzing the situation with incredible speed. Climbing down the tree’s trunk was almost impossible.
Jumping was equal to suicide, even for him, the distance was so great that nothing of him would remain if he jumped.
Staying until the egg hatched meant becoming the chick’s first meal.
Killing the Giant Sky Bird? Even thinking about it was absurd.
In the end, only one conclusion remained, the only creature that could take them down from such a height was the monster itself.
But before any decision, he had to understand what these three people were capable of, to see if he could get any help from them or if he had to rely only on himself.
Lian fixed his gaze on Ravian.
"Before we decide about escaping, I need to know what each of you can do." He said in a quiet voice.
Ravian looked at him in surprise for a few moments.
In such a situation, he expected a stranger they had just met to be blindly looking for an escape out of fear.
But Lian was like a commander in the middle of a battlefield, examining all possibilities.
"I’m not looking for combat power. Any skill that helps with climbing down, hiding, or surviving... tell me right now." Lian said again.
The three looked at each other, the first was Ravian, he placed his hand on the rough surface of the branch.
Mana slowly flowed around his fingers, feet, and even his tail, a few moments later, it was as if his body was stuck to the branch’s surface.
Even when he pulled himself back with all his strength, his hand did not separate.
"The name of this skill is Root Grip." He continued with a low voice.

"I concentrate mana into my hands, feet, and tail. As long as I have mana, I can climb most trees or rocks, maintain my balance on narrow branches, or stick to some monsters’ bodies." Then he gave a bitter smile.

"But it only works for myself. If I have to carry the weight of several people, my mana will run out very quickly. It doesn’t work well on very smooth surfaces either, and if I use it too much, my hands and feet go numb for a few hours.
Lian’s gaze unconsciously fell on the Giant Sky Bird’s feathers, thick feathers, a suitable surface for sticking.
He said nothing, but registered that information in his mind, and the next person was Sera, she picked up a handful of dried moss from around the nest.
Mana flowed between her fingers, a few moments later, the plant fibers slowly intertwined and formed a thin but strong strand.
Sera pulled it, and the rope neither broke nor changed shape.
"Thread Sap." She explained.
"I combine my mana with plant sap and make strands that are lighter and more resistant than normal rope." She wrapped the strand around her wrist.
"They stick to rough surfaces, have a lot of flexibility, and can hold the weight of several people for a short time." Then she lowered her gaze.
"But I can’t use it without plants. It’s not very resistant to fire either, and if it stays for a long time, it dries out and becomes brittle."
Lian looked around, branches, moss, dry fibers, the necessary materials were everywhere.
Finally, Nemi stepped forward hesitantly.
"I... I don’t have combat skills." Her cheeks flushed slightly.
"But... maybe this will be useful here." She quietly closed her eyes, and weak mana spread around her body.
Lian suddenly noticed that the sound of leaves hitting the wind had become slightly weaker, even the sound of Ravian’s breathing was less audible.
"Quiet Pulse..." Nemi said.

"It only works for a few seconds, but it makes the small sounds and vibrations around me weaker. It doesn’t create complete silence... it just helps that no one notices our movements." She then added with embarrassment.
"Its range is very short... it also consumes a lot of mana."
Lian nodded calmly, contrary to his initial thought, all three skills were exactly what he needed for such a plan.

And with just one look, it was clear that all three of their skills were for hunting, survival, and exploration, and based on that, he could reason that most of their abilities should be skills related to the environment and their way of life.
Probably most of their tribe’s people also knew these same skills and they were spread among the people.
He started examining escape routes one by one. The first option was climbing down the tree’s trunk.
"If we get from the branch to the trunk, maybe with Root Grip I can climb down slowly." Ravian said.
Lian immediately shook his head.
"You might be able to climb down a few hundred meters." Then he pointed to the clouds beneath their feet.
"But we don’t even know how many thousand meters tall this tree is. Your mana will run out before you reach the ground." He paused for a moment.
"Besides, the lower branches are full of flying monsters."
Everyone fell silent. The first plan was rejected.
The second option was building a glider. Sera suggested that with the fallen feathers around the nest and Thread Sap, they might be able to make something like wings.
Lian lifted one of the massive feathers, its weight was several times more than he had imagined, he immediately let it go.
"These feathers weren’t made for us to fly with." He turned his gaze among the three.
"None of us have any flying experience either. One small mistake... is enough for us to fall straight down."
The second plan was also set aside, and Ravian, after thinking for a moment, said hesitantly.
"If we wait... maybe after the chick comes out..."
Lian didn’t even let him finish his sentence.
"A chick that has just hatched, the first thing it will do is eat us."
No one said anything more, and he fixed his gaze on the Giant Sky Bird again.
This time, not as an enemy, but as part of the plan, his initial goal was also to use the bird as help for going down.
He noticed that one of the bird’s claws was still bloody, the feathers under its belly were wet in some places, and its belly didn’t look very full either.

That meant it hadn’t brought the prey for itself, it had brought it for the chicks, and it would probably leave the nest again after resting to hunt or drink water, because clearly it hadn’t eaten anything itself either.
"Sky Birds don’t stay in the nest for long." At that same moment, Sera said quietly.
"How do you know?" Lian looked at her.
"The tribe’s hunters have seen them from a distance several times. When the chicks are still inside the eggs, they travel between their hunting territory and the nest several times a day."
That sentence sparked something in Lian’s mind, he was completely silent for a few seconds, then a very faint smile settled on his face.
"We’re not climbing down this tree."
The three Lacerians looked at him at the same time, and he continued quietly.
"This bird itself will take us down."
"...You mean to let it grab us with its claws again?" Ravian was stunned for a moment, but wasn’t that synonymous with suicide?

When the chicks are still inside the eggs, they travel between their hunting territory and the nest several times a day."
That sentence sparked something in Lian’s mind, he was completely silent for a few seconds, then a very faint smile settled on his face.
"We’re not climbing down this tree."
The three Lacerians looked at him at the same time, and he continued quietly.
"This bird itself will take us down."
"...You mean to let it grab us with its claws again?" Ravian was stunned for a moment, but wasn’t that synonymous with suicide?

chapters.title: Chapter 192: The Crazy Plan II
paragraphs: He doubted the monster would be kind enough to be willing to help them.
"No." Lian pointed to the back of the bird’s neck and the base of its massive wings.
"We stick to there." Then very quietly, he explained the plan step by step.
Sera would make strong harnesses and ropes with Thread Sap.
Nemi would use Quiet Pulse to minimize the sound of their movement when approaching.
Ravian would move on the bird’s feathers with Root Grip and secure the main rope among the thick feathers behind the neck.
Then, Lian would attach everyone to the bird’s body one by one, and he himself would hide near the neck with Abyss Veil.
When the bird left the nest, they would fly with it, and when the height was right, they would cut the ropes and jump onto the lower branches.
"Why behind the neck?" Ravian thought for a few moments.
Lian answered without pausing.
"It can’t see that part with its beak." Then he continued.
"The wind current there is much less than at the tips of the wings. The feathers are thicker, easier to grip, and because it’s close to the center of the body, the flight movements are less."
The three nodded in confirmation, the plan was dangerous, but for the first time, it also seemed logical.
But one very big problem still remained.
"What if it notices us in the middle of the flight?" Ravian asked after a few moments of silence, he doubted they could hide from this monster by any method.
"Then we die." Lian answered with his usual calmness.
No one said anything, and after a few seconds, he continued.
"But if we stay here, we also die. The difference is that this plan... at least gives us a real chance." His gaze fixed on the Giant Sky Bird.
"But we have to make sure it doesn’t have the chance to pay attention to us at all."
The three looked at him in surprise, and Lian said quietly.
"When it wakes up, it has to be so shocked, worried, and in a hurry that the existence of four small creatures doesn’t matter to it."
"...What do you mean?" Sera’s eyes slowly widened, a bad feeling came over all three, as if this Otherworldly was about to do something insane.
Lian fixed his gaze on the massive eggs.
"If one of the eggs falls from the edge of the nest... or even a few of them..."
Nemi held her breath in terror.
"No mother will first look for four tiny creatures, the first thing she’ll do is save her chicks.
"You mean... we throw the eggs down ourselves?" Sera said quietly.
"Correct." Lian did not take his gaze off the eggs.
"When they fall, all its attention will be focused on them. We’ll already be hidden behind its body from before."
"This way it might really not notice us..." Ravian said slowly, and from his view, the plan seemed more possible.
"No, even if it does notice, it won’t have time to care about us." Lian smiled.
Sera immediately started collecting plant fibers, sticky moss, dry strands from the nest, and a small amount of the bird’s saliva.
Thread Sap skill was activated one after another, the plant strands turned into strong ropes.
She made a harness for each person that would be tied around the chest, waist, and thighs so that the flight pressure wouldn’t be concentrated on one point.
Lian also brought out the bones he had collected and carefully made a few small hooks, Ravian sharpened them on the branch.
Everything was slowly being prepared, and right at that same moment, the Giant Sky Bird moved.
All four froze, but the bird did not wake up.
It only opened one of its massive wings and laid it over the cracked eggs.
Now the entire path to the back of its neck was hidden under that same wing, at the same time, the scratching sound from inside the egg also became louder.
Lian looked at the path for a few seconds, if he waited... the chick might hatch before the mother woke up.
If he moved... he would have to pass under the wing of a creature whose every jump was tens of times his size.
"We’re not waiting." He made his decision very quickly, the three looked at him.
"We’ll pass under its wing."
No one objected, everyone knew there was no more time for hesitation.
Lian tied the made harness around his body and then turned to the three.
"From this moment on... no one moves without my order."
Nemi looked with fear at the darkness under the massive wing.
"You go first?" Ravian asked quietly.
Lian activated Abyss Veil, his body slowly disappearing among the nest’s shadows, and only his voice remained.
"I’ll clear the path."
He gave one last look at Ravian, Sera, and Nemi. They were amazed and shocked to see how he disappeared as if he didn’t exist at all.
But along with that, there was also awe. If their tribe had such a skill, they could easily become the strongest tribe among all the forest tribes.
And this made them even more curious about the Otherworldly ones. They not only had different faces and shapes compared to them, but they also had such amazing skills.
Did all of them have such skills? Or was it only for this stranger who had saved them?
"If we had that skill, hunting would no longer be so dangerous." Sera sighed.
Then, without saying even a single word, he stepped into the darkness under the Giant Sky Bird’s wing.
At that same moment, the world changed. If the nest was a world of gray light and wind, under the bird’s wing was like entering a living, breathing cave.
The black feathers, like massive pillars of steel, surrounded him.
Each one of them was taller than a human’s stature, and so thick that if someone looked from a distance, they would imagine they were walking among dark forest trunks.
The air here was warmer, not the warmth of the sun, but the warmth of a creature whose every breath could move hundreds of humans.
The smell of fresh blood, wet feathers, half-digested meat, and dense mana filled the space under the wing; a heavy smell that made breathing difficult.
Lian took a step quietly.
Every time the Giant Sky Bird breathed, its massive skin expanded, and thousands of feathers around him moved like a forest in the wind.
The monster’s heartbeat from that distance was like the beats of a war drum.
Boom...
Boom...
Boom...
Every beat slightly shook the nest’s floor, Lian did not even dare to change his breathing speed.
This was the first time he was experiencing such a path, and he truly never thought that moving under a bird’s wing would be such a terrifying experience.
A few meters ahead, suddenly the bird’s wing lowered slightly. Everything happened in a fraction of a second. The massive feathers came down on him from above.
His body was caught between the nest’s surface and the unbelievable weight of the wing. The air in his lungs was forced out, his shoulder bones groaned.
Lian clenched his teeth. Was he going to be crushed under these damn wings?

chapters.title: Chapter 193: The Plan in Action I
paragraphs: The smallest struggle would have woken the bird. He had only one choice.
He moved his body millimeter by millimeter, each movement so slow that even he himself did not notice it.
Five seconds...
Ten seconds...
Twenty seconds...
Finally, his right shoulder came out from under the pressure, then his left arm, then his torso, and finally, his legs were also freed from under the wing.
Cold sweat covered his entire body, but he was still alive. Unfortunately, Abyss Veil only hides his presence and does not completely turn his physical body into a spiritual one.
He could still make contact with objects in his current state, and if not, if he completely merged with the shadows, it would have been much better.
Without even stopping for a moment, he moved again among the feathers.
A few minutes later, Lian passed through the last row of massive feathers.
In front of him was the back of the Giant Sky Bird’s neck, and it was only there that he truly understood the real dimensions of this monster.
Each feather on its neck was taller than a human’s stature, the distance between two feathers looked like a dark valley.
Beneath them, the bird’s black, scale-like skin could be seen; skin through which mana veins flowed like faint rivers.
The mana pressure of the monster’s body, even in sleep, weighed on Lian’s shoulders like a massive weight.
He calmly took out one of the bone hooks, carefully inserted it among several thick feathers, then passed the rope through its ring.
Just as he was about to tighten the knot, one of the neck feathers suddenly trembled.
Lian froze.
The bird... had felt an itch.
The Giant Sky Bird’s massive head moved slightly, a few seconds later, its giant beak rose from beside its neck.
Its shadow covered the entire space around Lian, he immediately threw himself into the gap between the feathers.
The black beak was only a few meters away from him, the sound of it hitting the bird’s skin was like a massive hammer striking.
Tap...
Tap...
Tap...
Every time the beak scratched the skin, hundreds of feathers around Lian shook violently.

His body was lifted off the ground several times, his fingers clung tightly to the roots of the feathers, if the beak had gone just a little deeper between the feathers... his body would have been crushed between that beak and the monster’s skin.
A few seconds later... the bird stopped scratching its neck and lowered its head again.
Lian waited a few more moments, and when he was sure the monster had calmed down again, he quietly let out his breath.
He tightened the main rope, then gently pulled it only once.
The signal.
The path was safe.
A few minutes later, Ravian was the first to enter the darkness under the wing, Root Grip was active on his hands, feet, and tail.
He moved among the feathers like a massive lizard, and whenever he felt the path was slippery, he stuck himself firmly to the surface.
After him came Sera, carefully carrying the ropes and harnesses.
The last one was Nemi, Quiet Pulse had spread around her body, the sound of all three people’s footsteps was largely faded in the surrounding space.
But the range of this skill was very limited, so they had to move almost stuck together.
Everything was going well... until suddenly...
Crack...
Nemi’s foot stepped on a piece of dry bone, the bone broke, and its sound, although weak, did not completely fade away.
Everyone froze at that same moment, and an ominous feeling of terror overwhelmed their entire being, they felt a bone-chilling cold run down their spines.
One of the Giant Sky Bird’s golden eyes slowly opened, Nemi froze right there among the feathers.
’Damn, damn, damn, damn.’ Her body was trembling with fear, so much so that she even lost the ability to breathe properly.
The bird raised its head slightly and sniffed the surrounding air. Lian could only watch from behind the neck, there was nothing he could do.
If he moved now, he himself would be the first to be killed.
Sera quietly took Nemi’s hand, she didn’t even dare to pull her.
A few seconds... which felt like hours for all four, finally... the bird lowered its head again.
The smell of its own saliva had completely covered their body odor, the disgusting idea that Lian had accepted had now saved their lives.
Everyone gathered behind the neck, Sera attached the harnesses to the main rope one by one.
Each person was placed between two rows of thick feathers, Lian specified everyone’s position.
Ravian at the front, near the head.
Sera in the center.
Nemi between them.
And himself at the back, but one problem still remained. If the bird dived during flight, all the pressure would be concentrated on one hook.
Everything might come loose. Lian took the second hook and placed it on the thick skin beneath the feathers.
"If it feels pain... it will wake up at that very moment." Ravian said quietly and cautiously.
If this comes loose, we all fall. We have to take the risk." His gaze fixed on the hook.
Nemi activated Quiet Pulse again, Lian held his breath and pushed the hook into the thick part of the skin with the calmest movement possible.
The Giant Sky Bird’s body suddenly tensed.
The four froze, the bird did not move for a few seconds, and then calmed down again.
The hook... stayed in place.
The next step... the egg.
They went for the healthiest egg. Contrary to Lian’s expectations, even four people could barely move it.
Its weight was unbelievable. They wrapped Thread Sap around the egg, the rope was stretched to the edge of the nest, the goal was not for the egg to fall at that moment.
It only had to reach the edge, the rope would do the rest. All four pushed with all their strength.
The egg moved forward a few meters, then... it got fucking stuck!
Ravian clenched his teeth, activated Root Grip, and applied more pressure.
Crack...
Suddenly, the branch beneath the egg broke, and everything went out of control!
"Damn it, stop it or we’re screwed!" The egg rolled toward the edge of the nest at high speed, Sera tried to hold the rope.
The rope was pulled violently through her palm, the skin of her hand split, blood dripped onto the Thread Sap fibers.
"Damn it, why is everything going like this?" Lian cursed and without thinking threw himself on the ground.
Both his hands grabbed the rope, the impact of the egg’s weight dragged him several meters on the branch’s surface.
His nails left marks on the wood, only a few meters away from falling.
Ravian immediately grabbed Lian’s ankle, Root Grip activated, and his tail also wrapped around the root of one of the feathers.
Sera threw the rope around a thick branch, and finally... the egg stopped right at the edge of the nest.
Half of it was hanging out, but... the sound of breaking was enough.
The Giant Sky Bird’s breathing suddenly stopped, the entire nest fell into silence.
Then one of the monster’s golden eyes opened

chapters.title: Chapter 194: The Plan in Action II
paragraphs: The massive eye slowly moved across the nest.
The bird’s head slowly rose, the three Lacerians were hidden behind its neck, but Lian was still standing beside the rope, near the edge of the nest.
Abyss Veil was hiding his presence, but not enough to be completely invisible to such a creature.
The golden eye passed over the nest, over the prey, over the healthy eggs, and finally...
Over the egg that was half out of the nest, the Giant Sky Bird’s body suddenly tensed, all its feathers stood on end, and its golden pupil narrowed.
Then... it screamed.
A sound so horrifying that the entire nest shook, blood flowed from the ears of Nemi, Ravian, and Sera.
The surrounding clouds became turbulent, but the bird had not yet flown, and all its attention... was on the egg.
It moved its beak toward it, Lian understood at that moment, if it saved the egg... everything would be over.
He pulled out his knife, without a moment’s hesitation... he cut the rope.
The egg remained on the edge for a moment, and then... it fell.
"Wooooooommmm" The Giant Sky Bird’s second scream... was even more terrifying than the first.
The monster, without thinking, opened its wings, the resulting wind like an explosion swept through the entire nest, Lian was lifted off the ground and his body was thrown outward.
The harness rope suddenly pulled and for a moment half of his body was hanging outside the nest.
Below him... only clouds, and then the bird leaped from the nest, the rope violently slammed him against the monster’s back, and all the air in his lungs was forced out.
Now... all four were attached to the Giant Sky Bird’s body, and the monster, with insane speed... was diving after the falling egg.
It folded its wings and dove almost vertically.
The wind hit their faces like thousands of blades, breathing had become impossible, the ropes were digging into their flesh.
The massive feathers around them were dancing like whips in the air, and the sound of the wind... had swallowed the entire world.
Nemi had opened her mouth, but she couldn’t even scream.
Ravian was clinging to the feathers with all his might, his hands were bruised from the pressure of Root Grip.
"...The rope!" Sera suddenly said in terror.
One of the harness strands was tearing. Lian tried to move toward it, but the dive’s pressure wouldn’t allow him to move even a few centimeters.
A moment later... they all entered the clouds. The world turned white, cold... moisture, thick fog, nothing could be seen.
Only the sound of unknown creatures’ wings could be heard from around, fleeing in terror from the Giant Sky Bird’s path.
And then... Lian saw it. Something that made all the hair on his body stand on end, and his being trembled so much that his cells and instincts didn’t even dare to give him a warning...
"My god... is it itself?"
A shadow, much larger than the Giant Sky Bird, only for a moment, in the heart of the fog, a massive eye... slowly opened.
It wasn’t looking at them, but at the Giant Sky Bird. That was it, and nothing else happened.
But the Giant Sky Bird suddenly changed its course, as if it understood that the direction it was heading was forbidden.
Its body twisted violently in the air, Sera’s rope was stretched with a dry sound, and the strands were breaking one by one.
It was unclear how much longer it could hold...
The clouds parted, hundreds of meters below, the egg was still falling.
The Giant Sky Bird increased its speed, the next moment it opened its wings with all its power.
The deceleration impact was like hitting a wall, all four bodies were thrown forward.
"No, help! Help me! I don’t want to die! Sob sob" One of the hooks came loose, and Nemi let out a short scream, her body separated from its place.
Now only a thin strand was holding her, below her body... endless space.
If she fell, it would only be death.
Sera reached out her hand, but the distance was too great, she couldn’t help her sister.
"Hold on tight! Please, hold on tight!"
"I can’t... it’s hard! All my body hurts! My flesh is going to tear... noooooo!" Suddenly her fingers began to open one by one.
Not much time remained before she fell.
"Noooo, Nemi!" Ravian shouted in horror upon seeing his sister’s situation.
Lian without thinking freed his own rope and crawled among the feathers with one hand, and at the very last moment...
He grabbed Nemi’s wrist. The thin strand was almost torn, and at the same time... the Giant Sky Bird opened both its claws.
And caught the egg just before it hit the lower branches.
But... at that same moment... it felt something... a weight... a movement... that shouldn’t be on its back.
Its massive head slowly turned, one golden eye... only a few meters away from Lian.
Lian was clinging to the bird’s feathers with one hand, and with the other... he was holding Nemi.
The rope was slowly tearing under their weight, the golden eye... remained fixed on him.
For a moment... time stopped, and then the vertical pupil slowly narrowed... The Giant Sky Bird had realized something was on its body!
At that same moment, it folded one of its wings and spun its entire massive body in the air.
"Everyone... hold on tight!" Lian only had time to shout.
And the world... turned upside down.

Lian only had time to sink his fingers with all his strength into the thick feathers of the Giant Sky Bird. His instincts were warning him strongly that if he didn’t hold on tight, he would definitely die!
The monster had caught its egg and had noticed them, and now they had entered the most difficult part of their plan. From here on, they just had to hold on tight, or they might get killed!
The next moment, the sky and the forest swapped places, and the bird’s massive body rolled in the air.
Once...
Twice...
Three times...
The wind hit Lian’s face with such intensity that it felt like his skin would be ripped off his bones.
Even with his current level and stats, the speed of this bird was so terrifyingly high that it could put him in such a situation.
This showed that a Fallen level 50 was in a completely different league in terms of power, a league he was still far from...
All the ropes were stretched tight.
The black feathers around him, like massive walls, were rushing at him from new directions every moment.
With one hand, he was still holding Nemi’s wrist, and with the other hand, his fingers were buried deep into the feathers up to the last knuckle.
If even one of those two hands let go... everything would be over.
A few meters ahead, Ravian was almost locked onto the bird’s body, a faint green light was flowing on his hands, feet, and tail.
Root Grip was active at its maximum capacity.
But the skin on his palms had cracked, and blood was seeping from between his fingers, and his legs were trembling from the pressure.
A little further back, Sera was holding on with one hand and trying to tie the torn strand of Nemi’s harness back to the main rope with the other.
But every time the bird rolled, the rope would escape from her fingers again.
"Just... a few more seconds..." Her voice was lost in the roar of the wind

The bird’s head slowly rose, the three Lacerians were hidden behind its neck, but Lian was still standing beside the rope, near the edge of the nest.
Abyss Veil was hiding his presence, but not enough to be completely invisible to such a creature.

Over the egg that was half out of the nest, the Giant Sky Bird’s body suddenly tensed, all its feathers stood on end, and its golden pupil narrowed.
Then... it screamed.
A sound so horrifying that the entire nest shook, blood flowed from the ears of Nemi, Ravian, and Sera.

The harness rope suddenly pulled and for a moment half of his body was hanging outside the nest.

The world turned white, cold... moisture, thick fog, nothing could be seen.

Something that made all the hair on his body stand on end, and his being trembled so much that his cells and instincts didn’t even dare to give him a warning...

chapters.title: Chapter 195: The Plan in Action III
paragraphs: Suddenly... the massive egg that the Giant Sky Bird was holding between its claws slipped slightly.
The sound of the shell scraping against the giant claws was heard even through the howling wind.
The bird immediately stopped rolling, its entire body suddenly became still, and then it wrapped both claws more desperately around the egg.
Its massive head lowered, and all its attention... all its instincts... its entire being... was focused on that same egg.
"The egg... is still more important to it than us." Lian narrowed his pupils.
And this was a single glimmer of hope! If the monster was still forced to focus on the egg and forget about taking revenge on them, he felt... maybe... maybe they really would survive.
But time was very short. The bird had already finished that insane dive.
Now it was flying only a few hundred meters above the massive branches of the Forest of Giants.
Branches that even from this distance looked thicker than the federation’s defensive towers. If it climbed again... no hope would remain.
Lian looked down. His mind was working quickly. The ground was still far away, too far.
Jumping directly... was certain death. But... his eyes suddenly caught something.
A few hundred meters below... a massive mass of emerald moss was spread across a network of exposed roots.
Leaves as wide as building roofs were piled on top of each other, mushrooms as tall as small houses were sticking out of the soil.
And a little further away, a fallen branch stretched like a massive bridge between two parts of the forest.
Moss... was the best choice, if they were lucky.
"When we reach that branch..." His voice this time cut through the wind with all his power.
"We cut the ropes!"
"No! If we all jump at the same time, we might fall on top of each other!" Sera immediately raised her head.
Lian made the decision right then.
"Ravian first, you land on the trunk with Root Grip."
Then his gaze fell on Sera.
"Then you and Nemi, and I jump last."
No one objected, everyone knew there was no time to argue. This was their only chance to survive, if they lost it too, their death was certain!
At that same moment...
The Giant Sky Bird turned its head back again, its massive golden eye fixed on them.
Lian’s heart stopped for a moment, but right at that time...
Crack... the sound of the egg cracking again was heard, a new crack appeared on the shell, and the bird’s entire body tensed.
Its gaze was immediately lifted from the four small creatures on its back.
Its head went down in panic, its beak gently touched the egg’s shell.
The mother... no longer cared about them. Not because she had forgotten them, but because now, in its instinctive mind, nothing was more important than returning the egg safely to the nest.
Its chick was being born and it had to return it to a safe place as soon as possible!
Lian did not smile, he felt their plan had worked.
The bird opened its wings, another gust of wind, and this time it began to climb.
"Right now!"
Ravian was the first, with a quick movement, he cut his rope, and his body immediately separated from the bird’s back.
He fell for a few meters, then both hands, feet, and tail shone with green light.
Root Grip.
His body hit the massive trunk of one of the trees with great force, the sound of bone and skin hitting the trunk was heard even from this distance.
His shoulder was bleeding from the impact.
But... he did not fall, he was clinging to the trunk with all his being, and Lian breathed a sigh of relief.
"Next!"
Sera also jumped, and at the same time, after signaling to Nemi, Lian let go of her hand and released her, and both spun in the air.
The wind threw them a few meters away, then they landed on one of the massive leaves, the leaf bent under their weight close to the ground.
A moment later, like a giant spring, it threw them back into the air, and both fell into the thick mass of moss and disappeared.
Now... only Lian remained. He placed his hand on the harness around his waist.
He pulled, it didn’t budge.
The hook... was stuck!
The bird was climbing higher every moment.
In a few more seconds, everything would be lost. Although no sign of fear or worry could be seen on his face this time either.
It was just a rope, maybe he couldn’t kill that bird, but he could still pull this rope, and that’s exactly what he did.
The rope suddenly came free, his body was thrown backward, and the wind took all control from him.
The first impact... a massive leaf. His body slid on its slippery surface and then fell off the leaf’s edge.
The second impact... the stem of one of the giant mushrooms. The mushroom bent like a massive spring and threw him back into the air.
The final impact... a mass of moss. As if the entire world turned green, and a heavy blow hit his back.
Then... darkness.
When he opened his eyes again, it took a few moments to realize he was still alive.
He took a deep breath, his entire body was in pain. It hadn’t been long since the last time he had experienced such adrenaline.
Maybe not even a week had passed since he had survived the siege of the base by two monster races and a level 35 Fallen that had come for him.
And again, he was caught in such a situation... his fate was too full of ups and downs.
He slowly emerged from the moss, the first thing he saw was the sky.
The Giant Sky Bird was now just a black dot in the mist, holding the egg firmly between its claws.
It didn’t look back even once, with each flap of its wings, it got further away, and finally... it disappeared into the clouds.
A few minutes later... all four were standing together again.
No one was speaking, not because of exhaustion, but because the surrounding scenery didn’t allow for words.
Lian slowly raised his head, finally seeing the Forest of Giants from the ground.
And he understood that all his previous assumptions had been wrong.
This was not a forest, this was another world. The tree roots had emerged from the soil like multi-story walls.
Some of them were so thick that even dozens of people holding hands couldn’t encircle them.
The moss had grown up to a human’s chest, dew drops on the leaves were each the size of a human head, and green mana light was shining inside them.
Fallen leaves, like the roofs of massive houses, lay on the ground.
The gap between two roots... looked like a deep valley to them.
From a distance, the sound of unknown creatures moving, like the trembling of the earth, could be heard.
Sunlight barely passed through the canopy, thin columns of light had split the foggy forest air.
Green particles of mana were floating calmly in the air, an insect passed by them, its body almost the size of an elephant.
A few moments later, the creature disappeared.
Lian calmly looked up, the tip of the tree was not visible at all and was lost in the mist.
Now he understood even more how small he was in front of this forest’s trees.
The branch they had landed on a few minutes ago now from below looked like a bridge stretched between two mountains.
A few minutes later, when they were sure the Giant Sky Bird would not return, the silence among them was broken.
Nemi quietly came toward Lian, she just looked at him for a few moments, and her eyes were still trembling from the shock.
Then suddenly she wrapped both her arms around Lian’s arm, her voice trembling.
"We... we’re really alive... thank you so much! Thank you, thank you so much! You saved us!"
Lian said nothing and just gave a very faint smile, and Sera stepped forward, quietly lowering her head.
"You pulled us out of that monster’s saliva once, and the second time you saved us from its nest." She lowered her head again.
"Our tribe will never forget this debt."
Ravian said nothing for a few moments, his pride wouldn’t allow him to show his feelings easily, but in the end, he took a deep breath.
"If it weren’t for you..." His gaze went to the sky.
"We would have been dead even before that egg hatched."
Lian quickly changed the subject, his gaze fixed on the forest.
"I hope you at least know which direction your tribe is."
A few seconds of silence followed, and then Ravian laughed, the first real laugh since Lian had met him.
"Don’t worry." He placed his hand on one of the massive roots.
"As long as I can see the rivers, the moss, and the direction of the root growth, I can find the path." Then he pointed to the east.
"The tribe is that way."
Lian gave a brief look at the path, an endless forest, full of mist, full of unknown sounds, and creatures whose very breathing shook the ground.
"Then let’s go." He said quietly.

chapters.title: Chapter 196: The Forest Of Giants
paragraphs: Four people were moving along a narrow gap between two giant roots.
From a distance, their path might have looked like only a small groove on the forest floor, but for them, the walls on both sides rose like multi-story cliffs.
Thick layers of moss had grown on the roots’ surfaces, and their hanging strands were stretched down to the ground.
Some of those strands were thicker than a human arm, and with every gust of wind, they moved in the air like green snakes.
Ravian was walking at the front.
Every few minutes, he would stop, place his palm on the soil or the root’s bark, and carefully look around.

Sometimes he would check the direction of the moss growth, sometimes he would measure the soil’s moisture between his fingers, and sometimes he would listen to the sound of water flowing somewhere far away, behind several natural walls.
Sera and Nemi were moving in the middle of the group.
Sera was still injured in her shoulder, but she didn’t let the pain slow her down.
Nemi also looked at the hidden sky behind the treetops every few steps, as if she still expected the Giant Sky Bird to come down from the mist and catch them in its claws again.
Lian was at the back of the group, not because he was weaker or slower, but because [Predator’s Instincts] had not been turned off since the moment they had entered this part of the forest.
The feeling of danger did not appear as a clear and direct warning.
It was more like a cold pressure at the back of his skull; a vague feeling that told him something in that green vastness was always watching.
Maybe a monster in the mist, maybe an insect on the tree trunk.
Or maybe a creature so large that they themselves had not yet realized which part of its body they were walking on.
Lian did not take his gaze off the back of his companions, but all his senses were focused on the surroundings.
He saw every small movement of the moss, heard every change in the sounds, and felt every faint tremor in the ground.
The Forest of Giants seemed endless from above, but from the ground, it was infinitely worse.
Here, there was no smooth and simple path.
Every mass of moss was like a dense thicket that had to be pushed aside with hands.
Its soft stems reached up to their chests or even shoulders, and the dew drops on their tips would burst like water bags when they touched their clothes.
Sometimes, just to cross over an exposed root, they had to climb for several minutes.
A root that from a distance seemed like nothing more than a bump on the ground, when they got close to it, turned into a ten-meter-high wall.
The hollows between the soil looked like valleys to them.
Once, Nemi placed her foot on a part of the ground that was hidden under a layer of rotten leaves.
The surface beneath her foot collapsed, and she fell up to her waist into a dark crack.
Ravian had to grab her with his tail and pull her out.
A few minutes later, a drop of water separated from one of the tall leaves, the falling drop was the size of a human head.
Upon hitting the ground, it burst like a barrel full of water, and a wave of mud and moss splashed over all four of them, and Nemi wiped the water from her face with annoyance.
"It was just one drop?" Ravian said without turning back.
"You were lucky. Some leaves collect water for several days."
Lian looked up, the leaves were so far away that they were lost in the green mist.
"And if one of them falls down?" He could swear that this was one of, if not the worst, environment he had ever seen in his life.
Everything in this hell was larger than them, and if they weren’t careful, they would get crushed.
"Then it’s better not to be under it." Ravian was silent for a moment.
Before Nemi could say anything, a loud sound was heard from a distance, as if a mountain had broken, a few seconds later, the ground beneath their feet trembled.
Sera quickly placed her hand on the root wall.
"What was that?
"Probably a fruit." Ravian listened to the sound.
"A fruit?" Lian looked at him in disbelief.
Another wave of tremor passed through the soil, this time a few rotten leaves fell from the root’s surface.
Ravian shrugged.
"Some of them are larger than the tribe’s houses."
At that same moment, a shadow passed over their heads, Lian immediately looked up.
A flying insect, with a slender body and several-meter-long wings, passed through the columns of light.
The sound of its wings was like a massive piece of fabric tearing in a storm.
The creature didn’t even look down, it disappeared into the mist in the blink of an eye, they were used to these scenes.
The four continued on their path.
With every step they took, it became clearer that this forest was not made for creatures of their size.
Here, they were neither hunters nor even prey, only small particles that could disappear into the cracks of a tree’s bark.
Almost like parasites and very tiny worms.
About an hour later, Predator’s Instincts suddenly intensified.
Lian stopped in his tracks, raised his hand, and the other three immediately stopped.
"What is it?" Ravian turned back.
Lian didn’t answer, he lowered his head slightly and placed his foot more firmly on the soil.
A tremor.
At first it was very faint, then it came a second time, heavier.
Then a third strike, this time the soft soil beneath their feet moved, the sound of footsteps was heard from somewhere behind the root wall.
Each step was slow, but the weight of what was approaching forced the entire ground to respond.
"Something big is coming." Lian said quietly.
Ravian listened for only a moment, and the color of his face changed.
"Inside the crack." He pointed to a narrow space between two roots.
The four quickly placed themselves inside it.
The crack was like a natural corridor for them, but its entrance was hidden behind moss and hanging strands.
Ravian placed his finger in front of his lips, and the sound of footsteps grew closer.
The ground trembled every time, particles of soil fell from the crack’s ceiling onto their heads.
Then a massive shadow passed in front of the entrance, at first only one foot was seen.
A thick foot, covered with gray skin and layers of moss, its width was more than the bodies of several humans.
The claws sank deep into the soil with every step, and when lifted, they brought up masses of mud and roots.
Lian moved forward a little and looked outside through the moss, a massive creature was passing in front of them.
Its body was like a combination of a turtle, a deer, and a buffalo.
Its four thick legs carried its twelve-meter-long body, and a heavy neck had come out from under a layer of armor-like skin.
Two wide and curved horns had grown on both sides of its head, but the strangest part was its back.
The back of that creature looked more like a piece of the forest than the body of a monster, a thick layer of soil had gathered on its shell.
Moss had covered its surface, small mushrooms had grown out of the cracks.
A few bushes had grown on its sides, and even young saplings were placed on its back.
Insects were moving among those plants.
A few small birds were sitting on one of its horns and cleaning their feathers without worry.
The identification panel appeared before Lian’s eyes.
[Mossback Grazer]
[Rank: Normal]
[Level: 22]
Lian stared at the number for a moment.
Level 22.
Such a creature on Earth could single-handedly bring down the walls of a small city.
But here, it was only a calm herbivore that was busy digging a layer of fungus off a massive tree trunk.
"Don’t stare at it too much. This one is calm." Ravian whispered under his breath.
The creature lowered its head and scraped a mass of moss with its wide jaw.
"Just don’t get in front of its foot." As if to prove his point, the Mossback Grazer lifted its foot.
The shadow of its sole fell on the crack, for a moment, all the light disappeared.
Then the creature’s massive foot landed on the ground only a few meters away.
The impact was like an explosion, soil and moss were lifted from the ground, and a wave of mud rushed into the crack.
Nemi covered her face with her hand, Sera clung to the wall, and even Ravian was forced to take a step back.
The Mossback Grazer continued moving without the slightest reaction, it didn’t turn its head, didn’t smell them, and didn’t even notice that a few living creatures were hiding right next to its foot.
A few seconds later, its heavy tail passed in front of the crack and scraped a mass of moss from the wall.
Then its steps became distant, the ground still trembled for a while after it left.
Nemi slowly came out of the crack and looked at the creature’s massive footprint.
A deep pit remained in the ground; large enough for the entire group to stand inside.
Lian came out of the shelter, his gaze fixed on the creature’s path as it moved away.
He could kill it, Level 22 was not considered a real threat to him.
If he attacked the leg joints, he could limit its movement.
Then with Glacial Reaper Claw, he could enter through the soft part under its neck.
Maybe it would take a few more hits than the smaller monsters, but the result would not be different.
However, his hand didn’t even go near his weapon.
Killing that creature had no meaning, its body was so large that its blood would fill the area.
Its smell could attract predators against whom Level 22 was nothing more than food.
Power did not only mean the ability to kill, sometimes real power was understanding what was not worth killing.
Ravian looked at him, probably reading the same thought from his silence.
"It’s good that you didn’t attack it, it would have been very dangerous and crazy."
"What made you think I wanted to?" Lian took his gaze off the footprint.
"Even though we are not the biggest hunters in this forest, my tribe is still a hunting tribe, I could see that you were looking at it like prey." Ravian gave a faint smile.
Of course, he didn’t think Lian had the ability to kill that monster, how could creatures as small as them kill those giants?
He just thought that Lian’s species probably had some kind of combat instinct that was activating.
"Show the way." Lian nodded but didn’t continue the topic.

sentences.text: Four people were moving along a narrow gap between two giant roots.
From a distance, their path might have looked like only a small groove on the forest floor, but for them, the walls on both sides rose like multi-story cliffs.
Thick layers of moss had grown on the roots’ surfaces, and their hanging strands were stretched down to the ground.
Some of those strands were thicker than a human arm, and with every gust of wind, they moved in the air like green snakes.
Ravian was walking at the front.
Every few minutes, he would stop, place his palm on the soil or the root’s bark, and carefully look around.

Sometimes he would check the direction of the moss growth, sometimes he would measure the soil’s moisture between his fingers, and sometimes he would listen to the sound of water flowing somewhere far away, behind several natural walls.
Sera and Nemi were moving in the middle of the group.
Sera was still injured in her shoulder, but she didn’t let the pain slow her down.
Nemi also looked at the hidden sky behind the treetops every few steps, as if she still expected the Giant Sky Bird to come down from the mist and catch them in its claws again.
Lian was at the back of the group, not because he was weaker or slower, but because [Predator’s Instincts] had not been turned off since the moment they had entered this part of the forest.
The feeling of danger did not appear as a clear and direct warning.
It was more like a cold pressure at the back of his skull; a vague feeling that told him something in that green vastness was always watching.
Maybe a monster in the mist, maybe an insect on the tree trunk.
Or maybe a creature so large that they themselves had not yet realized which part of its body they were walking on.
Lian did not take his gaze off the back of his companions, but all his senses were focused on the surroundings.
He saw every small movement of the moss, heard every change in the sounds, and felt every faint tremor in the ground.
The Forest of Giants seemed endless from above, but from the ground, it was infinitely worse.
Here, there was no smooth and simple path.
Every mass of moss was like a dense thicket that had to be pushed aside with hands.
Its soft stems reached up to their chests or even shoulders, and the dew drops on their tips would burst like water bags when they touched their clothes.
Sometimes, just to cross over an exposed root, they had to climb for several minutes.
A root that from a distance seemed like nothing more than a bump on the ground, when they got close to it, turned into a ten-meter-high wall.
The hollows between the soil looked like valleys to them.
Once, Nemi placed her foot on a part of the ground that was hidden under a layer of rotten leaves.
The surface beneath her foot collapsed, and she fell up to her waist into a dark crack.
Ravian had to grab her with his tail and pull her out.
A few minutes later, a drop of water separated from one of the tall leaves, the falling drop was the size of a human head.
Upon hitting the ground, it burst like a barrel full of water, and a wave of mud and moss splashed over all four of them, and Nemi wiped the water from her face with annoyance.
"It was just one drop?" Ravian said without turning back.
"You were lucky.
Some leaves collect water for several days."
Lian looked up, the leaves were so far away that they were lost in the green mist.
"And if one of them falls down?" He could swear that this was one of, if not the worst, environment he had ever seen in his life.
Everything in this hell was larger than them, and if they weren’t careful, they would get crushed.
"Then it’s better not to be under it." Ravian was silent for a moment.
Before Nemi could say anything, a loud sound was heard from a distance, as if a mountain had broken, a few seconds later, the ground beneath their feet trembled.
Sera quickly placed her hand on the root wall.
"What was that?
"Probably a fruit." Ravian listened to the sound.
"A fruit?" Lian looked at him in disbelief.
Another wave of tremor passed through the soil, this time a few rotten leaves fell from the root’s surface.
Ravian shrugged.
"Some of them are larger than the tribe’s houses."
At that same moment, a shadow passed over their heads, Lian immediately looked up.
A flying insect, with a slender body and several-meter-long wings, passed through the columns of light.
The sound of its wings was like a massive piece of fabric tearing in a storm.
The creature didn’t even look down, it disappeared into the mist in the blink of an eye, they were used to these scenes.
The four continued on their path.
With every step they took, it became clearer that this forest was not made for creatures of their size.
Here, they were neither hunters nor even prey, only small particles that could disappear into the cracks of a tree’s bark.
Almost like parasites and very tiny worms.

Lian stopped in his tracks, raised his hand, and the other three immediately stopped.
"What is it?" Ravian turned back.
Lian didn’t answer, he lowered his head slightly and placed his foot more firmly on the soil.
A tremor.

chapters.title: Chapter 197: Just Stay Back
paragraphs: The faint light that was coming down through the treetops was slowly changing.
The thin golden columns were replaced by a colder and greener light.
Ravian had reduced their speed.
They were now passing through an area full of red moss and plants with wide leaves.
A sweet and heavy smell was in the air, which became thicker the further they went.
Lian felt several times that something was following them from a distance.
But every time he turned back, he only saw the moss moving.
Predator’s Instincts was still warning.
Not from one direction, but from several directions, and this difference was important.
A predator usually approaches from a specific point.
But this feeling... was like an invisible circle closing around them.
Lian walked slower and checked the sounds around him.
During this time, he had realized that his intuition was very reliable, and now he also knew that something was about to happen.
The buzzing of the insects, which had been heard throughout the forest until a few moments ago, had decreased.
One by one.
Until almost no sound remained.
"Why did everything go quiet?" Nemi also noticed the silence.
Ravian also stopped, his hand went toward the spear he had made from wood he had found on the ground.
Lian looked to the right.
The wind was blowing from the left, but the moss on the right was moving against the wind.
Not with a natural order, but something was passing through them.
"We are not alone." he said quietly.
Sera immediately pulled out the knife Lian had given her, and Ravian also took the spear from his back and held it in front of his body.
They could also feel that danger was approaching.
The moss moved in several places, then the sound of something hard scraping on the ground was heard.
Tick.
Tick.
Tick.
Two long antennae came out of the moss, then the creature’s head appeared.
It had a red and black shell that shone like dark metal under the forest’s weak light.
Two curved jaws on both sides of its head were opening and closing, and each time they hit each other, they made a sound like iron scissors.
Its body was almost the size of a large elephant, maybe even a little larger, and six thin but powerful legs were holding it on the ground.
At the end of its abdomen, a long red stinger, like a spear’s needle, had come out.
The panel appeared before Lian’s eyes.
[Crimson Needle Worker]
[ Rank: Normal ]
[Level: 18]
Before anyone could react, the moss on both sides of the path moved aside.
A second one came out.
A third.
Then a fourth.
A few seconds later, more than ten giant ants had appeared around them.
Some were smaller and thinner, but a few among them had bodies the size of tigers and their front shells were thicker.
[Crimson Needle Soldier]
[ Rank : Normal ]
[Level: 22]
[Crimson Needle Soldier]
[ Rank : Normal ]
[Level: 24]
Lian, without moving, counted their numbers.
Seventeen.
Maybe two or three more were still hidden among the moss.
"We have to run!" Ravian slowly stepped back, a hidden fear was clear in his tone.
These are not monsters they can handle!
"How dangerous are they?" Lian asked without taking his eyes off the ants.
"Not each one individually."
"But Crimson Needle Ants never move too far from the colony." Ravian clenched his jaw.
One of the Workers raised its head and its antennae trembled in the air, then it turned directly toward Sera’s wounded shoulder.
"They are following the smell of blood." Sera said quietly upon realizing it.
A few ants appeared from behind, the rear path was blocked, and Nemi raised her short spear, which she had also made from wood, but her hands were trembling slightly.
"There are too many of them. We have to fight together." Sera stood next to Lian.
"We can’t win! We have to try to break the encirclement and run!" Ravian said with seriousness and a sense of urgency.
He didn’t want to die by these ants now that they had managed to escape from that giant bird!
"It’s not necessary." Lian stepped forward, the sound of the ants’ jaws became louder.
Sera looked at him.
"You just stay back."
"This—" Ravian frowned.
"If one of them gets past me, then you intervene." Lian said with a quiet but so firm tone that it made all of them fall silent.
There was something in his tone that made Ravian not continue.
Lian looked at the enemies again.
Level 17.
Level 19.
Level 21.
Level 24.
None of the numbers he saw were even close to the danger limit.
The dark space of the forest floor was not suitable for normal eyes.
But [Night Eyes] was activated.
The colors of the world changed, the shadows became clearer, and the small movement of the antennae, the contraction of the joints, and the trembling of the ants’ legs became clear to him.
Predator’s Instincts also did the rest.
Danger from behind, slightly high, to the right, and Lian, without turning around, moved his head a few centimeters to the side.
Two metal jaws passed right by his ear.
The Crimson Needle Soldier had jumped out from behind the moss.
The creature hadn’t even had time to close its jaws again when Lian raised his hand.
Cold and dark mana gathered around his fingers, the moisture in the air froze in an instant, and an elongated claw of dark ice formed on his hand.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
The surrounding temperature suddenly dropped, a thin layer of ice settled on the moss.
The level 22 ant tried to pull its head back, but it was too late.
Lian moved his hand only once, and the ice claw passed through the connection point between the head and the chest.
The monster’s hard shell was split open.
The sound of armor cracking echoed with a muffled noise in the forest, the ant’s head did not separate from the body.
But the cut was so deep that it had almost severed its entire neck.
Dark blood was about to gush from the wound, but before even a single drop reached the ground, the edges of the wound froze.
The corpse fell a few steps ahead.
The three Lacerians remained motionless, the whole event had taken less than a second.
One of the Soldiers had been killed, without a scream and without a fight, without even being able to land a second strike.
"How is this possible?" Sera whispered in disbelief, and her siblings’ reaction was not much different.
The other ants paused for a moment, their antennae turned toward the corpse with quick movements.
Then they all moved at the same time, six creatures charged from three directions, and the veins on Lian’s neck and arms darkened for a moment.
Blood flowed through his body with more pressure, the muscles in his legs contracted.
The world slowed down for him.
Not literally in the sense of the word, but his body’s speed increased so much that the movements around him seemed heavy and predictable.
For Ravian and the others, Lian suddenly vanished from his spot.
A Worker turned its head toward him, it hadn’t even completed half of its movement when Lian landed on its back.
He brought down his ice claw, the connection point between the head and body was split open.
The ant collapsed.
Lian jumped to the left before the corpse hit the ground.
The second ant had opened its jaws, he struck the inner part of the jaw with his knee.
The creature’s head was deflected, and then the Glacial Reaper Claw went straight into one of its eyes.
The ice spread from inside its head, the movement of its legs stopped at that very moment.
The third ant raised its abdomen, the red stinger shot out from the end of its body.
Lian saw it, he could dodge, but he didn’t.
The tip of the stinger hit his shoulder with all its force.
The sound of the impact was like a steel nail hitting a rock, a small spark jumped from the contact point, and the skin on Lian’s shoulder became transparent and dark for a moment.
[Diamond Skin]
The stinger could not even scratch the surface of his skin.
The ant remained motionless for a moment, as if even the monster was shocked.
As if they had doubted whether they were prey or predators.
Lian turned his head toward it.
The creature might not be able to feel fear, but its antennae suddenly moved with agitation.
He wrapped his hand around the end part of its abdomen, planted his feet firmly on the ground.
Then he lifted the entire several-hundred-kilogram body of the ant off the ground.
Ravian was watching in disbelief.
The muscles of Lian’s arm and shoulder contracted under his clothes, he swung the ant’s body in the air and violently slammed it into one of its kind.
The sound of shells breaking echoed in the space, both creatures fell to the ground.
One of them was still moving.
Lian landed on its head and with one kick, crushed the front part of its shell.
The remaining ants did not attack directly this time.
Instead, they tightened the circle.
Six Workers and four Soldiers came out from the moss.
Their legs moved on the ground with strange order, their antennae went up and down at the same time.
They had seen the previous attacks, now they wanted to apply pressure from all sides.
Lian took a calm breath, the ice claw on his hand cracked.
But it was still not destroyed.
He looked around, the distance between the enemies, the slope of the ground, the thickness of the moss, and the positions of Ravian, Sera, and Nemi.
Everything came together in his mind in an instant.
Then he knelt down, placed his free palm on the ground.
Mana moved under his skin.
It went down from his shoulder, passed through his arm, gathered in his palm, and for a moment, the soil beneath his fingers sank.
[Cataclysm Pulse]
The explosion had no sound.
First, only a heavy impact came from within the ground, then a compressed wave spread in all directions.
The moss was uprooted, and the soil rose in a ring around Lian.
The shell on the underside of the ants’ abdomen, where their armor was thinner, cracked under the wave’s pressure.
A few Workers were thrown into the air, one of the Soldiers fell on its side and its legs kicked aimlessly in the air.
The encirclement formation was broken in an instant, and Lian jumped out from the dust of the soil.
The first ant was still trying to turn around when Glacial Reaper Claw passed under its jaw.
The second one lost its balance with a direct hit to the front leg joint.
Lian stepped on its shell, climbed up, and sank the claw into the back of its head.
The third one prepared its stinger.
Lian grabbed it, pulled the creature’s body toward himself, and crushed its forehead with a knee strike.
The fourth and fifth attacked at the same time.
Lian spun between them, one’s jaw passed by his side, his claw passed through the other’s chest.
Then with a short kick, he threw the first ant into a small crack between two roots.
The sound of its body hitting the rock was heard, it did not move anymore.
The battle had turned into a slaughter, not one of those fights where the result was uncertain.
A one-sided massacre of giant monsters.
And Ravian, Sera, and Nemi were watching in shock, and were slowly becoming sure that Lian might be more powerful than all the hunters of their tribe.
What kind of monster were they bringing to their tribe?
